EPC-022.whatItIs: The 4.0.0 release plan addresses issues filed by this repository and by adopters. The original 2026-10-12 scope covered 26 issues against CodeFlow 3.0.0 and 3.1.0. The combined scope covers `codeflow ci` verdicts that depend on how a range is spelled, planning and exemption pull requests that cannot be classified, guards that miss commands, writers and history reads that can be redirected in a local clone, CodeFlow's own pushes using a personal credential, managed CI steps an adopter must edit by hand, a landing mode, tests that touch an enclosing repository, and one post-release evaluation. This epic fixes or settles each of them for the 4.0.0 release, which the operator renumbered from 3.2.0 on 2026-10-28 (Version relabel amendment below).
EPC-022.serves: It serves every adopter and contributor who runs `codeflow ci`, the hooks, the guards and the managed CI.
EPC-022.doneMeans: each task below has landed on `integration/EPC-022-the-3-2-0-milestone-fixes` with its cross-lineage review, the integrated body passes the full gate and the journey below on the installed candidate, and its pull request to `main` is ready for a human merge.

EPC-024.title: quality defaults, local scan parity and seat capacity
EPC-024.deliverable: after this merges, an adopting project gets strict, define-once and lean-repository checks by default with every relaxation recorded and reported, runs the managed scans locally with the hosted verdict, and keeps its seats running by their remaining capacity.
EPC-024.whatItIs: Five feature requests from adopters in October 2026 ask CodeFlow to change its defaults rather than fix a defect: a define-once gate with a tracked exemption register (issue 274), strict typing and linting by default with an explicit opt-out (275), a repository that holds only what it needs long term (279), a local run of the managed secret scan and dependency audit (252), per-project account profiles with limit-aware seat routing (234), and the supervisor and separate-account layers of lane isolation (286, items 2 and 3; item 1 is TSK-437 in 4.0.0). The operator placed them on 2026-10-22 in one separate epic, smaller than EPC-022, sized by issue 280's guidance; this epic is that placement.
EPC-024.serves: It serves adopters who run several languages, several seats and hosted scans.
EPC-024.doneMeans: each task has landed on this epic's line with its cross-lineage review, the integrated body passes the full gate and the journeys below on the installed candidate, and its pull request to `main` is ready for a human merge.

EPC-025.title: the coordination ledger: follow-ups and lanes
EPC-025.deliverable: After this merges into the EPC-022 line and then `main`, any orchestrating or lone session, on any harness or model, can see and follow up every open commitment and every lane from disk, across restarts, usage limits, lost transcripts and a change of coordinator, and nothing handed over goes quiet. The operator approved the design on 2026-10-23 (cf-present session `dac94188`, `approve_with_notes` at revision 9) with three notes, folded in: direct work by the coordinator is tracked as a follow-up with no lane; a seat the new coordinator's harness cannot reach is judged by its own heartbeat and reports, never assumed dead, and replaced on its resources only with stopped-work evidence or a resolved overlap; and the data model ships with a field-level schema reference and a figure. Decided by the operator on 2026-10-22: the name "coordination ledger"; location A (clone-local), JSON Lines, one ledger per project (per clone, one machine), work streams `WS-NNN` with one live coordinator each so several coordinators run at once within and across harnesses, any session may add follow-ups, only the holder closes, closure on proof; lane scope is descriptive (task, tasks, epic or topic) and changes as events; `check interval` 10 minutes and `heartbeat timeout` 30 minutes, configurable, timeout longer than interval; takeover only by explicit `adopt`; the turn-end check warns by default and a policy key can make it blocking outside tracked delegate sessions; only a stream's coordinator opens or closes its lanes. Still open for the operator: the Codex hook route (TSK-440 establishes it). | Issue | Tasks | |---|---| | https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/272 | TSK-422 (contracts, store and `follow`), TSK-439 (lanes, attempts, seats, the coordinator lease, the parent link and session fields), TSK-1126 (reports flow up the tree), TSK-440 (surfaces on three harnesses and the tree view), TSK-423 (rules, skills, the three roles and the fresh-context proof) |
EPC-025.whatItIs: Issue 272 asked for an orchestrator follow-up ledger: every handed-over item logged, checked and closed on proof. The operator shaped it on 2026-10-22 into project-level working state that CodeFlow owns for any orchestrating model, and an independent Codex review of the design (sound with changes, 22 findings, 14 high) settled its contracts: the coordination ledger, a clone-local single event log with follow-ups (`FU-NNN`, `codeflow follow`) and lanes (`LN-NNN`, `codeflow lane`), the coordinator as lead role, hooks on every harness, and the rules and skills that adopt them (ADR-0086). It is its own small epic, sized by issue 280's guidance, and it targets 3.2.0 as the operator placed issue 272 there. It lands on its own integration line, `integration/EPC-025-the-coordination-ledger-follow-ups-and-lanes`, cut from the EPC-022 line, because the epic-line binding (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:880-917`) requires a task's epic to equal the line's epic, so an EPC-025 task cannot bind to the EPC-022 line (found at the first EPC-025 push on 2026-10-23; amended the same day, a reversible primary decision). The closing step: once its four tasks have landed and the epic's criteria are proven on its own installed candidate, the EPC-025 line merges into the EPC-022 line through one reviewed pull request, gated once as a candidate there, before the 3.2.0 pull request to `main`; that pull request describes both epics' outcomes, and the operator merges it. Amended 2026-10-24: `codeflow ci` lands an `integration/` head only on the default branch, so each merge of this line into the EPC-022 line is carried by an EPC-022 task branch that merges it (the first is TSK-1000), and the operator chose that day to merge the line once now, with TSK-422 landed, so the 3.2.0 pull request can open.

TSK-247.title: An update is previewed read-only before anything is written
TSK-247.about: After this merges, an agent in an adopting project can run `codeflow update --plan` against the live repository, see every file's predicted action, the citations and overrides the update makes stale and the paths only a person can write, with nothing on disk changed.
context: Fixes the preview portion of #74. An adopter who has tailored CodeFlow needs the whole update in view before it lands: which files change and how, which project rules and docs cite managed lines that move, which new defaults the project overrides, which skill mirrors have drifted apart, and which paths the agent's session cannot write so a person must. Today the only preview is one file's `decide` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/update.rs:141`), `--diff` writes its report after applying, and a sandboxed run that cannot write `.claude/` stops part way with the manifest unwritten. An adopter on 3.1.1 reported on 2026-10-13 that an agent now has no preview route at all: exporting the tree to a scratch copy is refused by the guard, so the preview has to run against the live repository without writing.

This task adds a read-only `codeflow update --plan [FILE]` produced by the same steps as the apply (one write sink, so the plan cannot drift from the apply), a cross-reference scan of project-owned text for citations of managed lines that move, a write preflight shared by plan and apply, the policy report for every changed default the project overrides, and a mirror-pair comparison. The plan separates the files an agent may resolve from the files only a person may change, so the agent prepares the first set and hands the person a short list for the second. It reads bases as `SPC-015` defines them (TSK-1087).

History: allocated as a standalone task on 2026-10-06 (its branch `task/TSK-247-update-plan` never landed); joined this epic on 2026-10-30 when the operator's version decision brought the read-only update plan into 4.0.0. Two criteria moved out on 2026-10-30 and their ids are retired, never reused: AC-5 (whole-file drift in doctor, which read the recorded shipped hash that the baseline replacement removes) is TSK-1087 AC-7, and AC-7 (the procedure file, `[scaffold] ignore` in the adoption guide and the skew warning naming the procedure) is TSK-1088 AC-1, AC-3 and AC-5; this task's skew warning names `--plan` only, under AC-9. Non-goals: generating one skill tree from the other (an ADR-sized change, a recorded follow-up in the epic), embedding changelog entries or ADRs (the plan links each release), and a doctor cross-reference check.

TSK-275.title: codeflow ci gives one verdict for a range however it is spelled
context: `codeflow ci` gives different `work.acceptance_binding` verdicts for one range when `--base` is a ref name or the commit id that ref points at (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/141), and an explicit `--head` takes its branch context from the checkout without saying so (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/130). After a sync merge of `main` into an integration line, both lead the tool to recommend reopening tasks already reviewed on `main`. At v3.1.0, `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:471-477` takes the acceptance target only from a named base, and `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:276-281` picks the frozen or amendable mode from it. This task resolves base, head and branch context once, before any rule runs, and makes the output say where each came from. The two issues share one cause and one code path, so they are one task. Non-goal: attribution of commits that follow a merge (issue 69).

Amended 2026-10-13 for https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/165: run locally without `--base`, the range base falls back to the policy's protected branches (`origin/main`) even when `--branch` names a branch that targets an integration line, so the range covers the whole line's divergence from `main` and reports criteria changes the line received as the branch's own (`detect_range` in `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs`, the terminal fallback). The branch's declared target is already readable: a task branch's `integration_target` (`declared_work_target`), a planning branch that names its epic, and an `integration/*` line, whose target is the default branch. Same resolution step, so the same task: the base is chosen from the declared target before the protected fallback, and the output says which rule chose it.

TSK-276.title: A planning amendment can update the project's document index
context: An epic amendment that adds a planning home cannot also add that home's row to the project's documentation map. `classify::amendment_path` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/classify.rs:257-281` at v3.1.0) admits records, plans and non-product files under `docs/`, but not a root index such as `DOC-INDEX.md`, so the range loses the planning class and fails `work.criteria_frozen` (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/136). The `docs/research/` half of https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/83 was fixed by PR 61 (TSK-229, ADR-0078); its index half and its request that the refusal name the admitted path set remain. The two issues are the same gap, so they are one task. This task lets a project declare its document index files in policy, admits them into a planning amendment, and makes the refusal name the path and the admitted set. Product globs keep precedence, so `docs/portal/**` stays out by design. Non-goal: a general configurable planning-path list (issue 83 option 1); one declared index is the narrower change and covers both reports.

TSK-277.title: A secret-scan exemption into the base can be classified
context: Since PR 26 the secret scan reads exemptions from the trusted base commit, so an integration line that carries a reviewed false positive needs a small exemption pull request into `main` first. That pull request has no class `codeflow ci` accepts (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/139): with `Task: TSK-NNN` it fails `work.stable_planning_anchor` on a dependency that is complete only on the line, and with `Task: EPC-NNN` `amendment_path` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/classify.rs:257` at v3.1.0) refuses the hidden `.gitleaksignore`. The operator then merges over a red required check. This task adds one narrow class for a range whose only changed path is the secret-scan ignore file the managed CI reads (`.gitleaksignore`). Non-goal: admitting the ignore file into the planning class, which would let any planning PR carry an exemption.

TSK-278.title: A closed record can be redacted without losing its results
context: A project that must remove personal or customer names from a completed record has no sanctioned route when a non-planning commit followed the record's landing on its line (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/134). PR 111 (TSK-253, ADR-0080) lets a completed standalone task's criteria text be corrected, but the acceptance block and an `acceptance_superseded` block cannot be redacted, and the waiver that the `work.acceptance_binding` message names has no documented field or format (a grep of `docs/` and cf-method finds none). This task adds a record-only redaction route that keeps every result, the reviewed commit and the review provenance and records a digest of the replaced text, and documents the waiver. Non-goal: changing a criterion's meaning or result, which stays a reopen.

TSK-279.title: One local command gives the hosted release-impact verdict
context: Pre-push runs `scripts/release.py preflight`, which never applies the marker floor or the equality rule that hosted `release impact` applies through `check-pr`, and `release_local::preflight` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/release_local.rs`) never passes the PR body. On 2026-10-08 PRs 99, 111 and 97 passed pre-push and failed hosted CI (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/117). This task gives one local command that returns the hosted verdict for a base, head and PR body, and makes the preflight report the same mismatches when a body is available. Pre-push keeps reporting them as warnings, as it reports a missing entry today (`docs/releasing.md:355`), and no policy key is added. Non-goal: making pre-push block on them.

TSK-280.title: Policy keys have one placement rule and a check
context: No written rule or check says where a new policy key goes, so agents ship keys in the policy template, where an adopter's older pinned binary can meet them and fail closed (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/118). Since 3.0.0, `git.pr_summary` lives only in the schema and the code default, with a per-key note (`crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/policy_schema.rs:392-393`); `git.claim_remotes` was first added to the template and then removed; two replays on 2026-10-08 put a key in the template again. This task writes one rule where a contributor adding a key reads, ties it to the two-step upgrade in `docs/adoption.md`, and adds a check that holds it. TSK-276 adds a key and follows this rule, so it lands after this task.

TSK-281.title: Temporary-file writes never follow a link at the temp name
context: `file_lock::atomic_write` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/file_lock.rs:328-333` at v3.1.0) writes a fixed `<path>.tmp` with `fs::write`, which follows a symbolic link at that name. A branch that commits a link at `.codeflow/test-config.schema.tmp` can redirect the test-config schema write (`crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/setup/mod.rs:423`), and other writers have their own temp paths (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/96 and its comment). TSK-244 fixed the record writers through `crates/codeflow-core/src/contained.rs` and left this class open. This task makes every CodeFlow temp write safe against a planted link, or records why a location is trusted.

TSK-282.title: Test fixtures stay in their own folder and never hang on pipes
context: Running the tests with `TMPDIR` inside a git repository made two commits on that repository's branch and rewrote its `core.hooksPath`, because fixtures create a project folder without `git init` and git discovers the enclosing repository (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/104; `crates/codeflow-core/tests/scaffold_test.rs:22-28`, `:249-260`, `:280`, `:1787-1788` at v3.1.0). Separately, a test that polls a child before reading its piped output hangs when the host pipe buffer is small (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/100). The named estimate test was fixed in PR 84; the `read_bounded_regular` FIFO unit test and a durable check for the class remain. Both issues are test-harness hygiene in the same helpers, so they are one task. It changes no shipped behaviour.

TSK-283.title: Guards read the git configuration a command will use
context: Exec-guard's outward-release check reads a git alias from configuration files and `-c` and refuses `--config-env`, but it ignores configuration given through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` or `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/98; `crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs:725-790` at v3.1.0). Only git-guard covers that case today. Files that an existing `include.path` or `includeIf.*.path` names are not protected, so a planted alias or pager there runs under a later git command (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/88; an open residual in `docs/policy-reference.md:476-477`). Both need the configuration git will actually use, and one shared reader serves both, so they are one task.

TSK-284.title: Files that run code in a later shell or login are protected
context: Three kinds of file make code run later without any command the guards judge: a program written into a user directory on `PATH` ahead of the real one (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/87); a session environment file under `environment.d` that sets `PATH`, `BASH_ENV` or `ZDOTDIR` for every later shell (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/90); and a login item such as `~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist`, a systemd user unit or an autostart entry (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/91). Each is issue 86's class (planted startup state) through a user folder, each is protected by path for native edits and shell writes, and ADR-0075 tracks all three, so one design and one guard change serve them. Package-manager settings (issue 89) are split into TSK-285 because a project `.npmrc` is a repository file adopters edit for ordinary reasons and needs a key-level rule, not a path rule.

TSK-285.title: Package-manager script shell settings are guarded
context: npm runs every package script through the program its `script-shell` setting names, read from `~/.npmrc`, a project `.npmrc` and the environment; setting it makes every later `npm run`, `npm test` or install script run a chosen program while the guards see only `npm test` (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/89). yarn and pnpm have similar settings. A project `.npmrc` is a repository file that adopters edit for registries and engines, so a whole-file path rule would block ordinary work; this task guards the runner keys and the commands that set them. It is split from TSK-284 for that reason: a different file class, a key-level rule and a different effect on adopters.

TSK-286.title: The deletion guard is proven against the native tools
context: The deletion guard judges a command by its own model of each tool's input grammar, and where that model differs from the native tool it can allow a command that deletes something it would refuse if typed directly (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/102). PR 84 fixed the `-0`, `-d`, quoting and parallel newline cases and judges every unmodelled xargs or parallel option as unproven; the rest of the grammar has no native proof. The issue's comments add two findings: `crates/codeflow-core/src/root_checkout.rs:918` maps a literal Unix backslash in a `.gitmodules` path to `/`, and `crates/codeflow-core/src/ids/inventory.rs:32-41` splits a remote ref at its first slash. This task proves the guard against the native tools. Its sed row builds on TSK-290 (lands on main in 3.1.1; the line takes it when it merges main): TSK-290 gives git-guard one sed script reader for issue 147, and this task's sed row proves the guards against native sed through it. TSK-290 is not on this line, so it is not in `depends_on`.

Amended 2026-10-13 after re-reading the issue's comments. Both findings above are this task's AC-4, and each still needs the native fixture the comments say was not run (`root_checkout.rs:918` and `inventory.rs:37-40` are unchanged at `main` 4226a9408). The comment from the PR 84 review says which xargs and parallel options are to be modelled: the ones PR 84 round 19 judges unproven. The line takes 3.1.1, and with it TSK-290's sed reader (`crates/codeflow-core/src/security/sed_script.rs`), by the merge of `main` that this amendment's pull request names, so once that merge is on the line the sed rows start with the other grammars. TSK-299 (planned in draft pull request 162) changes how a nested quoted sed script is judged; the sed rows here prove whatever reader the line holds when they run. `ids/inventory.rs` is also read by the adopter feature epic's program report, which builds on the corrected remote boundary.

TSK-287.title: Every judging history read refuses an overlaid history
context: Local history checks trust commit parents that a graft file, a replace ref, a forged commit-graph or a shallow boundary can rewrite (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/122). PR 107 guarded `review_covers_pin` by calling `release_line::history_overlay` and `shallow_boundary` first, but parent and ancestry reads are not centralized: at v3.1.0 the guard is called from a few sites (`acceptance.rs:946-955`, `landing.rs:192-196`, `work_start.rs:1328-1333` and `:1933`, `release_line.rs`), and about 30 judging sites in the issue's sweep read parents directly. Hosted CI on a fresh clone is unaffected; the local floor (pre-push, work start, task status, a local `codeflow ci`) is not. This task adds one guarded reader and moves every judging site onto it.

TSK-291.title: CodeFlow's own pushes use a configured non-personal credential
context: CodeFlow's own pushes (the registry reservation from `task new`, `epic new` and `adr new`, `work claim`, `epic new --integration`, `ids sync`) use whatever git credential is ambient (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/151). A project that requires agent pushes to come from a bot or GitHub App identity had to inject a credential helper per command through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and its keys. Since 3.1.0 git-guard refuses that route under `git.hook_integrity` (the issue comment), and repository or worktree writes of `credential.*.helper` are refused too, so an agent's reservation goes out under the operator's personal credential; the adopter has stopped agent CodeFlow pushes. This task gives a first-class setting that CodeFlow applies to its own pushes only, reports it in doctor, and can refuse an agent push when no non-personal credential is configured. A credential helper runs a program (`credential.helper=!cmd`), so where the setting is read from and who may change it is a security boundary; the design settles it first. It is first in the 4.0.0 build order because an adopter is blocked on it.

Amended 2026-10-13 for the adopter's comment of that day on issue 151: on 3.1.1 the per-command route is still refused, and the 3.1.1 notes' upgrade step (a repository-scope helper set after an empty value) omits `credential.useHttpPath`. A helper that answers for one repository only never sees the path unless `credential.useHttpPath=true` is also set, so git gets no credential and, with the empty reset, has no fallback. When CodeFlow applies the helper per call, it passes `useHttpPath` with it, or the design note says why that is not needed.

TSK-292.title: A project can refuse inline gitleaks:allow on trusted commits
context: The managed secret scan accepts an inline `gitleaks:allow` on any commit the trusted commit already holds (`assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml:739-773` at v3.1.0). A project that refuses every inline allow, so that a finding is exempted only through the reviewed ignore file on the base, must delete the `held` filter from the managed step and carry that edit through every update (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/152). The same step passes `HEAD` or `<sha>..HEAD` to `--log-opts` without resolving `HEAD` or ending with `--` (`:458-466`, `:722`); a path named `HEAD` would make git's argument ambiguous, which fails closed today. This task adds a policy key for the inline allow, hardens every revision enumeration and diagnoses legacy remerge fingerprints for reviewed migration. It is split from TSK-294 (the same workflow file) because the secret scan is a security boundary with its own review.

TSK-293.title: codeflow integrate can land a reviewed head with a merge commit
context: `codeflow integrate` lands a unit by rebasing it onto the line and fast-forwarding (`crates/codeflow-core/src/integrate.rs:1-7` and `:241-266` at v3.1.0). A project that lands each reviewed head with a no-fast-forward merge, to keep the reviewed commit and the acceptance binding that names it unchanged on the line, can use `integrate` only when the unit already sits on the line tip; every other landing is a hand merge, gate and push (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/150). This task adds a merge mode. Rebase stays the default.

TSK-294.title: A project can route dependency-audit exceptions through its own reviewed check
context: When the managed dependency audit fails, its advice tells the reader to record a suppression in an `osv-scanner.toml` beside the lockfile (`assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml:920`, with the route described at `:822-829` at v3.1.0). A project that records audit exceptions elsewhere, such as a reviewed dependency register with an owner, an expiry and a reason per row, must edit the managed step and reconcile that edit on every update (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/149). This task adds a project exception hook, on the pattern of the project setup hook `.codeflow/ci-setup.sh` that issue 46 added: an optional script, read from the trusted commit, that runs after the managed audit and may accept findings that a trusted project file records. When the hook exists, the failure advice names it. The hook is chosen over an advice text key because it serves both halves of the issue without a new policy key. The 3.1.0 hardening that replaces every `osv-scanner.toml` with the trusted commit's copy stays.

TSK-304.title: Pre-push checks every pushed tree or refuses the push
context: With `git.test_gate_on_push` at `block`, a commit that fails the push set can still be pushed: edit a tracked file without committing and push again, and the pre-push hook skips the tree checks with a note (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/156, reproduced 2026-10-12). `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs` runs `validate --docs` and the quick targets only when the checkout is clean, complete and at the pushed commit (`push_set.rs:184`, `tracked_tree_clean` at `:1725`); every other ref gets the `PUSH_TREE_UNCHECKED` note, never a violation, whatever the level. The range checks still run first, so not every pre-push check is skipped. The existing CLI tests in `crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli.rs` expect success on the unchecked dirty-tree and other-ref paths.

This task makes the gate fail closed for the whole class, not only the dirty-file spelling: at `block`, a pushed ref whose tree the hook cannot check (dirty tracked files, a ref other than `HEAD`, several refs in one push, a sparse or incomplete checkout, a submodule whose checkout differs from the pushed gitlink) is either checked on the pushed commit in a temporary checkout or refused with the clean-checkout remedy. The builder chooses between the two and records the choice and its cost in the PR; the Codex triage of 2026-10-13 (`triage-codex-02.md`, "Patch contents and release order") names both. Lower levels keep the note, honestly worded. The documented caveat that untracked files can influence a working-tree test (`push_set.rs:11`) stays and is tested.

The destination-held exception is limited to advertised branch history: tag pushes run no push set and cannot establish this exemption. A clean, complete checkout at the pushed commit still runs the tree checks first (AC-4).

Operator record: kept first in 3.2.0 rather than in a 3.1.2 patch (SETTLED_DISSENT of 2026-10-13 in the workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`), because hosted CI reruns the same checks on every pull request and they are required on protected branches. Non-goal: changing which checks the push set holds.

TSK-305.title: An unanswered default-branch lookup is reported as a network failure
context: `codeflow ci` and the pre-push hook ask the destination for its default branch with one `git ls-remote --symref` call and a fixed 10-second deadline (`crates/codeflow-core/src/git/remote_query.rs:15`, `ls_remote` at `:28`, no retry). When the destination answers slowly, the push is refused (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/161). The failure is wrapped at `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/release_line.rs:182-187` and reported by `scope_refusal` in `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:223` and by the record check in `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/work_records.rs:142`.

Two parts of the report differ in age. The message the issue quotes, with a `sanctioned` line that points at a planning PR, is the older text: at `main` 4226a9408, `scope_refusal` already says "repair the destination or policy named above, then rerun codeflow ci" (`acceptance.rs:227`). The defect that remains in the current source is the classification: a destination failure is still reported under a lifecycle rule (`work.criteria_frozen` through `FROZEN_RULE`, and `work.records`) rather than under a rule of its own, and its remedy does not name the network.

Failing closed is right and stays: an unanswered destination never lets a range through unjudged, and a stale local default is never trusted. This task distinguishes the causes (a timeout, an authentication failure, a malformed advertisement, and a destination with no usable default branch) and reports each once under its own rule with a remedy that names the network or the remote. One shared lookup owns the query and its bounded retry sequence: a first-attempt success makes one network attempt; a timeout gets a bounded number of extra attempts with a short backoff, whether they end in success or exhaustion; the other causes are not retried. The lookup's final answer, or its final error, is cached and shared: pre-push passes it to its child checks (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:354-360`, `--advertisement-stdin`), and no child check or additional pushed ref queries the destination again. Scope per the Codex triage of 2026-10-13 (`triage-codex-01.md`, the paragraph on issue 161). Non-goal: a configurable deadline.

TSK-306.title: A line's newer task version wins over a copy main inherited
context: Pre-push refuses a task branch on an integration line when `main` holds an older version of the task record that the line itself held and later amended (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/176). With `main` and the line diverged, `judge` in `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/landing.rs` (from `:442`) finds no judged point that is newer than every other (`:458-475`), falls to `agreed` (`:523-559`), and refuses whenever the held criteria signatures differ. It never asks whether one point's version was inherited and then replaced on the other point's line. The issue states the search backwards: `judge` looks for a point that descends from every other point, not for their common ancestor. The current refusal is intended: `held_versions_that_differ_still_give_no_answer` (`landing.rs:1354`) builds this shape and expects unknown authority, so this task changes that test and settles the inheritance rule. 3.1.1's issue 153 fix (TSK-295) left this case unresolved; it did not cause it.

The fix adapts the inherited-supersession reasoning the recovered-record path already has (`recovered` from `:562`, `inherited` at `:633`, and its merge-resolution handling near `:668`, which tells choosing an old version apart from inheriting it unchanged) to held records, and keeps refusing competing introductions, ambiguous identities, unreadable history and overlays. Copying the helper alone does not supply every safeguard of its current caller. The issue's suggested rule, dropping a version whose bytes appear somewhere in the other point's history, is not used: `main` may revert to v1, reintroduce v1 independently or resolve a merge to v1 after the line chose v2, and equal bytes do not make those decisions stale (`triage-codex-02.md`, "The stale-record refusal"). This is a core acceptance rule, never a project setting.

Recovery first. Merging current `main` into the line makes `main` an ancestor of the line tip, so a task range based on the new tip has a newest judged point (`landing.rs:458-475`) and takes the line's criteria without `agreed`. That recovery is proved through the installed hooks before any code, and the result is written in this record. If it fails through the installed gates and no other sanctioned recovery exists, the operator decides whether this fix moves to 3.1.2 (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, triage of 2026-10-13). Merging `main` into the task branch alone, while the judged line base stays old, is not the same recovery, and dropping `--policy-from` or `--commits-from` is not a workaround.

Written before any code, at the EPC-022 line tip 1e6e29e93 (`landing.rs` line numbers below are at that revision). It settles the held-version inheritance rule, the cases, the AC-1 recovery procedure and the change to the existing test. The AC-1 result is appended to this record as a dated "Recovery proof" note when the procedure is run, before the first code commit; nothing below reports a run. Revised the same day after the Codex design review (`target/review-design-TSK-306-codex-01.md`): the recovery procedure's judged points and its setup route are corrected (F1, F2), and the three fix-now clarifications are taken (fixture interleaving, the stricter `recovered` path, the AC-5 and AC-6 output). Revised again after the build found F4 (`target/review-design-TSK-306-codex-03.md`, `target/build-TSK-306.md`): the rule now compares introductions with introductions, never with a tip, so a version one point restored after seeing the other's stays a competing decision; the rule paragraph, the walk-through table and the `recovered` consequence below are the revised text. Revised a third time on 2026-10-15 after the security review's SEC-306-01 (`target/security-review-TSK-306-01.md`): introductions are traced by criteria signature, not by blob; the definitions, the introduction paragraph, the blob-or-signature decision and the non-criteria row of the walk-through table are the revised text.

**The shape.** `main` planned T at v1; the line forked from that commit and amended T to v2; `main` moved on without touching T. The pre-push judges the task branch at two points: the line tip (the range base) and the `main` tip (`--policy-from`).

Neither point descends from the other, so `judge` finds no newest point (`landing.rs:458-475`) and asks `agreed` (`:523-559`), which compares only the criteria signatures the points hold now and refuses at `:550`. `held_versions_that_differ_still_give_no_answer` (`:1354`) builds this exact shape and expects the refusal.

**The inheritance rule for held records (decision, revised for F4).** Definitions first. For a held judged point P, `s(P)` is the criteria signature of the record P holds for T (`CriteriaList::signature`, the one the criteria freeze compares), and `I(P)` is the set of commits in P's history that introduce `s(P)`: a commit holds a record with `s(P)` while some parent holds no record of T or one with another signature, or it has no parent. A merge that resolves a conflict between two signatures therefore introduces the one it keeps, whatever its bytes, and a merge whose parents all hold `s(P)` introduces nothing. `I(P)` is read by the shared walk over P's whole history and is unreadable, which refuses, on an overlay, a shallow cut, a held doubt, a second uid, or when it comes back empty. The refusal messages still name each point's blob, which identifies the record it holds.
The predicate, for two held points P and Q whose criteria signatures differ:
> P yields to Q if and only if every commit in `I(P)` is a proper > ancestor of every commit in `I(Q)`.

Read: Q's version was decided, every time it was decided, after every decision for P's version, so P's version is the older on every line that holds either, and P's tip holds it unchanged since. The relation is asymmetric (mutual yielding would need c before d and d before c) and needs no point order. Among the held points, every point that yields to some other held point with a different signature is dropped; the points left must share one criteria signature, and the record of the point left (the newest of them when more than one agree) is the authority; otherwise no answer, naming each point and its blob (AC-5). The same predicate replaces `inherited` on the `recovered` path (`:590-608`, `:633-704`), so the spec states one rule.

What this tells apart, and why the first rule could not: the first rule compared `I(P)` with the other point's tip ("every introduction of P's version is an ancestor of Q"). A tip is reached by everything the point merged, so when `main` merged the commit B that introduced the line's v2 and then restored v1, every introduction of v2 was an ancestor of `main`'s tip and the rule dropped the line's own decision as if it were an inherited copy, leaving `main`'s restoration as the authority, which AC-3 forbids (F4, the two failing tests). Introductions are decisions and tips are not. Comparing with `I(Q)` instead, the restoration fails on both sides: `main`'s v1 has an introduction (the restoring commit R) that precedes no introduction of v2, so `main` does not yield; and v1's first introduction A precedes B, so the line's v2 does not yield either, because v1 was not decided wholly after v2. Both decisions stay, and the answer is unknown. In the positive case `main`'s v1 has the one introduction A, which precedes B, and v2's introduction B precedes nothing of v1, so only `main` yields. The two conditions AC-2 names are this predicate read from each side: every introduction of v1 precedes the line's v2 (main yields), and the line replaced v1 with v2 after holding it (v2's introductions descend from v1's, which is the same ancestry read the other way). A version a point introduced after it saw the other's is a competing decision, never a stale copy, whatever its bytes.

An introduction is a decision for a signature: a commit introduces it when it holds it and at least one parent holds no record of T or another signature. A merge whose sides held different signatures introduces the one it keeps, as a merge naming the record's path against the automatic remerge did under the blob reading; a merge whose sides held the same signature, with any text, introduces nothing.

On the `recovered` path (revised 2026-10-15 for SEC-306-04 and the Codex review's F2, `target/security-review-TSK-306-02.md`, `target/review-TSK-306-codex-05.md`): when two holders hold different criteria, one supersedes the other only by criteria-signature introductions, exactly as on the held path. Status and epic never erase an earlier introduction of a competing signature: tracing the tuple of criteria, status and epic let a restore of S that also changed the epic or status drop S's first introduction A, so the line's V yielded where AC-3 requires no answer. Status and epic only order holders whose criteria agree (`same_version`), where the walk traces the tuple, so a line's completed version still supersedes a stale line's planned one with the same criteria (the control at `landing.rs` near :1426 and TSK-295's expectations).

The introductions of a version are a property of one task's history, so the run's cache of them is keyed by the task's full identity (id, uid and own file) as well as the holder and the version, and a cached refusal is kept per task too (SEC-306-03, Codex F1): one task's proof never answers for another task with the same criteria.
**What identifies a version in the walk: blob or signature (decision, revised for SEC-306-01).** Two options were open.

TSK-307.title: A misshapen acceptance file is refused by name
context: `codeflow task status <id> complete --acceptance <file>` refuses a file whose YAML has no top-level `acceptance:` key with "a complete record needs an acceptance block in its Closeout", which names the task record and reads as a problem with it (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/175). The command reads the file verbatim and inserts it (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/new.rs:733`), and the lifecycle check then finds no block (`NO_BLOCK`, `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/lifecycle.rs:894`). The option's help (`new.rs:96`) says "the YAML between the fences", which starts with `acceptance:`, but the template comment lists the fields, not the key. This task parses the file before inserting it and refuses a file without the top-level key with a message that names the file and the key. It does not wrap the fields silently: the refusal is explicit, so a lane learns the shape once. Non-goal: changing the acceptance block's fields.

TSK-308.title: The acceptance binding counts a landed line adoption
context: After a task's landing merge, any non-merge commit on the line's first-parent chain that changes a non-planning path refuses that task's acceptance binding (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:1079-1140`, the message at `:1137`). Since 3.1.0 an epic records a reviewed direct commit in `line_adoptions` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/line_adoption.rs:1-10`), and the pull request classifier reads it; the binding does not. So an adopted direct commit, such as an owner's `.gitleaksignore` change on an epic line, still refuses the binding of every task landed before it (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/167, part E). This task is the narrow defect of issue 167; the issue's other parts are the adopter feature epic's work (design task T1 of the adopter design approved on 2026-10-13).

The binding consumes the verified result of `line_adoption::check_range`, errors included, so an adoption the line check proves counts like a merge for that binding, and a forged entry on a branch, an unreadable history or a changed acceptance block stays refused. `bind_completion` (`acceptance.rs:341`) also gains a public structured result (the reviewed commit, the landing merge, the span head and the completion tail), which the adopter feature epic's carry task reads (design foundation F7). The adopter's case is declared fixed only after a reproduction with a valid, landed entry (`triage-codex-01.md`, the issue 167 row). Non-goal: the record-hygiene checks and guidance of issue 167 parts A to D.

TSK-309.title: codeflow update never lowers the project's pinned version
context: `codeflow update` writes the binary's own version into `scaffold_version` unconditionally (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/update.rs:371-373`), so an update run by a binary older than the project's pin lowers the pin and rewrites managed files with the older binary's assets, while the `[scaffold_sha256]` table may still name the newer release. `codeflow update --pin` already refuses a lower version (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/release_pin.rs:418`, "the pin only rises"), and `version_skew_warning` only warns (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/version.rs:33-43`). Found by the adopter feature design of 2026-10-13 (section 9, approved by the operator), which homes the fix in this epic; the adopter epic's install-on-clone task relies on a pin that never falls. This task makes `update` refuse, before it writes anything, when the binary is older than the project's `scaffold_version`, naming both versions and the remedy. The fix binds binaries that carry it; an older released binary still behaves as before, which the release note states. Non-goal: a `codeflow ci` check on a pull request that lowers the pin.

TSK-311.title: The program report shows every record on every fetched line

next.reason: task TSK-311 depends on TSK-286, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: An adopter with many integration lines has no generated answer to "where does the program stand": `codeflow status` reads the working tree only (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/status.rs:7-17`), and `work next` judges a record only on its own target's tip (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs:633-657`) (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/166). This task adds `codeflow report program [--json] [--host] [--strict] [--epic] [--line]`, a read-only report over every fetched ref that says, for each epic and task, which copy is the truth and whether every other copy is the same version, behind, ahead or divergent. It builds the two foundations the rest of EPC-023 reads (design section 3):

items.text: F1, the cross-ref record reader: one snapshot of ref names to object ids; parsed fields per distinct blob; the last-change commit per record path per distinct tip; full ref names as identity, with a label; unreadable records kept in totals as `unreadable`; a duplicate id with a different `uid` is a conflict row. It extends the `ids` inventory (`crates/codeflow-core/src/ids/inventory.rs`).

F2, home and currency. A task's home is its `integration_target` as its copies on the trusted remote's default branch and integration lines declare it; disagreement, or two lines matching an epic, is `unknown`. An epic's home is its unique line, else the default branch. The home copy is the truth. The last-change commit of a record on a ref is the newest commit on that ref's first-parent chain whose blob differs from its first parent's or, for a merge, from either parent's; a merge whose result and both parents agree is no change. Each other copy carries agreement (`equal`, `differs`), currency (`equal` is `same`; for `differs`, with H the home's last change and C the copy's: `behind` when C is reachable from the home tip, else `ahead` when H is reachable from the copy's tip, else `divergent`; `unknown` when the home is unfetched or ambiguous or the history read refuses) and placement (`home`, `elsewhere`, `off home only`, `planned on default`, `branch only`).

context: Each row carries, for every epic and task on every fetched ref: the home, the status at home, each other copy with its agreement, currency and placement, the derived readiness (as `work next` derives it at the home, `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs`) and the branches that hold it. Rollups are by epic and by line, and per epic the estimate against the actual where recorded outcomes exist (`crates/codeflow-core/src/estimate/outcomes/`). A fact the report cannot supply is an explicit incomplete-data field: readiness is `unknown` when the home is `unknown` or unfetched, and the estimate-against-actual fields are `unavailable` when an epic has no outcomes, never zero and never omitted.

Authority comes only from copies in the trusted remote's namespace (the remote `landed_policy` selects) on the default branch and `integration/*` lines; local branches, other remotes and forks are shown and never choose a home. The report never fetches and prints its snapshot time; filters filter output only; `--host` adds pull request facts, else `unknown`. Class and lane grouping is TSK-314. Non-goal: any check or verdict; this is a report.

Amended 2026-10-22 on the move to EPC-022, for issue 280 item 2: each line row also carries the drift facts TSK-420's reader derives (commits behind the protected target, the last sync event and its date, the creation state (known from evidence, or `unknown` with the oldest divergent commit labelled), the oldest unlanded task's age, and the flag against the project's sync interval), read through that reader, never recomputed. The per-stream view of open epics the issue's comment asks for is not in this report: streams are clone-local coordination ledger state (EPC-025), which a record-only report never reads; `codeflow coord status` (TSK-440) shows it, and a tracked stream home would be TSK-313's vocabulary (4.1.0) if the operator wants it here. Deferred, named.

next.reason: task TSK-312 depends on TSK-311, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: `codeflow status` has no `--json` (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/status.rs:7-17`), so a tool that wants the checkout's work facts parses text (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/166).
