context: This task builds on the input classes and per-target evidence TSK-352 adds; it does not define a second key.
Decisions recorded here:

items.text: **Two kinds of completeness.** A *completed target execution* is one target that ran to its end in some run: its exit status was recorded, it was not interrupted, cancelled or timed out, it passed, its declared inputs were unchanged from its start to its end, and every output it declares exists with a recorded digest. A *complete gate* is today's run-level `complete`: an unrestricted full run with no skipped target. Reuse needs the first and never produces the second.

**What may be reused.** A completed target execution from any run (quick, essential, full or `--only`), whether or not that run was a complete gate, may be reused when its `content` class and its evidence (TSK-352: mode and command, tools, platform, relevant environment, membership, producer outputs and inputs) match the current check. A target of any other class or with any missing evidence executes. Environment equality uses TSK-352's one contract (audited non-secret metadata as values, opaque keyed fingerprints otherwise, fail closed when neither is safe); this task adds no other encoding and never stores or prints a raw environment value.

**Producer outputs.** A consumer is reused only when each producer's output exists now and matches its recorded digest; a missing or corrupt output makes the producer execute and the consumer re-evaluate.
**Provenance.** A reused result names the run that executed it; a result reused again keeps naming that original run, never an intermediate one.
**Never certification.** A run that reuses any target is never recorded complete. A landing candidate's gate runs with `--all` and executes every target (TSK-352).
**Push protections.** The pre-push ref, range, authority, release preflight and checked-out-tree checks are never reused. The repository's config decides which targets qualify; unknown means no.

context: Non-goals: hosted CI reuse (TSK-359), and any compiler cache (not adopted; TSK-357 records the verdict). Product surface: adopter-facing engine (CAP-004 run records and the gate runner) and the pre-push hook path.

TSK-356.title: Slow test fixtures run once and exhaustive matrices run in the full gate
context: Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17, ranked change 4 and its table of the 30 slowest tests (JUnit of run `8b201fe4-2175-47a7-b3b8-1ac6961dfc71`, 5,278 cases, 11,040 seconds of summed test time, 1,144 seconds elapsed).

The full gate's elapsed time has a floor set by the nextest serial group (`.config/nextest.toml`): 319 cases and 737.27 seconds, of which `init_e2e` is 585.76 seconds. The slowest case, `fresh_scaffolds_install_the_confirmed_herdr_delivery_and_update_brings_it` (`crates/codeflow-cli/tests/init_e2e.rs`), takes 242.02 seconds because it runs the Herdr stub suite six times: four fresh installs and two updates. Two remedy tests in `crates/codeflow-cli/tests/remedy_clearing/push.rs` each sleep 61 seconds to cross a time budget. Other slow cases rebuild the same planned-project fixtures many times (`readiness_journey.rs`, `read_commands_offline.rs`, `release_line_cli.rs`, `ci_cli.rs`) or run exhaustive tier, harness and crash matrices on every run.

Outcome: the full gate keeps every distinct boundary it proves while repeated identical work runs once, and exhaustive matrices are placed explicitly: the full gate runs them all; routine runs keep representative and security counterexample cases.

Overlap settled here, folded rather than duplicated: the restored test-time task of PR 224 (it replaces TSK-301) owns the guard random-words fuzz tests and `startup::installed_hooks_refuse_unresolved_forms_beside_a_named_target`, including their timing and the `rust-coverage` time limit. This task does not change those tests. TSK-351 (the hosted repair) owns the fixture fixes it lists; this task starts from its landed fixtures.

Non-goals: removing a test, a security counterexample or a distinct installation, recovery or shell boundary; adding any environment variable or production knob that shortens a security timeout; the coverage floor. Product surface: this repository's tests and gate config. A testability seam in production timing code, if needed, is product code and states so.

TSK-357.title: Rust build profiles cut disk and runtime without new tools
context: Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17 (ranked change 6), and the primary's build-speed research of the same day (scratchpad `build-speed-research.md`, read-only, nothing built), which replaced the planned sccache pilot with this task by the primary's decision of 2026-10-17.
Where the time goes, from 32 passing essential runs in 6 worktrees:

items.text: The essential Rust test step is 79 to 98 percent serial test-binary execution (94 to 100 binaries); its wall time ranged from 1,183 to 2,650 seconds. TSK-354 moves it to nextest.

Warm compile steps take 35 to 133 seconds (`rust-build` 35 to 96, `rust-clippy` 41 to 133), with outliers of 480 to 600 seconds under contention. Clippy waited on the build directory lock in 7 of 18 sampled runs; TSK-331 AC-9 gives clippy its own target directory.

Disk: one worktree's `target/debug` holds 56 GB (30 GB `incremental`, 26 GB `deps` with 453,923 `.o` files); worktree target directories total about 260 GB. On macOS the default `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"` leaves debug info in object files.

The debug `codeflow` binary is 75.6 MB (release 18.2 MB), and the tests launch it thousands of times (123 `CARGO_BIN_EXE_codeflow` uses, 282 `Command::new` in tests) with unoptimized dependencies. The first launch of a freshly linked binary took 1.06 seconds (one sample), then 0.01.

`crates/codeflow-cli/build.rs` reruns on changes under `crates`, `assets`, `docs`, `project-management`, `.agents`, `.claude` and more, and emits three `rustc-env` values; whether that recompiles all 52 CLI integration test targets after a docs-only edit is unverified.

context: Outcome: Rust build profiles and test layout cut disk use and build and test time without any new tool, each change kept only if its measurement meets its criterion.
In order:

items.text: **Do first: debug info.** `[profile.dev] debug = "line-tables-only"` for workspace crates, `[profile.dev.package."*"] debug = false` for dependencies, and an opt-in `[profile.debugging]` (`inherits = "dev"`, `debug = true`) for debugger sessions. Cargo PR 17518 proposes the same default upstream.

**Pilot: optimized dependencies in dev.** `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 1`, measured on test wall time, since the tests spawn the debug binary thousands of times. The repository already does this for `sha2`.

**Pilot: fewer integration test binaries.** Consolidate the 77 integration test files (52 in codeflow-cli, 24 in codeflow-core, 1 in codeflow-present) into a few binaries per crate, codeflow-core first, updating nextest filters that name binaries (`binary(present_cli)`, `binary(init_e2e)`, `binary(test_gate_cli)`) and any CI references.

**Check: the build-script cascade.** Whether a docs-only edit rebuilds the CLI binary and all 52 CLI test targets. If it does, the fix touches the embedded-identity design and is a separate decision; this task records the finding.

**Measure only: macOS XProtect first-launch scanning.** How much it adds per fresh binary and per test run. Exempting a terminal or agent host from XProtect weakens a system security control; that is the operator's decision, and this task only measures and reports.

context: Not adopted now, with the research verdict recorded: a compiler cache. sccache's Rust cache key includes the working directory, so hits across worktrees at different paths are unproven; it cannot cache incremental, bin or proc-macro crates; and compile time is a minor share of the gate. Revisit event: compile time becomes a material share of gate time after TSK-354 and this task land. kache is not considered (created 2026-02-15, one author with most commits). Shared target or build directories, other linkers, Cranelift and the parallel frontend stay out, as the research explains.

Non-goals: sharing any target or build directory between worktrees, installing any tool, changing the hook binary's embedded identity, and any XProtect setting. Product surface: this repository's `Cargo.toml` profiles, test layout and gate config; no shipped default changes.

TSK-358.title: Hosted Linux and Windows gates run on ready pull requests into integration lines
context: Source: the hosted-red diagnosis of 2026-10-17 ("Main merge impact and the process gap") and the operator's direction of the same day, relayed by the primary, to close that gap.

At `eaf2ed04e`, this repository's `.github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml` ran its Linux and Windows gate jobs on a pull request only when the base is `main` or `master`: the `if:` of `gates`, `gates-coverage`, `gates-coverage-report`, `gates-verdict`, `windows-build`, `windows-tests`, `windows`, `windows-release-journey`, `windows-journeys` and `windows-verdict` (lines 102, 283, 364, 416, 455, 513, 571, 621, 638 and 680 at `eaf2ed04e`). A task pull request into `integration/**` therefore landed with those jobs skipped, and its first Linux and Windows result arrived after landing. PRs 209 and 210 show this: their rollups mark every Linux and Windows job SKIPPED, they merged at 17:27 UTC on 2026-10-17, and their pushes added new failures to a line that had been red since 2026-10-12. The shipped template (`assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml`) has no such restriction; the restriction is this repository's own.

Outcome: a pull request into an integration line gets hosted Linux and Windows verdicts before it lands, once it is ready for review. A draft skips the expensive gates and runs security jobs plus verdicts that report the missing gates.

Cost, from one failed-run sample (run 39053855357 on 2026-10-17, which failed): 157.25 summed job minutes (55.58 Linux, 101.67 Windows), 30m42s from run start to its last update, of which about 16m14s passed before the first job started and 14m27s was job execution; a fan-out of 19 jobs at once (12 Windows partitions, 5 gate parts, 2 coverage shards). A green run and queueing will differ; AC-4 measures this task's own run. The repository is public, so standard GitHub-hosted runner minutes are not billed. The real costs are the account's concurrent job slots, which every workflow shares, the queueing that causes for other runs, and the wait per ready push. At this line's recent rate (17 merged pull requests from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-17) that is a few extra runs a day; a new push to a ready pull request cancels its run in progress (the workflow's `concurrency` group). Until TSK-359 lands, the push that lands each pull request runs the jobs again.

The operator decided on 2026-10-17 that a GitHub ruleset shall require the hosted `codeflow gates` and `windows` checks on `integration/**`, applied once TSK-377 has made the line green. The primary prepares the ruleset and shows its exact content before applying it; this task carries that as AC-6. (Historical; superseded on 2026-10-18: the operator applies the ruleset, as the Deliverables and Execution contract below state.)

Non-goals: changing the shipped template, the secret scan, canary and security review jobs, and broader hosted reuse (TSK-359). Reuse association checks found in review are repaired here because integration pull request runs expose them. Product surface: this repository's CI and its integration-line ruleset.

TSK-359.title: An integration push reuses the hosted verdict of an identical pull request tree
context: Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17, ranked change 7, and `scripts/ci-reuse.py`. Amended after the Codex review of PR 226 (finding F2).

A push to `main` already reuses a pull request run's verdict when the pushed merge commit has exactly the tree of the pull request head and the conditions in `scripts/ci-reuse.py` hold (one merged pull request, ancestry, unchanged cache inputs, the present part's apt cache, and a fully successful pull request run). The operator approved that reuse on 2026-10-11 for `main`, and on 2026-10-17 extended it to integration lines.

The existing lookup has a provenance gap that matters once several lines reuse: it picks the newest successful run by head SHA, event and workflow path (`scripts/ci-reuse.py` near lines 116 to 144). It does not bind that run to the merged pull request's number, its base line and base commit, or the merge tree the run actually tested. Counterexample: head H contains line A's tip; a pull request for H into A lands with tree H; a newer successful run for the same H into line B tested merge(H, B), which holds changes absent from H; the lookup can pick that run and certify A's push. A retargeted pull request creates the same ambiguity, and a workflow file changed at the same path is not distinguished.
Once TSK-358 runs the gate jobs on ready pull requests into integration lines, the push that lands such a pull request runs the same jobs a second time on the same tree.

Outcome: a line push, and a `main` push, reuse a hosted verdict only from the run that tested exactly the merged pull request into exactly that destination, on the exact pushed tree, under the same workflow content and job contract; anything unproven runs the jobs.

The task starts with evidence: it first finds at least one real pair after TSK-358 lands (a ready pull request run and the landing push run on one tree) and records both runs and their timings. If no pair exists, because landings change the tree (for example a merge of a moved line), the task records that and closes without a change.
Decisions recorded here:

items.text: Extend `scripts/ci-reuse.py`; do not add a second mechanism. The stronger binding applies to `main` pushes as well as line pushes.

The pull request run records, in its own job output or artifact, the Git tree id of the merge it tested and the base commit it merged with. Reuse reads those from the run itself, never from text the pull request controls.
The secret scan, gitleaks canary, security review and CodeQL never reuse.

The required job set is read from the pushed workflow's verdict jobs, so jobs added later (for example by PR 224's hosted policy and native platform tasks) join the contract instead of being frozen out.

context: Non-goals: reusing local results as hosted evidence, changing the shipped template, and the cache-priming design. Product surface: this repository's CI only.

TSK-360.title: The repository contract states builder evidence and the hosted green landing rule
context: Source: the operator's request of 2026-10-17 to make the gates fast while the right checks run locally and in hosted CI, the decisions taken on it the same day, and the hosted-red diagnosis of 2026-10-17. Amended after the Codex review of PR 226 (finding F4 and a minor on the builder rule).
Two rules this repository works by are not written where builders and the primary read them:

items.text: **Builder evidence.** Builders no longer run routine whole essential or full gates. Their evidence is targeted tests plus the quick gate (the pre-push quick run counts for the same tree), as the managed block of `AGENTS.md` already states in its "build" row; one full gate runs on each landing candidate. Targeted checks that exist only in a heavier mode (`codeflow test --mode essential --only <target>` and the like, as `.codeflow/rules/workflow-discipline.md` already requires) and measurement trials a task authorizes stay allowed. The project section of `AGENTS.md` still asks for `codeflow test --mode essential` on every `crates/**` change.
**Hosted green before the next landing.** The line was red on hosted Linux and Windows from 2026-10-12 while later pull requests landed.

context: The hosted landing rule, as written by this task:

items.text: Ordinary landings on an integration line wait until the line's current tip has green `codeflow gates` and `windows` verdicts.

Recovery exception: while the tip is red or lacks evidence, the only landings allowed are the repair of the failure and work needed to produce the evidence (for example a workflow fix without which the jobs cannot run). After such a landing, ordinary landings still wait for green verdicts on the new tip.
Pending (a run still in progress) is not green: wait for it.
Cancelled, skipped (other than a reuse that names a green run, TSK-359), and missing (no run for the tip) are not green: start or rerun the run.
Stale (a green verdict for an earlier tip) is not evidence for the current tip.
A failure shown to come from runner infrastructure is rerun, never read as a pass; a failure shown to be unrelated to the next landing still blocks it until repaired, under the recovery exception.
Once TSK-358 lands, a pull request into a line also needs its own green `codeflow gates` and `windows` verdicts at the exact head that lands; TSK-358 updates that sentence when it lands.

context: The managed block between the codeflow markers is maintained by `codeflow update`, and the files under `.codeflow/rules/` are managed scaffold destinations, so both rules go in the project section of `AGENTS.md`, below the markers.

Authority: the operator decided on 2026-10-17 that hosted gates run on ready pull requests and that a line lands only on hosted green, from the request to make sure the right checks run locally and in CI. Protection: no landing without Linux and Windows evidence, and no landing on top of an unproven or failed hosted run. Cost: a check of the line's latest hosted run before each landing, and a wait while a run is in progress (about 31 minutes from run start to finish in the failed-run sample of 2026-10-17).
Non-goals: the managed block, shipped rules, and the shipped pipeline default (TSK-370). Product surface: this repository's contract only.

TSK-363.title: Policy keys with no reader are refused or warned, never documented as controls
context: Source: the Claude Fable 5.1 test integrity audit of 2026-10-17, finding F1, at `eaf2ed04e932186cdd26dc4a7e5740cc553acee3`.
Two shipped security policy keys are parsed, defaulted, shipped and documented as controls, and no code reads them:

items.text: `security.script_bypass` (default `warn`, `assets/base/policy.json:56`), described at `docs/policy-reference.md:82` as refusing actions found in a script a command runs. `crates/codeflow-core/src/security/privilege.rs:11` says TSK-172 reads it; TSK-172 is cancelled. The docs do not say it is unread.

`security.sandbox_retry` (default `allowlist`) and `security.sandbox_retry_allow` (`assets/base/policy.json:62`), described at `docs/policy-reference.md:88` and `:89`. The shipped entry carries literal placeholder digests (`"<sha256 at qualification>"`). The schema validates only `program` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/policy_schema.rs` near line 1333). TSK-174 is cancelled. `docs/policy-reference.md:598` discloses that these keys are not read yet.

context: An adopter who sets `block` gets nothing, on a security surface.

Decision (the primary's default, 2026-10-17): remove the claimed behaviour. The keys stop being documented as controls, a policy that still sets them gets a clear "not supported, has no effect" message naming the key, the shipped template and default policy drop them, and `codeflow update` migrates an adopter's managed copy. Implementing either control remains a separate future decision. A key that a project still carries must not break its hooks: the message warns, and `codeflow doctor` reports it; it never silently passes as a control.
A reader contract test makes this class of defect fail the build: every policy key the schema accepts and the reference documents has a module that reads it, or is listed as refused or unsupported.
Product surface: adopter-facing engine (policy load, schema, doctor), scaffold (`assets/base/policy.json`) and docs.

TSK-364.title: A substituted hook binary cannot pass a hook silently

next.reason: task TSK-364 depends on TSK-324, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Source: both test integrity audits of 2026-10-17 at `eaf2ed04e932186cdd26dc4a7e5740cc553acee3` (Codex medium finding on hook dispatch; Fable finding F2 and probes 1 and 3; Fable minor M6). Amended after the Codex review of PR 228 (finding R1) with the primary's decision of 2026-10-17.

Every installed git hook shim (`assets/base/git-hooks/*`, installed under `.codeflow/git-hooks/`) runs `CODEFLOW_HOOK_BINARY` when it names an executable file, checks only that it prints `hooks 3` to `git-hook capabilities`, and then takes its verdict (`pre-commit:7` to `:24`). An executable that prints that line and exits 0 disables the commit-time secret scan, the commit format check and the pre-push gate. The code calls the variable "a dispatch hint, not authentication" (`crates/codeflow-core/src/git/mod.rs:21`); tests cover only a missing or non-executable path (`crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli.rs:7256`). No test presents an impostor that answers the handshake. The secret scan is the gate that is never relaxed (`.codeflow/rules/git-rules.md`).

Two related local overrides are honoured without a record: `CODEFLOW_INTEGRATE_TOKEN` is accepted when non-empty (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/mod.rs:37`), and no test sets it empty, so weakening that check to "set" survives; and `CODEFLOW_HUMAN_OVERRIDE=1`. Neither use is written to the ledger.

Split with TSK-324 (EPC-022 since 2026-10-18): TSK-324 AC-5 makes the guard refuse an in-session assignment of `CODEFLOW_HOOK_BINARY` and a `PATH` that changes which `codeflow` resolves, and TSK-324 records the verified binary's digest under `~/.codeflow/versions/`. This task depends on TSK-324 and covers what happens when the variable is set anyway, from the launching environment.

Decision (the primary's, 2026-10-17): an impostor is refused, never admitted with reduced assurance. The shim dispatches only to a binary whose identity CodeFlow has established, for example the binary CodeFlow installed and recorded with its digest; a substituted binary that answers the handshake is refused through every entry point. A legitimate development binary (this repository's hook and policy tasks run the worktree's own build) is admitted only through an explicit trusted route that records its digest outside an agent session; the ADR names that route. No choice that relaxes the secret floor is left to the builder.

Outcome: the trust contract of a designated hook binary is written down, an impostor is refused at every entry point with the repository unchanged, a legitimate designated binary still works through the trusted route, and override and integrate-token use is visible.
Product surface: adopter-facing scaffold (the shims) and engine (hooks, ledger).

TSK-370.title: The shipped pipeline verifies each change with targeted checks and quick
context: Source: the operator's decision of 2026-10-17, during the gate efficiency amendment, to change the shipped adopter pipeline default to targeted checks plus the quick gate for each change, with one full gate per landing.

The shipped develop pipeline (`assets/base/claude/workflows/pipeline.workflow.js`, installed at `.claude/workflows/pipeline.workflow.js`) ends its final verification stage with `codeflow test --mode essential --strict` whenever a target defines an essential mode, else `codeflow test --mode quick --strict` (near line 252). `cf-develop` and the managed `AGENTS.md` "build" row already say a builder cites targeted tests and the quick gate and the full gate runs once on the landing candidate, so the shipped pipeline contradicts the shipped method.

Ownership stays as it is (the primary's decision of 2026-10-17, after the Codex confirmation review of PR 226, finding F7): the pipeline is user-owned (`assets/base/scaffold-manifest.toml`, `ownership = "user-owned"`), seeded once and never rewritten by `codeflow update` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/update.rs`, the user-owned branch). Fresh installs get the new default. Existing copies, this repository's included, are never rewritten; the release note and the `codeflow update` output tell adopters the exact one-line edit that adopts the new default, and `codeflow doctor` reports when an installed pipeline still runs essential per change. There is no ownership migration.

Outcome: a freshly installed pipeline's verification stage runs the affected targeted checks (including a heavy-mode check through `--only` where a check exists only in that mode) and `codeflow test --mode quick --strict`, and states that the primary runs one full gate on the landing candidate; an adopter with an existing copy is told the one-line edit and `codeflow doctor` reports the old default; this repository's own copy gets that edit by hand in this task.

Kept as it is: `--strict` (a NoTargets run is not verification) and the rule that any nonzero exit is `changes_requested`. Product surface: adopter-facing scaffold (CAP-010 duo orchestration and the user-owned workflow) and engine (the update notice and the doctor check).

TSK-378.title: The guards judge every script interpreter the way they judge python and node
context: Source: the security review of PR 239 (TSK-373) on 2026-10-18, marked "must fix before 3.2.0 ships". Severity high. It is unreleased TSK-302 work, so 4.0.0 would otherwise ship the gap.

The interpreter family list (`crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs:1220-1236`, `interpreter_family`) knows only `python`, `node`, `nodejs`, `perl` and `ruby`. A script run through another launcher passes both guards with an enforcement path as its argument:

items.text: `deno run -A tool.ts .claude/settings.json`
`bun tool.ts .claude/settings.json`
`npx tsx tool.ts .claude/settings.json`
`uv run tool.py .worktrees/w/.git`

context: `uv run python tool.py ...` is already refused, because the guard reaches `python`. The fix either adds these families (`deno`, `bun`, `tsx` and `ts-node` through `npx` and `pnpm dlx`, `uv run` and `uvx` with a script operand), or treats an unknown program followed by a script-like operand as an interpreter. The builder chooses and records the reason; the outcome is the same either way.
Outcome: **a script run through deno, bun, tsx or uv gets the same verdict as the same script run through python or node.**
Non-goal: modelling what each runtime's script does; the guard judges the operands, as it does for python and node.
Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

Widened on 2026-10-20 (EPC-022 amendment) by the primary under the operator's rule that every security gap belongs in 3.2.0, with finding P-2 of the `cf-security-reviewer` round 1 review of PR 264 (TSK-380) at `c03b082dc`, severity high, likely, pre-existing on base and head (`.worktrees/tsk-380/target/review-TSK-380-security-01.md`). GNU `parallel` runs the Perl inside a `{= perl =}` replacement string for each input, so a template word is interpreter code the guards never judge: `parallel foo '{= system("touch ".$ENV{HOME}."/.zs"."hrc") =}' ::: x` passes exec-guard on both binaries, and the same shape can name an enforcement path in a `system` or `open` call the template builds at run time. Today the guards read the commands `parallel` builds from its template and `:::` inputs (`docs/policy-reference.md`, the closed rule; `crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:4980`, `parallel_violation`, and `crates/codeflow-core/src/security/unresolved.rs:872`), and a template word in braces is read as a replacement string, never as Perl. The widening: a `{= ... =}` replacement string (a `--rpl` defined replacement string holding Perl, and the `--plus` forms, included) is judged as `perl -e` code in addition to every check the line already gets: no existing refusal is removed, and no line refused today is allowed. So exec-guard, which judges `perl -e 'open(F, ">", ".claude/settings.json")'` as `git.hook_integrity` and `perl -e 'system("touch $ENV{HOME}/.zshrc")'` as `security.shell_startup` today, refuses the same text inside a replacement string for the same reason; git-guard keeps every refusal it gives those lines today (it names `.claude/settings.json` on the line, and reads a `{= =}` string as a glob it will not inspect past 4096 entries), and `perl -e` verdicts stay as they are on both hooks. Grok 4.7's round 3 review of PR 268 judged every line on the tree at `d55b752ad` (`target/review-PR268-grok-03.md`, the seven-row table) and is the base for the evidence below. Before the Perl judgment can be the verdict the test sees, the deletion reader has to model `--plus` and `--rpl` as input options (`crates/codeflow-core/src/security/deletion.rs:4404`, `input_options_unproven`, from `judge_parallel` at `:4430`), which today refuse any `parallel --plus` or `--rpl` line on exec-guard as an unmodelled option under `security.dangerous_commands`. A replacement string the guard cannot read refuses as cannot-verify, naming it, on a line that names a protected path or where one is reachable. The P-2 line itself builds its path from pieces at run time (`$ENV{HOME}."/.zs"."hrc"`) and names no protected target on the line: that is the existing piece-assembly residual (`docs/policy-reference.md`, "Every harness": a path assembled by a program from pieces is kept as an allowed regression; the operator decision of 2026-10-15), which `perl -e` of the same text is allowed under today, and this widening does not narrow it: the P-2 parallel line stays allowed on exec-guard and stays refused by git-guard's current glob reading of the `{= =}` string, and `perl -e` of the piece text stays allowed on both hooks. What the widening closes is that the replacement string was not judged at all. `parallel` was not installed on the reviewer's host, so the behaviour was read from the GNU parallel manual and its `{= =}` documentation, and the builder confirms it with GNU parallel in a scratch fixture before the tests are written.

TSK-379.title: Repository and worktree discovery cannot unprotect enforcement files
context: Sources: SEC-377-5 from the security confirm of PR 246 (TSK-377) on 2026-10-18, and Grok's review of PR 246 at `a3de25c80`, findings F2, F3 and F6 (`.worktrees/fix-hosted-red-5/target/review-TSK-377-grok-01.md` in the codeflow checkout, outside the repository). Severity high. All are pre-existing on 3.1.x. PR 246 cites this task as their owner.

Protection follows the repository the guards discover from the working directory, not the repository that holds the target. Four ways to move or hide that discovery make another checkout's enforcement files writable:

items.text: **Nested repository or non-repository cwd (SEC-377-5, F6).** After `git init sub`, with the cwd in `sub`, `printf x > ../.claude/settings.json` passes git-guard, and native writes of `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` and `<repo>/.git/hooks/pre-commit` pass edit-guard (`crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/edit_guard.rs:241-290`). A submodule gitfile cwd does the same. From a directory outside any repository the Write and the interpreter argument also pass.

**`core.worktree` (F2).** `git config core.worktree <decoy>`, or the same through `--file .git/config`, is allowed by both guards. `core.worktree` is not in `SAFE_CONFIG` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/security/git.rs:46-101`), and a local write with no file resolver drops the finding (`crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:8516-8532`, `:9060-9092`). Afterwards both checkouts' enforcement files are writable.

**`mv` then `git worktree prune` (F3).** A plain `mv` of a registered worktree directory followed by `git worktree prune` unregisters a live checkout, and its `.claude/settings.json` becomes writable from the main checkout.

**Registration that disagrees with its checkout.** When a worktree is moved by hand, every guard fails closed and `git worktree repair` is refused under hook integrity. The remedy text does not name the person's route (`git worktree repair` run outside the harness). Folded here from the Fable confirm of PR 246, because this task changes the same messages.

context: Outcome: **an enforcement file of any repository that encloses the target, or of the session's project, is refused whatever directory the command starts in, and no git or shell command can move, hide or unregister a checkout to drop that protection.**

Reach, defined once here: a target is judged against every repository that encloses it (its work tree; for a linked worktree, also its common directory and main checkout) and against the session's project repository with its registered worktrees. So an absolute-path write into another repository's enforcement files, from inside this repository or from outside any, is refused the same way as a write into this one. Refuse writes of `core.worktree` (and the other keys that move a work tree) under `git.hook_integrity`. Refuse a shell move of a registered worktree directory. Protect every directory under the configured worktree locations whose `.git` gitfile names this repository's git directory, registered or not, so a checkout hidden by a move and a prune is still protected when it returns. The guard decides from on-disk state only, never from a memory of earlier commands.

Non-goal: a path that no repository encloses, other than the session project's files; the harness settings folders in the home directory are TSK-395. TSK-396 was cancelled on 2026-10-18 because this definition covers its case.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision). The coordinator widened SEC-377-5 into this task on 2026-10-18.

TSK-380.title: A search pattern given to rg or grep is never read as a write target
context: Issue: #242. A read-only search is refused as a shell-startup write. `rg --files | rg '/CHANGELOG.md$'` gets "`rg` takes `/CHANGELOG.md$`, which the guard cannot resolve, and its directory is `/`" under `security.shell_startup` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/security/startup.rs:2740-2750`). The argument is a search pattern, and the command writes nothing. The adopter's workaround is to avoid searching. The same reading applies to `grep` patterns.
Outcome: **a search tool's pattern argument is never read as a path it writes, and a read-only search is never classed as a shell-startup write.**

The pattern operand is the first operand of `rg`, `grep`, `egrep`, `fgrep`, `git grep` and `ag` when no `-e`, `-f` or `--regexp` supplies it, and every `-e` or `--regexp` value. Paths those tools write stay judged: `rg --pre <program>`, `grep` has none, and an output redirect is judged as any redirect.
Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

TSK-381.title: A pinned research input stays satisfied after its producer's line is deleted
context: Issue: #236. A task with a pinned research input cannot be claimed once the producer's integration branch is deleted after landing. `work claim` and `work next` report "depends on TSK-104 on 'integration/EPC-002-carry', which is not fetched here: unknown, not satisfied" (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:109`), although the producer is complete and the pin is an ancestor of both the consumer's target and `origin/main`. The adopter's workaround repoints the producer records' `integration_target` to `main`. The issue's comment adds a second defect: readiness reads the local `main`, so a pin on `origin/main` fails until the local branch is fast-forwarded (`work_start.rs:2591`, "not on 'main'").

Outcome: **a pinned research or decision input stays satisfied after its producer's line is deleted, when the pin holds the producer's completed record and is an ancestor of a verified target that still exists, and readiness reads remote-tracking refs, never a local branch that may be behind.**

Identity, completion and the other claim checks stay. A missing object or an unproven landing still fails closed. TSK-341 owns stacked predecessor pins (`kind` absent); this task owns research and decision pins.
Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

TSK-382.title: An amendment note under a criterion keeps its closing journey tag
context: Issue: #199. R-50 counts a `(journey)` tag only where it opens or closes a criterion. CodeFlow's own amendment practice adds an indented sub-bullet under a criterion ("- Amended <date> ..."). The checker reads the sub-bullet as part of the criterion, so a criterion whose head line ends with `(journey)` stops counting once amended (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:2190-2210`). The effect spreads: `work.journey_criterion` then blocks every adopter-facing task, including one that serves the epic's journey criterion. The workaround is to move the tag to the start. This repository deferred the issue on 2026-10-17; the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18 brings it into 3.2.0 because it blocks work.

Outcome: **an amendment note (a dash sub-bullet whose first word is exactly `Amended` or `Moved` and whose next word is a `YYYY-MM-DD` date) and its wrapped continuation are left out of tag reading, while every other sub-bullet stays criterion text, so a closing tag on the head line counts, and a refusal names the hiding sub-bullet or note when a tag is still unreadable.**

The rule must keep substantive continuation lines of a criterion (wrapped text) part of the criterion, and keep direct and served journey semantics unchanged. The `serves` and `(after release)` tags follow the same rule.
Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

TSK-383.title: Remote protect changes only the rules it owns, and doctor reads the live rules
context: Issue: #200. `codeflow remote protect` updates in place "every active repository ruleset that already targets a branch" (`crates/codeflow-core/src/remote.rs:15`, `:343`). In a repository that splits `main`'s rules across rulesets with different bypass lists, that run would add rules to each and change the intended separation. The dry run also plans protection for `master` when the policy lists it and no such branch exists. `codeflow doctor` warns that no host rules are recorded for `codeflow/registry` although an active ruleset already blocks force pushes and deletion there, because it reads the recorded receipt, not the live rules. The adopter's workaround is to accept the warning and never run the command. Deferred on 2026-10-17; the operator's rule of 2026-10-18 brings it into 3.2.0.

Outcome: **`remote protect` changes only rulesets it created or one the operator names, plans nothing for an absent branch, and `doctor` accepts live rules that already give the required protection.**
Constraints carried from the 2026-10-17 deferral: the preview is exact, and unrelated protections and bypass lists are preserved.
Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

TSK-384.title: A project can run a gate target in its own split job without weakening the gate
context: Issue: #203. The managed gates job in `assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml` runs `codeflow test --strict` over every target in `.codeflow/test-config.json`. A project cannot keep a target out of that job, so a target that needs its own runner shape (the reporter's browser target, sharded in its own workflow with `codeflow test --only`) makes the managed job fail or time out. The only route inside the project is to edit the managed workflow, which `codeflow update` overwrites. Deferred on 2026-10-17; the operator's rule of 2026-10-18 brings it into 3.2.0 because it forces an adopter workaround.

Outcome: **a project can declare that a target runs in its own CI job; the managed job leaves it out, and the gate counts as complete only when a green, current run of that target from the split jobs is present.**

Constraints carried from the 2026-10-17 deferral: every shard binds to the same revision and configuration; missing, failed or stale evidence is refused; required checks are kept; globally disabling the target is not a green result. `ci_skip` keeps its current meaning.
The edge to TSK-355 is real: split-job evidence is recorded target execution evidence, which TSK-355 defines and reuses.
Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

Widened 2026-10-27 for issue #352, item 3 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). An adopter's managed gate job ran five targets in series on the 2-vCPU `ubuntu-24.04` runner in 23 min 54 s; running two targets at once in one job starved the CPU and one hit its 900 s limit. The adopter split the gate into a matrix of shards, each `codeflow test --strict --only <targets>` on its own runner, with one aggregate job keeping the required `codeflow gates` name and a unit test against shard drift, and measured 10 min 26 s. This task's outcome (a target runs in its own job and the gate is complete only with every split result green and current) already covers it; AC-5 and AC-6 ask the managed workflow to generate the shards from the test config, so the list cannot drift. The issue's items 1 and 2 (cancel superseded runs, skip a proven repeat) are TSK-1026.

TSK-385.title: The quick gate runs the cheap repository-wide contract checks
context: Source: landing candidates 12 and 14 on 2026-10-18 (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 morning and midday). Builders now cite targeted tests and the quick gate (AC-57, TSK-360), but quick does not run the cheap repository-wide contract tests. Three landing candidates failed on them alone: PR 206 and PR 222 pushed `docs/cli.md`, and PR 222 `docs/capabilities.md`, over the Technical word budget (`guide_altitude_budget`); PR 237 added a remedy catalogue row with no `remedy_clearing` entry; candidate 14 failed `name_decode_scan` on TSK-375's new `trim()`. Each runs in seconds. Today quick holds only `contract-scans` (`git_spawn_contract`, `artifact_budget_contract`) and `repository-update-noop` (`.codeflow/test-config.json`).
Outcome: **a unit that fails a cheap repository-wide contract check is stopped at the builder's quick gate and pre-push, not at the landing candidate.**

Scope: every integration test file under `crates/codeflow-core/tests/` that scans the whole repository or its records and runs in a few seconds (including `name_decode_scan`, `manifest_consistency`, `guide_altitude_budget`, `policy_key_placement`, `pipe_drain_rule`, `stdin_pipe_rule`, `history_read_scan`, `rule_map_contract`), the `remedy_clearing` catalogue check and the derived lookups (`docs/cli.md` command table and similar). The selection rule is recorded before any scan is excluded: a whole-repository scan joins quick when its median of three runs on the reference host is under 15 seconds; the builder measures each, lists the chosen set with its timings, and states each one left out with its reason. The three replays in AC-2 hold whatever the rule selects. The set is selected by a rule (a whole-repository scan under a time bound), so a new scan joins without a hand edit where the harness allows.
Not adopter-facing: this repository's gate config and contract only.
Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

TSK-386.title: Shipped CI scripts and the test harness remove their temporary directories
context: Source: found while landing PR 235 (TSK-371) on 2026-10-17 (workspace `RELEASE-PLAN.md`, 2026-10-17 late). The shipped CI scripts create temporary directories and never remove them: `assets/base/ci/ci-generic.sh:139`, `:178`, `:186`, `:196`; the GitLab template `.gitlab-ci.yml:182`; the Bitbucket template `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:177`, `:216`, `:224`, `:234`; and `assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml:128`, `:291` and `codeflow-policy.yml:149`. This repository's own `ci_pin_platforms` tests run these scripts and left 61,216 `tmp.*` folders (about 4,800 a day) in the macOS user temp directory, which made the macOS guard case lookup slow enough to stretch guard suites past 30 minutes.

Outcome: **every shipped CI script removes every temporary directory it creates on success, failure and interruption, and this repository's tests run them under a private temporary directory they remove.**

TSK-387.title: The managed map and autonomy guidance cover multi-session coordination
context: Issues: #223 and #225, two field reports from one adopter that ran a coordinator, six lanes and many Codex and Grok seats on one machine for a day. In each case CodeFlow already had the guidance, or nearly, but the managed `AGENTS.md` map or `cf-method` autonomy guidance never pointed a session at it, so the operator repeated it in chat.
From #223 (the map):

items.text: seat tabs: the cleanup row covers branches, build output and worktrees, not Herdr seat tabs (`cf-herdr` "Cleanup" has the rule);
standing operator rules: no row says where a rule the operator gives in chat is recorded (`standing_reviews` in `.codeflow/model-selection.json`, policy or a config key, else one project line);
standing reviews: the review and PR rows do not name the reviews `codeflow models resolve` owes for the touched areas;
pre-handoff checks: the status row does not say to check live state (remote ref, PR, checks) before handing the operator a command.

context: From #225 (autonomy guidance):

items.text: a peer seat's command prompt inside its brief's scope is the host's to answer and record; anything outside goes to the operator;

a classifier refusal with no stated rule of an in-scope verification command is distinct from a policy guard that names the operator; the sanctioned next step is stated, including a host-run route the operator turns on once in config;

message budgets: batch one digest per lane rather than stall on a count;
a stuck-lane sweep before each status report.

context: Outcome: **a session in an adopting project finds, from the managed map and the autonomy guidance, what to do in each of these multi-session cases without the operator repeating it.**

TSK-392.title: The macOS case lookup stays fast in a crowded directory
context: Source: found while landing PR 235 (2026-10-17). The macOS case normalizer (`edit_guard::normalize_case`) reads the parent directory listing for every path component, so a crowded temp directory made the interpreter suite take 2025 seconds. TSK-386 removes the leak that crowded it; a guard that slows with directory size remains a cost for adopters with large directories.
Outcome: **a case-insensitive path lookup on macOS costs about the same in a directory of 50,000 entries as in one of 50.**

Measurement basis, fixed before implementation: the reference host is a macOS arm64 workstation of this repository's workspace; the workload is 1,000 lookups of a three-component path whose last parent holds 50 entries, then 50,000 entries; the threshold is a median 50,000-entry lookup no more than twice the 50-entry median. TSK-386 removes the leak that crowded the temp directory; this task first measures the residual after TSK-386 on that workload, and the result decides whether code changes.

TSK-397.title: The exec guard adds a strict rule where the sandbox is absent or loosened
TSK-397.about: After this merges, the strict text rule applies in every session by default, and an operator can choose the line's rule for a project by landing `security.text_guard: relaxed` on its protected refs. No command the line refuses is allowed, except a line made only of bare `cd`, `pushd` and `popd` builtins under relaxed, which writes nothing. The change is breaking (4.0.0): `codeflow doctor --check sandbox` shows the rule in force.
context: Source: PR 239 (TSK-373) final confirm, 2026-10-18. `cd src && python3 tool.py ..` from the checkout root is refused, because the guard's directory set keeps the starting directory after a `cd` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs`, `DirSet::change`).
History of the outcome:

items.text: 2026-10-25 (operator): narrowing after `cd` cannot be made sound against shell state the guard cannot see, so `cd src && python3 tool.py ..` stays refused. The PR 331 reviews found 14 text-bypass classes.
2026-10-27 (operator, option D): every stop in launcher traversal keeps its words judged, with a non-executing allowlist.

2026-10-28 (operator, narrowed option (c)): the allowlist and its shadowing analysis are removed. The text guard has two outcomes, selected from the harness configuration the host can read. The specification is design note D revision 4.1, Part A (`target/tsk-397-design-D.md` in the TSK-397 worktree; checks: Codex 01 to 03, Fable 01 to 04).

2026-10-29 (operator, option 2): selecting the outcome from the harness configuration is removed. A trigger list (rounds 15 to 16) and then an attestation (rounds 17 to 18) each missed a layer or key that let a weaker configuration select the relaxed rule, so the feature could not be made sound. The strict rule is the default; the relaxed rule is the operator's choice in landed policy.

context: The two outcomes:

items.text: **Strict**, the default, adds the strict branch, PR 331's rule with every name-based exemption removed. It applies to every call unless the operator chose relaxed.

**Relaxed** is the line's rule. It applies when `security.text_guard` is `relaxed` in every policy the hook reads at the remote-tracking refs as last fetched: the call's repository (its remote's default branch, the one policy authority since TSK-1077) and, for a Claude Code call, the session's project. A working copy, a local branch or tag, a remote `HEAD` outside the remote, a ref file that is a symbolic link and a repository without a remote stay strict. The guard verifies no sandbox under relaxed. A recognized marked retry (`dangerouslyDisableSandbox`), and every call on native Windows, stay strict under relaxed.
The strict rule's own refusals always block, under `security.text_guard`; `git.hook_integrity` sets the level of the line's findings only (security review round 1, SEC01-1).

context: Doctor and the hook decide through the same function (`sandbox_state::reasons`). Doctor prints `text rule: strict` with its reason, or `text rule: relaxed by operator choice, not verified` with the ref it was read from. `codeflow init` and `codeflow update` never write the key.

The strict outcome keeps every relaxed finding. Neither outcome allows what the line refuses, except the H-3 class below, which relaxed allows and strict refuses. A replay of the historical corpus is the test.
Hardening in both outcomes:

items.text: a NUL byte refuses (H-1);
the headless `xargs` reader no longer guesses a bare optional-value option or a BSD option (H-2);
a line made only of bare `cd`, `pushd` and `popd` builtins no longer takes the startup write judgement (H-3, issue 342);
the enforcement paths are explicit `sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite` entries in the presets (H-4);
`~/.codeflow/authority/` is a protected directory, reserved for the 4.1.0 qualification records (H-5).

context: `codeflow doctor --check sandbox` names the rule in force and why (H-6). Non-goals for 4.0.0: qualification, receipts, capability relaxation and the other Part C units, which are planned for 4.1.0.
Limits, each as it is on the line today unless noted:

items.text: An unread program (a script file, code the guard does not read) can write an enforcement file or read a secret wherever no kernel deny holds. The strict branch narrows the text-visible paths and contains nothing.

Under relaxed, the guard trusts the OS sandbox the project configures and does not check it. An unsandboxed retry the harness does not mark (a Codex seat has no field) follows the relaxed rule; TSK-1052 fails closed there for a command that runs code after a same-line write (EPC-022, filed by PR 390).
Doctor's state-root check reads Claude write grants only; Codex and Grok grants are not computed, and doctor does not claim the state root is unwritable.
An `awk` inline program that writes an enforcement path passes the exec guard (git-guard refuses it); it is the unread-program residual above, to be tracked once.
Debug builds honour `CODEFLOW_TEST_CLAUDE_MANAGED_DIR`, which moves the managed settings layer doctor reads; release builds ignore it.
The `Monitor` tool is outside the hook matcher (4.1.0, TSK-1058).

Policy authority under `refs/remotes/origin/*` and `packed-refs` is writable by a direct file write (4.1.0, TSK-1057). A relaxed value written there by a session, or a stale relaxed ref before the next fetch, would be read as landed; the same gap applies to every policy key. Security review round 1 (SEC01-2) narrowed the read to plain refs inside the remote's namespace with no symbolic-link ref files; it does not authenticate them.

A file a repository configuration `include` names is read by libgit2 with a blocking read and is not checked. A fifo named only by an include stalls that read until the guard's own deadline (TSK-1082, merged from the line on 2026-10-30) refuses with exit 2 after 20 seconds; the stall never allows the command (`docs/policy-reference.md`, repository discovery). The repository's own `config` and `config.worktree` files, the policy and the project settings are checked first (SEC01-3).
Neither rule sees the environment a command inherits (`PATH`, `HOME`, Codex's `shell_environment_policy`, secret-bearing variables); Fable F3-1's attestation finding is moot, this residual is not.
In a linked worktree, protection of the shared `.git`'s `hooks`, `config` and `config.worktree` is unverified (4.1.0, TSK-1054).

TSK-400.title: An opt-in infrastructure preset refuses commands that change live cloud state
context: Issue: #171, its defect portion. exec-guard has no way to refuse commands that change live cloud state: `terraform apply`, `tofu apply`, mutating `gcloud` verbs, `kubectl` writes and `flux` pass at `security.outward_actions: block`, because `crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs` knows only the shipped families. The adopter's workaround is its own deny rules in the Claude permission preset and Codex command rules, to be removed once a release refuses these commands.

This task ships the opt-in infrastructure preset that TSK-320 first planned (operator decision 5 of 2026-10-13): `security.project_action_presets: ["infrastructure"]`, off by default. When on, it refuses exactly decision 5's forms, as recorded in TSK-320's description: `tofu` and `terraform` `apply`, `destroy`, `import`, `state rm`, `state mv`, `force-unlock`, `taint`, `untaint`; `gcloud` verbs `create`, `delete`, `update`, `deploy`, `set-iam-policy`, `add-iam-policy-binding`, `remove-iam-policy-binding`, `enable`, `disable`; `kubectl` `apply`, `create`, `delete`, `patch`, `replace`, `scale`, `edit`, `rollout`, `drain`, `cordon`, `taint`; `flux` as a whole program; `helm` `install`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`, `rollback`; `pulumi` `up`, `destroy`, `import`, `refresh`. They are refused at the `outward_actions` level, through the shipped unwrapping, and `update` reports a changed preset.

The preset is a list-valued security key, so it must survive policy composition. Today `crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/landed_policy.rs` starts from the default branch's policy (`:77`) and folds in each declared integration target through `stricter` (`:108`), which composes levels and level-like enums (`:342`) and unions only `git.protected_branches` (`:360`). A main policy with the preset off would erase an integration target's opt-in. This task adds a bounded union for `security.project_action_presets` in that function, across every default-branch candidate and declared target, so any applicable landed authority that turns the preset on keeps it on. It does not wait for TSK-322's typed composition API and adds no edge to it. If TSK-322 is already on the integration line when this task lands, this task routes the preset union through that typed API; otherwise TSK-322 does so when it lands. In both cases the later task reruns this task's AC-5 against the combined implementation and cites the result in its PR.
Project-declared commands (`project_actions`) remain TSK-320 in EPC-023 (4.1.0), which now depends on this task and adds its declarations beside the preset.
Outcome: **an adopter that turns on the infrastructure preset has these commands refused by CodeFlow and can drop its own deny rules.**

context: Issue: #169, its defect portions. Two adopter workarounds:

items.text: A carry of one landed, reviewed task change to another integration line has no checked route. A carry pull request fails `work.stable_planning_anchor` because the task's record lives on its home line (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1466-1530`), so the adopter lands carries by a gated merge outside every check.

The cleanup rule deletes a pushed branch only when its PR is `MERGED` and the tip equals the PR's recorded head (`assets/base/rules/worktrees.md:93-110`). A branch whose content landed by ancestry, with no merged PR (a carry merged into its destination line, or a closed PR whose head is an ancestor of `main`), can never be deleted.

context: This task gives both a checked route that exists today. A carry is a merge of the task's reviewed head (or its home line) into the other line, which `codeflow integrate --no-ff` (TSK-293) can make; `codeflow ci` judges it by the source task's binding, which TSK-339 establishes for imported completions. The proof is recorded in the cleanup step. Patch equivalence (`git cherry`) is never a deletion proof: it compares diffs with whitespace and line numbers removed, so a patch-equivalent lead is evidence to investigate, as TSK-319's rule already states.
The one-commit carry class with byte comparison (TSK-318), and the remote branch inventory with compare-and-swap deletion (TSK-319), stay in EPC-023 (4.1.0); both now depend on this task.

TSK-405.title: A resolved update conflict does not come back on the next update
context: Issue: #74, its comment of 2026-10-13 only. When `codeflow update` hits a conflict in a managed file the project customised, it writes `<file>.new` and a report note, but keeps the old shipped baseline and manifest hash (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/update.rs:818`, the `ManagedStep::Conflict` arm; the clean-merge arm at `:809` records the new shipped hash and baseline). The adopter's workaround is to re-resolve the same conflict on every update; a project that customises its CI workflow hits it every release.

The Codex review of PR 249 reproduced it with this worktree's binary (`target/review-PR249-update-conflict-02.txt` in the planning worktree): after a simulated resolution the second update exits 2 and recreates the same conflict. In a control, setting only the existing baseline and manifest hash to the pristine candidate, with the person's file kept, made the next update exit 0 and keep the project's change, with no format change.

Outcome: **a person's accepted resolution of an update conflict is recorded against the correct shipped base, so the same conflict does not return on the next update and later upstream changes still merge.**

Invariant: the baseline and manifest hash keep describing shipped content, never the person's merged file. The existing formats stay. The baseline replacement and `codeflow update --plan` stay in 4.0.0 and carry this regression test forward.

The builder chooses how the resolution is recorded (for example, the conflict arm writes the new shipped baseline beside the `.new` and records the resolution as pending, and the next update accepts it only when the `.new` is gone and the file holds no conflict markers; or an explicit resolve step) and records why.
