TSK-452.title: Review cadence and guidance state each rule once
context: Guidance repeats work and repeats itself. Every review round rereads the whole unit "not only the delta" (`findings.md:64-66`), a security change can get five or six passes over one diff (`cf-security-reviewer.md:12-34`), cf-reviewer is mandatory in one file and optional in another (`cf-develop` step 4b, `workflow-discipline.md:265`, `cf-model-orchestrator` SKILL.md:381-383, `cf-reviewer.md:138-139`), rounds 6 and 7 found sibling cases one at a time, the routed required reading is about 150 KB, batch landing is stated in four files and the plain-writing rule in eight. Source: the operator approved process audit of 2026-10-23, including the operator's decision of that day on the security review stack (line numbers at `c9993bcf3`).

Scope: (1) Review cadence at four stages: plan settlement (epics only), PR ready, landing candidate (hand-resolved hunks only), epic close. Between stages the finder confirms a fix on the delta plus the affected tests; one final holistic pass on the final substantive revision precedes approval. (2) The builder's sibling sweep, with file:line per site, precedes the first review on a class fix; a reviewer who finds a sibling returns the unit to the sweep. (3) Security: the one other-lineage whole-unit review runs with the security checklist as the attacker lens; the Claude side triages scanner output inside its integrated judgment; cf-reviewer runs only when no other-lineage seat exists, stated once; the "high complexity" and "material depth" triggers for an extra family are dropped from `routing-policy.json`, the security and irreversible triggers stay. (4) Only material findings block; nits get a disposition. (5) Estimates come from planned throughput (`cf-estimate`, "Durations"). (6) Lane and queue rules: lanes sized from host memory and CPU, cheap targeted checks run freely while heavy work takes TSK-331's admission, and only the primary runs the full gate. (7) Research, review and consult work gets no durable record unless it produces a durable artifact; the evidence ledger text goes; one findings record linked from the PR (resolving the conflict between `completion.md` and `pr-evidence.md`). (8) Dedupe: batch landing in one home (cf-method "Managing a body of work"), the plain-writing rule once in `.codeflow/rules/writing.md`, the delivery flow once, one editorial-review trigger, cf-present loads specimens on demand, and the orchestrator preflight is printed by `codeflow doctor` (configured versus observed values, with unavailable evidence reported) and read, with the live observation still made.

(9) Planned work is delivered at speed (operator direction of 2026-10-23). Exploration, research and planning stay deliberate; once work is planned into an epic and tasks with criteria, builders execute without re-planning, re-litigating settled decisions or confirmation work for its own sake. Throughput expectation, set by the operator as an explicit decision of 2026-10-23 (which satisfies "Only the operator adds process"): each build lane delivers at least one planned task to ready-for-review per hour, preferably two. Quality is not traded: criteria, the tests that prove them and real security stay. Speed practices: targeted tests in the worktree, the quick gate once before ready, no local full gate, one push at ready, no reruns on an unchanged tree, lean PR bodies carrying criteria with file:line and test evidence, any stop over 15 minutes reported at once, reversible choices decided by the builder. TSK-1014.title: Coverage defaults apply to targets that set no rules of their own
context: Issue #299, its defect half. The shipped test-config schema says `defaults.coverage` holds "Default coverage rules applied when targets omit them" (`assets/base/testing/test-config.schema.json`, `defaults`), but the engine never applies them: `crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/config/mod.rs` reads `defaults.coverage` only for its glob check, and `collect_coverage_reports` in `crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/gate.rs` skips a target with no coverage configuration and judges a target's own rules only. A project that writes its floor once in `defaults.coverage`, as the schema invites, gets no floor at all and must copy the rules into every target, a workaround the release rule of 2026-10-18 places in 3.2.0. Codex's review of PR 343 separated this from the issue's feature half (a mandatory 80 floor with recorded exemptions), which stays TSK-1006 in EPC-024.

Outcome: **the rules a project writes in `defaults.coverage` are applied to every target that collects coverage and sets no rules of its own, and a test target that cannot be covered by them (no coverage producer) is named in the gate output rather than passing silently.**
Rules:

items.text: Defaults carry rules only, not a producer (format, artifact, the mode command that writes it). A target with a `coverage` block and no rules inherits the default rules; a target's own non-empty rules replace them, as "applied when targets omit them" says.

A target with no `coverage` block while `defaults.coverage` is non-empty gets a warning naming the target and the missing producer; it is not failed, since no floor applied to it before and the mandatory floor is TSK-1006's decision.
The inherited rules are enforcing exactly as a target's own rules are: a missing artifact fails the gate.
No minimum is imposed and no default value changes; the schema text is kept and now true.

TSK-1024.title: git-guard allows read-only git commands it cannot place
context: Issue #357 and its comment (CodeFlow 3.1.1). git-guard refuses read-only git commands in common shapes, so agents split or rewrite harmless inspection lines, and the guard's own advice (`cd /path/to/repo && git …`) is a form it then refuses.
Rechecked on 2026-10-27 through `codeflow hook git-guard --contract 3` with the 3.2.0 binary built at TSK-397's head `caf728c70`, payload cwd a worktree of this repository:

head: Issue case
Result on 3.2.0
rows: 2 and 2b: `cd <repo> && git remote -v | head -2`, the same with `git worktree list`
still refused, `git.policy_authority`, "a directory change on a line the guard does not model", after a note advising `cd /path/to/repo && git …`
allowed with the "judged it as a protected branch" note
allowed with a note: no longer reproduces
comment: `gh issue comment … --body "… git remote show …"`

context: Causes, read on the line tip `7172229aa`:

items.text: Case 1: `discard_intent` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:20146`) expands every operand with `expand_word` before it parses options; a glob fails there (`crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_target.rs:244`), although the `branch` arm (`git_guard.rs:20268`) treats only a forced delete as a discard.

Cases 2 and the comment: on a line `flat_top_level` does not model (a pipe, `||`, a group), `moves_for` (`git_guard.rs:8561-8569`) makes every git command's directory unknown when the line changes directory, and an unknown target is allowed only for the subcommands of `discard_readonly_git` (`git_guard.rs:20466`): `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `rev-parse`, `ls-files`, `ls-tree`, `merge-base`, `for-each-ref`, `show-ref`, `cat-file`, `check-ignore`, `help` and `version`.

context: Outcome: **a git command that cannot change refs, the index, the work tree, configuration, hooks or a remote is allowed with a note wherever git-guard cannot place it, and a refusal's advice names a form the guard accepts.**
Design, fixed here:

items.text: The guard does not start modeling `cd`. The operator decided on 2026-10-25 (TSK-397's amendment) that narrowing directories cannot be made sound against shell state the guard cannot see; the issue's suggestions 3 and 4 (model a leading `cd`, model paths created earlier on the line) are therefore not taken. An unknown directory stays unknown; what changes is which commands are safe there.

One read-only classifier replaces `discard_readonly_git`. It decides from the subcommand and its parsed options, not from the subcommand name alone, and serves the unresolved-target block in `check_git`, `may_change_discard_state`, an early exit in `discard_intent` and `check_discard`, so discard intent is decided before any operand is expanded, and `check_authority` (`git_guard.rs:8635`, run first for every git command from `check_git` at `:8722`). There, a command whose `-C` target is a worktree created earlier on the same line takes its source's authority only for `status` (`:8674`), so `git -C <new> log -1` still loads policy from a directory that does not exist yet and is refused (`:8679-8685`). The classifier replaces that `status`-only test; a mutation still needs a readable target and every branch check.

Read-only forms it accepts: the current list; `branch` with only listing options (`--list`/`-l` with patterns, `--show-current`, `-a`, `-r`, `-v`/`-vv`, `--contains`, `--no-contains`, `--merged`, `--no-merged`, `--points-at`, `--format`, `--sort`); `worktree list`; `remote` with no subcommand, `-v`, `show`, `get-url`; `config` read forms (reusing `config_only_reads`, `git_guard.rs:10716`); `stash list` and `stash show`; `tag` with `--list`/`-l` only; `describe`, `name-rev`, `rev-list`, `shortlog`, `blame`, `count-objects`, `var`, and `symbolic-ref` with no new value.

Never read-only: any form that creates, renames, deletes or sets something (`branch <name>`, `-m`, `-c`, `-d`, `-u`, `tag <name>`, `remote add`, `config` without a read flag), and any option that runs a program or writes a file: a `git -c` setting, `--exec-path`, `--output`, `grep -O`/`--open-files-in-pager`, `--upload-pack` and `--receive-pack`. `grep` joins the list only without those options.

The advice printed with an unresolved target says why the guard could not place the command (a pipe or `||` on the line, an unresolved `cd`) and suggests `git -C <literal path> …`, never `cd /path && git …`.

context: Severity: medium. No refusal of a write is removed; the cost is agent turns and confusing advice on every read-only inspection line with a pipe after `cd`.

TSK-1025.title: A standalone task files its own follow-up record in its pull request
context: Issue #354, item 1 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, an adopter's standalone task TSK-643). The task's pull request carried its own record and a new follow-up task record that its AC-6 waiver names, and `codeflow ci` refused it under `work.classification`: "a task PR may add only its own standalone task record". Removing the follow-up record after completion then forced a reopen, which led to the issue's other two items. Those are placed elsewhere: the waiver refused after a reopen is TSK-340 AC-7, and `work.criteria_frozen` counting the task's own remote branch is TSK-350 AC-5.
Read on the line tip `7172229aa`:

items.text: the refusal: `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/classification.rs:1055-1066` refuses any added record that is not the PR task's own, and any second added record;

the documented route: `docs/cli.md:118` (`--follow-up-of`) says a standalone task's follow-up is "a standalone task, filed on a task branch cut from the target, with its record filled in and committed, then claimed with `work claim`". That is the follow-up's own task pull request, which carries its code, so the record reaches the target only when the follow-up's work lands, after the source task that names it;

the issue says `work claim` needs the predecessor complete on the target. Not confirmed: `task new --follow-up-of` writes only `follow_up_of` and no `depends_on` edge (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/light_paths.rs:200`), so a claim is held back only when someone adds that edge by hand.

context: Outcome: **a standalone task can file the follow-up its own acceptance names in the same pull request, and the docs give one route that works before the source task lands.**

Design: a standalone task pull request may add, besides its own record, only the follow-up records its own acceptance block names in `follow_ups`: new standalone tasks whose `follow_up_of` is the pull request's task, at status `todo`, with no product path of their own. Every other added record stays refused, as does a follow-up record that is complete, names another source, belongs to an epic, or is changed by a later commit in a way that would bind work to it. The alternative, docs only (file the follow-up first in a records-only pull request), keeps classification unchanged but adds one pull request and one merge cycle per follow-up, which is the cost the issue reports; the bounded allowance is chosen because the added record carries no work and is reviewed with the source task that names it.

TSK-1026.title: The managed CI cancels superseded runs and skips a proven repeat

next.reason: task TSK-1026 depends on TSK-359, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Issue #352, items 1 and 2 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). The managed workflow `assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml` has no `concurrency` group, so a new push to a pull request leaves the superseded run going to its end, and a push whose tree an earlier hosted run already passed runs the whole gate again. An adopter edited the managed file to add both and recorded it as a workaround. The issue's item 3, sharded gates, is TSK-384 AC-5 and AC-6.
Read on the line tip `7172229aa`:

items.text: the template has no `concurrency` key (none in its 1,079 lines); this repository's own `.github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml:30-32` already uses a group per workflow and ref with `cancel-in-progress` only for `pull_request` events;

the template runs on `pull_request`, on pushes to `main` and `master`, weekly and on dispatch (`codeflow-ci.yml:26-35`), and since TSK-449 a pull request runs the essential mode and a push the full mode (`:170-198`);

this repository skips a repeated push run through `scripts/ci-reuse.py`; TSK-359 is hardening that lookup's binding (the exact merged pull request, base, tested merge tree, workflow blob and required jobs) and states "changing the shipped template" as its non-goal.

context: Outcome: **the managed workflow cancels a superseded pull request run, and a push to the protected branch whose tree a bound pull request run already passed reuses that verdict under TSK-359's binding, with the secret scan and every security job still running.**
Design and tradeoffs:

items.text: Concurrency: a pull request run is superseded only when a run for a newer head of the same pull request starts. Proposed, for AC-6 to confirm: a group per workflow and pull request, `cancel-in-progress` true only for a `synchronize` event (the one `pull_request` event that brings a new head), and the queue mode TSK-1040 adopts (`queue: max`), so a same-head event (`opened`, `reopened`, a re-run, a repeated arrival) neither cancels a running run nor replaces a pending one; it waits and completes. If AC-6 finds that expression unsound, each run first checks whether its head is still the pull request's head and stops when it is not, and same-head runs share no cancelling group. Push, schedule and dispatch runs are never cancelled, so a protected-branch verdict is always completed. Cost: a cancelled run shows as cancelled on the superseded commit, which only matters for a commit nobody merges; a queued same-head run costs one more run.

Reuse: the managed workflow gets the same binding TSK-359 proves here, read from the run's recorded provenance and executed from the trusted base's copy of the helper, never from the pushed tree. A full-mode push that reuses an essential-mode pull request verdict would weaken the full gate, so reuse is allowed only when the reused run's effective mode equals the push's effective mode. A project may opt in to running essential on push, which changes the push's effective mode; it never waives the equality. Unproven reuse runs the jobs.
Never reused: the secret scan, the gitleaks canary, the security review and CodeQL, as in TSK-359.

TSK-1027.title: A review seat on macOS has a sanctioned route to drive a browser

next.reason: task TSK-1027 depends on TSK-437, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Issue #355 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, macOS, a Codex review seat in Herdr). Under the managed `cf-guard` profile, Chromium does not start: both the system Chrome and Playwright's headless shell exit with `bootstrap_check_in org.chromium.Chromium.MachPortRendezvousServer: Permission denied (1100)`. A UI review that needs the reviewer to drive a browser then falls back to a capture the author's host runs, which the reviewer can only recheck by hash, so the live checks are not independent.

Read on the line tip `7172229aa`: the limitation is known and stated in the shipped config (`assets/base/codex/config.toml:13-18`: Playwright's Chromium did not start under `cf-guard`, `cf-builder` or `:workspace` because the sandbox denies its Mach port rendezvous; it starts unsandboxed). No managed guidance gives a review seat a sanctioned route to run browser checks. The issue's observation was not re-run here.

Outcome: **a review seat on macOS can drive a browser against the reviewed head itself, through one documented route that does not widen the seat's file or network access, and a review that cannot use it says so as reduced assurance.**
Options and the choice:

items.text: Allow the Mach registration in `cf-guard`. Not chosen as the default: whether a Codex permission profile can express a Mach allowance is not established, and a Mach service allowance in a read-only reviewer sandbox is an IPC surface outside the file and network rules the profile states. AC-1 establishes the facts; if a narrow, named allowance exists and the security review accepts it, it may be the route.

Run the browser outside the seat's sandbox as a lane-owned browser server started for the reviewed head, which the review seat drives over its own lane socket. This reuses TSK-437's per-seat socket allowance, and the reviewer issues every interaction itself. Chosen unless AC-1 finds a sound profile allowance. A lane socket controls who connects, not what the connected browser can do (TSK-437 states that a browser server can read files the browser reaches and take raw DevTools commands), so this route needs its own boundary: the browser process runs in its own sandbox, or behind a broker that passes only the automation commands the review needs, with file reads limited to the served reviewed head and a scratch profile, network limited to the local server under review, and downloads and file writes refused. The seat's own denies being unchanged does not prove that boundary; AC-2's negative canaries do.
A host-executed capture with a hashed report stays the documented fallback and is recorded as reduced assurance, never as an independent live check.

TSK-1028.title: The scaffold ships a useful status line and leaves effort to each person
context: Issue #351 and its two maintainer comments of 2026-10-27 (07:38Z and 21:04Z), CodeFlow 3.1.1. The scaffold writes personal preferences into the shared project settings, where they replace each contributor's own choice: a branch-only `statusLine` and `effortLevel: "high"` in `.claude/settings.json`, and `model_reasoning_effort = "high"` in `.codex/config.toml`.

The 21:04Z comment states the status line both consuming repositories now carry as their workaround, and asks that it, or a configurable equivalent, be the scaffold default, with a contributor's own line in `.claude/settings.local.json`. Quoted from the comment:

It reads Claude Code's status JSON on stdin and prints the model display name and id, the Claude Code version, the output style, the folder name, the git branch when there is one, and the context used as tokens out of the window and as a percentage: green below 50, yellow below 80, red from 80. It needs `jq`.
Read on the line tip `7172229aa`:

items.text: the three Claude presets set both keys: `assets/base/settings/default.json:7` and `:576-579`, and the same in `acceptEdits.json` and `bypass-sandboxed.json` (`:7`, `:577`); the shipped line is `printf '%s' "$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo codeflow)"`, unchanged since `fe644c345` (2026-06-12) per the 07:38Z comment;

`codeflow update` adds any shipped top-level key a project's file lacks and keeps any value it has (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/settings_merge.rs:200-207`), so a project that deletes `statusLine` or `effortLevel` gets them back on its next update, and a project still holding the old shipped line never receives a new default. `env` and permissions have a baseline-guarded rule; these keys do not;
`assets/base/codex/config.toml` sets `model_reasoning_effort = "high"`, and the file is managed (`assets/base/scaffold-manifest.toml:278-282`);

every seat launch already passes its effort (`cf-herdr/SKILL.md:104-107`: Claude `--effort`, Codex `-c model_reasoning_effort=…`, Grok `--reasoning-effort`), so the effort pins set only what a person gets when they start a session by hand;
the effort pins are a recorded decision: ADR-0056 says "Codex project settings pin high. Claude settings provide `effortLevel: high` as a starting default";

`.claude/settings.local.json` outranks the shared file (`cf-customize/references/claude-context-policy.md:47-49`) but is per checkout (gitignored, `assets/base/gitignore:17`). Corrected during review: since Claude Code v2.1.211 a worktree session uses the main checkout's file, with stated exceptions such as Windows, so one personal file serves every worktree there. Codex has no per-project personal file; the issue says its only per-person override is a `-c` flag (not verified here).

context: Outcome: **the scaffold ships a useful project status line that degrades cleanly without `jq`, effort is the contributor's own unless a project opts in, and the docs say where each person sets their own values.**
Change and tradeoffs:

items.text: Status line: ship the comment's line, or a configurable equivalent that shows the same fields, as the default in the three presets. Without `jq` it prints a short fallback (folder and branch) instead of an error or an empty line. A long inline command is hard to review; the builder may ship it as a managed script the setting calls, if update keeps that script current. On update, a project whose `statusLine` is exactly a value CodeFlow shipped, proved by the recorded baseline, moves to the new default; a line the project changed stays and is reported. The shared line still outranks a person's user settings, so the docs name `.claude/settings.local.json` as the personal route and state its per-checkout limit.

Effort: `effortLevel` and Codex `model_reasoning_effort` become opt-in, offered by `cf-customize` and documented, and are no longer shipped. On update, a key whose value is exactly what CodeFlow shipped is removed; a project's own value stays. The cost: a person who starts a session by hand without their own effort setting gets the harness default, which may be lower than high; primaries launched through `cf-herdr` still enter at high.
The effort change supersedes ADR-0056's settings-pin sentence, which is the operator's call; that part waits for the approval, recorded in this task's pull request.

TSK-1029.title: The Claude compaction point is a documented project choice
context: Issue #358 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). Every scaffolded `.claude/settings.json` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=1000000` and `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=50`, so sessions compact at about 500K tokens, and the shared value sits above each contributor's own settings. The adopter reports long orchestrator sessions running near that point, and is measuring 50, 40, 35 and 30 percent on cost per session and on whether a session still knows its task, branch and next step after compaction.

Operator decision of 2026-10-27: 35 percent of the 1M window (compaction at about 350K), replacing 50; the operator proposed it ("how about 35% (350k)"). The value is revisited once the adopter's measurement lands.
Read on the line tip `7172229aa`:

items.text: the presets set both keys (`assets/base/settings/default.json:3-6`, `acceptEdits.json:3-6`, `bypass-sandboxed.json:3-6`), shipped by `3adda9b44` (2026-10-03);

the issue's "undocumented" claim holds only in part. `cf-customize/references/claude-context-policy.md` states the values, the thresholds (about 500K against Claude Code's default of about 967K on a 1M-window model; about 100K on a session limited to 200K), how to change or opt out, and the per-person override in `.claude/settings.local.json` (`:47-49`). It does not say why the value was chosen or what it costs, and it is reachable only through `cf-customize`;

`codeflow update` keeps every `env` value a project has (`crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/settings_merge.rs:227-290`), so a changed shipped default reaches only fresh installs unless update learns to move a value that is exactly the old shipped one;

the qualification kit pins the percentage at 100 in `.claude/settings.local.json` for its compaction fixtures (`cf-evaluate-model/scripts/eval_kit.py:396-403`), so it does not depend on the shared value.

context: Token-cost tradeoff, stated for the record:

items.text: every turn sends the whole context as input; with prompt caching most of it is billed as cache reads, but per-turn input still grows with the context: a turn near 350K carries about 0.7 times the input of a turn near 500K, and about 2.3 times one near 150K;
without these keys a 1M-window session compacts near 967K, so any pin lowers the peak against the harness default;

a lower point compacts more often; each compaction reads the full context once and writes a summary, and detail the summary drops is lost. The orient digest that SessionStart prints after a compaction (ADR-0013) gives context and pointers to the durable records, and rereading those records recovers task, branch and next step, which limits that loss;
the percentage also applies to sessions limited to 200K, which compact at about 70K with 35 percent;
some models price input above a size threshold at a higher rate; the current rate for the model in use is checked, not assumed (not verified here).

context: Outcome: **scaffolded sessions compact at 35 percent of the 1M window, the docs explain the cost and context tradeoff and where a project and a person change it, and the value is revisited from the adopter's measurement.**
The keys stay in the shared file: the compaction point is a team cost policy and also applies to subagents.

Corrected during the build: AC-3 first gave the personal file a per-checkout limit. Since Claude Code v2.1.211 a worktree session uses the file at the main checkout's root, except outside git, with the repository root at the home folder, on Windows, or under another owner (TSK-1028 corrected its AC-6 the same way), so AC-3 now asks where the file lives for a worktree. The AC-4 revisit is TSK-1049 (EPC-023).
Added during review (Codex rounds 2 to 5): moving a shipped value made `codeflow update --diff` and update's report show settings values, so this task also makes them show no project content.

Display contract, stated identically in TSK-1029 and TSK-1051: a diagnostic, report line or export never contains a value, key, heading or line a project wrote, in its text, its `Debug` form or any error it wraps. It may name a path, a line and column, a count, and a schema name or heading CodeFlow defines. A version is shown as `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, plus a prerelease only in CodeFlow's own release form (`alpha.N`, `beta.N`, `rc.N`); any other prerelease, and any build metadata, is shown as `(with a suffix)`, and a value that does not parse as a version is not shown.
Ownership:

items.text: TSK-1029 owns everything `codeflow update` and `codeflow update --pin` print and write to the `--diff` export. The export is judged only against the assets embedded in the binary (`scaffold/diff_redact.rs`). Report lines name step positions, keys and paths. The readers and wrappers they reach are covered: the project metadata and state files (`scaffold/state.rs`, `registry.rs` and its locked read in `file_lock.rs`), the version check and version display (`scaffold/version.rs`), pending update records (`scaffold/update/pending.rs`), the PR template diagnosis, whose project headings are named by position or count (`scaffold/pr_template.rs`), the workspace policy load (`hooks/policy.rs` `Policy::load_file`), the remote policy read (`remote.rs`), the CI pin checks that `codeflow doctor` shares (`scaffold/release_pin.rs`, `doctor/ci_pin.rs`: an unreadable digest line is named by number, a duplicated key only when CodeFlow defines it), and release downloads, named by artifact and failure category, never by URL or curl output, with an invalid `--pin` named without its value. TOML and JSON errors become a `ParsePlace` (`scaffold/mod.rs`): format, a fixed kind, line and column. `ScaffoldError` never keeps a parser error as its source.

The boundary is a type (Codex rounds 5 and 6). Every line those commands print or export is a `Shown` (`scaffold/shown.rs`), whose text is private and which has no conversion from a string. Its fixed-text constructors take only `&'static str`; runtime values enter only as a count, a path, a parse place, an I/O category, a version under the rule above, a date, a hash the binary computed, or a slice of a `Shipped` text (`scaffold/assets.rs`), which only the asset reader or compiled-in text makes. `shown!` takes a literal format and `Shown` arguments only. `Report`, `ScaffoldError` and the `--diff` sections hold only `Shown`; the pin report keeps its versions as strings and formats through `Shown` (`PinReport::shown`). Their `Debug` writes the same text, and `ScaffoldError` keeps no source. A catalogued remedy is filled in one pass over its own text, so a brace in a filled path is copied as text. The other public report and error types update reaches (`PinReport`, `PinnedDigests`, `Unparseable`, `RootUnreadable`, `Diagnosis`, `KeptTemplate`) have a `Debug` that shows no project text. Everything update prints after its report (the workspace hint, the cf-present state warning, the registry warning, the PR template prompt, `update --pin`) goes through the CLI writers `say`, `warn` and `prompt`, which take a `Shown`; a failed git read is named by the step and its exit code. Because `Report` and `ScaffoldError` are shared, `codeflow init` and the docs portal setup build their lines the same way; TSK-1051 still owns their review, and `init --workspace`'s git step output (`git_run`). `tests/update_display_boundary.rs` checks in the core and CLI sources what the type cannot see: no `leak`, each runtime-text constructor call listed with what feeds it, and no print outside the writers in the CLI functions update and `update --pin` call. It reads source, not expanded code, and follows calls by name, so it is not a proof that every route crosses the boundary; its limits are in its header. `codeflow-present` is out of its scope: update calls only `provision_state_root` there and prints a fixed line on failure. `tests/update_canary_sweep.rs` plants one canary in every input update and `update --pin` read (every installed file and baseline, the registry, a kept PR template, a pending record, task and epic records with and without a migration baseline, the version, the pin argument, the release URL and a served release), five ways each, and checks stdout, stderr and the export. These two tests and the adversarial helper tests are the contract.

TSK-1051 owns every other reader and printer in the three crates and in every shipped asset that runs, including error types outside `ScaffoldError` that keep a parser error as their source, semantic validation messages (such as `hooks/policy_schema.rs`) and `codeflow init`'s report.

TSK-1030.title: The shipped instructions say what belongs in a repository
context: Issue #279 and its comments of 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-27. Agents under CodeFlow treat the repository as the place to keep everything they produce, and nothing in the shipped instructions or the reviewer's verdict asks whether a new file belongs there. One shipped row invites the opposite: `cf-method` `references/project-organization.md:670` (the issue cites `:560` at 3.1.1; the row moved) names `docs/verification/<task>/` as the home of "retained comparison evidence" that lands on protected branches. One adopter's `main` grew to 492 files (26 MB) in 61 per-task folders under `docs/verification/`, and the adopter copied the row into its own rules.

The operator placed the instruction fix in 3.2.0 on 2026-10-27; the gate stays in TSK-428 (EPC-024, 4.2.0), because it needs TSK-424's exemption register and baseline. This task takes TSK-428's former AC-1 (the instruction) and AC-2 (the review question), which are instruction and review-question changes small enough to ship alone.

Outcome: **the shipped instructions state what belongs in a repository and what stays out, required evidence lives in the PR body or the task record, the `project-organization.md` row that names `docs/verification/<task>/` is replaced, and `cf-reviewer` asks of every added file whether it is needed long term and in its smallest form.**
Rules:

items.text: What belongs: product or authority content, code with its tests and config, and evidence a live record cites that the PR body cannot carry, in summary form. What stays out: run output and per-run logs, review records and verdict files, superseded iterations, build and cache output, copies kept for reference, scratch and session working files, duplicate copies, and per-task verification folders. Git history keeps removed evidence, so a clean-up does not lose it.
Vendoring gets one rule (the 2026-10-27 22:46Z comment): a copy a runtime needs is admitted through the project's dependency rule; a copy kept for reference is not.
The replaced row points to `cf-ship/references/pr-evidence.md` for required evidence and keeps prototypes out of protected branches as the table already says.
Consumer-facing examples that cite CodeFlow's own `docs/verification/` paths are dropped or reworded, so the folder stops looking expected.
The block and warn tiers, citation safety for removed evidence and exceptions are TSK-428's (gate), not this task's.

context: Non-goals: the gate and its tiers (TSK-428); CodeFlow's own managed-copy footprint (TSK-429); deleting what adopters or this repository already hold (AC-1 records this repository's state and routes it).

items.text: The row: `assets/base/claude/skills/cf-method/references/project-organization.md:670`, mirrored in `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills` and both `.codeflow/.baseline` trees.

Examples citing CodeFlow's own evidence paths: `assets/base/agents/skills/cf-present/resources/figure-grammar.md:153` and `utility-presentation-system.md:29`, the same two in `cf-docs-portal/resources/`, `assets/base/rules/writing.md:287` and `:334`, and `cf-model-orchestrator/resources/grok-host.md:56`.
Defaults that treat the folder as standard: `assets/docs-portal/starter/portal.config.json:11` and three fixtures in `cf-evaluate-model/resources/fixtures.json` (`exclude: ["docs/verification"]`).

Nearest existing rules: `assets/base/rules/workflow-discipline.md:145` "Write only what earns its keep" (code, not files); `cf-ship/references/pr-evidence.md` (the PR body's evidence, no rule on files); `cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/evidence.md` (evidence quality, no home rule); the managed `assets/base/gitignore` (secrets, editor files, worktrees; no build or run output); `cf-reviewer` (`assets/base/claude/agents/cf-reviewer.md`) has no added-file question.
This repository: `docs/verification/` holds 91 MB in 60 folders, and 79 records under `project-management/` cite paths in it.

TSK-1031.title: The shipped instructions hold project tooling to the tests product code gets
context: The operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, tests and coverage (D2). Issue #299 asks that every test-running target meet the coverage floor; TSK-1006 (EPC-024) builds that floor as a default, and TSK-1014 (this epic) fixes the ignored `defaults.coverage`. Neither says that a project's own tooling (scripts, build helpers, code generators, release and CI helpers, hook scripts) is code held to the same tests and floor. The shipped coverage rule speaks of "aggregate production-code coverage" and lets generated, vendor, fixture and test code be excluded, so an agent can read tooling as outside the rule, and adopters' tooling went untested and unchecked (issue #275's evidence: 59 JSON loaders and 21 git wrappers in one repository's tooling).
This task is the instruction half, small on its own; the default floor for tooling targets needs TSK-424's register and stays in TSK-1006.

Outcome: **the shipped instructions say that project tooling is code that ships with tests, runs in a test target and counts toward the coverage floor; `cf-stack` wires a test target for the project's tooling when it has any; and `cf-reviewer` treats an untested tooling change as it treats untested product code.**
Non-goals: the floor as an enforced default and its exemptions (TSK-1006); the defaults fix (TSK-1014); this repository's own untested scripts (AC-1 records them and routes them).

items.text: `assets/base/agents/skills/cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/coverage.md:19-25`: the 80% floor applies to "aggregate production-code coverage"; no word on tooling.
`assets/base/rules/workflow-discipline.md:176` "Prove it at every surface": tests ship in the same change; no word on tooling.
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-stack/SKILL.md:17-28`: test targets per package; no tooling target.
`assets/base/testing/templates/` (nine templates): none has a tooling target.
`assets/base/claude/agents/cf-reviewer.md` step 4: coverage against the configured floor, with no scope statement.

This repository: `.codeflow/test-config.json:299` runs eight `scripts/test_*.py` files with no coverage; `scripts/changelog_split.py`, `gate-binary.py` and `coverage-shards.py` have no test file; the nine vendored Python files under `assets/` (eight in `cf-evaluate-model/scripts`, one in `cf-herdr/scripts`) are not under a coverage target.

TSK-1032.title: The shipped instructions require typed code and typed data at every boundary
context: Issue #275 (items 1 and 6 and its comments of 2026-10-22) and the operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, strict typing (D3). Three shipped texts steer agents away from strictness: `cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/design-implementation.md:24-33` (types "where they prevent material errors"; no "stricter-compiler or language migrations merely to satisfy this rule"), `cf-develop/SKILL.md:41-44` ("never force a stricter compiler") and `cf-stack/SKILL.md:32-35` ("Do not mandate TypeScript, a validator library"). Under them, reviews passed Python at 5% annotated, hundreds of `dict[str, Any]` and hand-written validators, and TypeScript never type-checked as a whole.

This task takes TSK-427's former AC-1, AC-2, AC-4 and AC-5 (the texts, the review check, qualification and the journey), which are instruction and review-question changes small enough to ship in 4.0.0. The tooling per language (TSK-426), CodeFlow's own code passing the defaults and relaxations through the register (TSK-427) stay in EPC-024, because they need TSK-424's register and baseline.

Outcome: **by default the shipped instructions require new and changed code to be fully typed, every escape type and suppression to carry an inline reason, and data crossing any boundary (files, network, process, environment, database, user input, another module's untyped output) to be parsed into a typed model that also validates it, with the language's standard library for it (for example Pydantic models in Python, zod schemas in TypeScript, serde types in Rust, structs with a validator in Go); a typed representation alone (a plain Python dataclass or a TypeScript interface) does not validate its input, so the instructions name both parts; TypeScript is the default for new projects and new files, and an existing JavaScript codebase type-checks its JavaScript in place; adding the project's type checker, linter and typed-model library is in scope for `cf-develop`; and `cf-reviewer` checks it.**
Rules:

items.text: A project opts out of the default only by stating its reason in the project-owned part of `AGENTS.md` (its Stack standards) until TSK-424's register ships in 4.2.0, when TSK-427 moves the route to a register entry (the operator's decision of 2026-10-27).

TypeScript is the default for new projects and new files. An existing JavaScript codebase type-checks its JavaScript (for example `checkJs` with JSDoc types) instead of being rewritten (the operator's decision of 2026-10-27); AC-1 confirms the mechanism per toolchain.
The proportionality wording that remains applies to how much a boundary model holds, never to whether code is typed.

context: Non-goals: per-language tool setup and gate targets (TSK-426); CodeFlow's own code passing the defaults and the register route (TSK-427); rewriting adopters' existing code.

items.text: `assets/base/agents/skills/cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/design-implementation.md:24-33`: types "where they prevent material errors"; trust-boundary parsing only for untrusted input ("Trusted internal values do not need redundant runtime validation").
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-develop/SKILL.md:41-44`: points to that rule and adds "never force a stricter compiler, dependency, language, or stack migration merely for compliance".
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-stack/SKILL.md:29-35`: reuse an existing type checker; "Do not mandate TypeScript, a validator library".

`assets/base/claude/agents/cf-reviewer.md:40`: already asks for meaningful type contracts, flags unchecked casts and other bypasses, and requires runtime parsing and validation at trust boundaries with invalid, absent and unexpected values tested. The gap is the default: it applies "where they prevent material errors", so it does not require new code to be fully typed or data at every boundary to be modelled. The extension keeps its runtime-validation requirement.
`assets/base/testing/templates/example-node.json`: no type-check target.

This repository: the present web (`crates/codeflow-present/web`, TypeScript with `tsconfig.json`), the docs-portal starter (`assets/docs-portal/starter`, Astro with `tsconfig.json`) and many `.mjs` tooling scripts; Rust uses serde types at its file boundaries.

TSK-1033.title: The shipped instructions declare each value once and reviews ask about copies
context: Issue #274 and the operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, declare once (D4). Two adopting repositories held hundreds of hand copies of names, ids, team slugs, paths, settings and closed sets of strings, most bypassing a home that already existed (an exported constant nothing imports, a declared tuple compared against raw literals, a required-check guard covering two of six names), and 12 copied helper families (21 git wrappers, 59 JSON loaders, 82 repository-root lookups); a team rename needed 122 lines in 50 files edited by hand, and both reviews checked only that the edit was complete. The shipped instructions say "keep business rules single-sourced" and "stay DRY with judgment", but say nothing about declaring each value once as an enum, constant or type, and the reviewer is not asked about copies.
TSK-425 (EPC-024) is the define-once gate; it needs TSK-424's register and baseline. This task is the instruction-level part, small on its own.

Outcome: **the shipped instructions require each value with meaning (names, ids, paths, settings, closed sets of strings, limits) to be declared once as a constant, enum or type that every use reads, generates from or checks; shared shapes and helpers to have one home that callers import; and code to be DRY and modular in that sense; and `cf-reviewer` asks whether a change copies a value or code that already has a home, a new unchecked copy being a material finding.**
Rules:

items.text: The rule covers values across languages and file types (code, workflows, policy, infrastructure, config); where one language cannot import another's value, the copy is generated from or checked against the home.
A copy kept on purpose (a test's independent oracle, a stable protocol constant, documentation) is allowed with a stated reason; the instructions say which cases count.
This task delivers the review question that TSK-424 AC-5 first named ("whether a change copies a value that has a home"); TSK-424 AC-5 keeps only the exemption question.

context: Non-goals: the gate, adapters, the known-values file and exemptions (TSK-425, TSK-424); rewriting copies that adopters already hold.

items.text: `assets/base/rules/workflow-discipline.md:147-159` "Write only what earns its keep": "stay DRY with judgment, modular"; "duplicated business knowledge" is brittle under-design.
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/design-implementation.md:15-22`: "keep business rules single-sourced"; "Do not hard-code ... duplicated domain decisions".
`assets/base/claude/agents/cf-reviewer.md:30-32`: flags "duplicated business knowledge or existing abstractions"; no question about copied values or literals.
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-design/SKILL.md:195` and `references/composition-and-design-system.md:294`: the same idea for UI tokens and components.
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-stack/SKILL.md`: no duplication or magic-value lint (Ruff `PLR2004`, ESLint `sonarjs/no-duplicate-string`, jscpd) in its setup; TSK-425 owns that.
`project-management/tasks/TSK-424.md` AC-5: the review template asks "whether a change copies a value that has a home".

TSK-1034.title: A non-trivial project uses its standard framework, in proportion
context: The operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, frameworks (D5); no issue or task existed. Adopters' agents build non-trivial user-facing surfaces as hand-written vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS (issue #275's evidence: about 450 plain JS and MJS gate and prototype files in one repository), and nothing in `cf-stack` or `cf-design` says when a project should use its type's standard framework instead. CodeFlow's own runtimes point both ways: the present web is Preact with TypeScript and esbuild, the docs portal is Astro with Starlight, but the shipped `cf-present` and `cf-docs-portal` design-system kits are a 1,357-line hand-written `chrome.js` that works with no build step, and an agent may read that kit as the model for product code.

Outcome: **`cf-stack` and `cf-design` tell an agent to use the project type's standard framework (and its component, routing, state and build tooling) for a non-trivial project instead of hand-written vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS; a proportionality rule says when plain code is right (a one-page tool, a trivial script, a static page with no interaction); and the guidance states CodeFlow's position on its own bounded runtimes such as `cf-present`.**
Rules:

items.text: "Standard framework" is chosen per project type and stack from current practice and the project's existing choice; the guidance names the decision criteria and examples, not one framework for everyone. An existing framework in the project is reused.
Adopting a new framework in an existing project is a stack decision the owner approves (`cf-stack` step 1); the guidance says so.

The position on CodeFlow's own runtimes says why each is built the way it is (for example, a reference kit that must open from a folder with no build step) and that it is not a model for product code, or changes it where AC-1 finds no such reason. Rebuilding a runtime is out of scope and becomes a tracked item if AC-1 recommends it.

context: Non-goals: the strict typing defaults (TSK-1032, TSK-426); rewriting adopters' existing surfaces; rebuilding `cf-present` or the docs portal.

items.text: `assets/base/agents/skills/cf-stack/SKILL.md`: no framework guidance; step 3 reuses existing tools and says "Do not mandate ... a language/stack change".
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-design/SKILL.md:302-304`: implementation "follows the established repository architecture"; no framework choice for a new surface.
`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/ui-design.md:94`: "framework-native data flow", assuming a framework exists.

`assets/base/agents/skills/cf-present/SKILL.md:9-11` and `resources/design-system/README.md:3-5`: the bounded local runtime and a kit that "works with no build step"; `resources/design-system/chrome.js` is 1,357 lines of hand-written JavaScript, mirrored in `cf-docs-portal`.

TSK-1035.title: A doubled slash in a path is judged like its plain spelling, and the essential gate passes
context: Found by TSK-435 (PR 364), diagnosed by its Codex review (`.worktrees/tsk-435/target/review-TSK-435-codex-01.md`, GPT-6 Astra, session `01a17fcb-712f-7450-901f-d6a412fbb4bc`, "TMPDIR assessment") and reproduced for this record. This repository's essential gate target creates its run directory with `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cf.XXXXXX"` and exports it as `TMPDIR` (`.codeflow/test-config.json:151`). On macOS the default `TMPDIR` ends in `/`, so the exported path holds `//` (`.../T//cf.ab12cd`). Under such a `TMPDIR`, 12 essential tests fail; with a plain path they pass. Every local essential run on a macOS host is red, and the failures hide real regressions in the same suites.

One of the 12 is a real protection miss, not a spelling difference: `security/outward.rs:549` normalizes the candidate path, while `security/interpreter.rs:152` (`secret_path_spelling`) strips an unnormalized `HOME` prefix, so a `HOME` spelled with a doubled slash can let a secret path read through the guard (`refusal_journey/secret_paths.rs:67`). Paths the guards compare reach adopters from their own environment, so this is a security defect wherever a root is spelled with `//`.
Codex's split of the 12, confirmed by the reproduction below:

head: Group
Tests
Cause named by the review
rows: `crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/repo.rs:993` rejects repeated separators, then canonicalization fails at `hooks/git_discard.rs:224`; git-guard refuses `git worktree prune` under `git.discard_uncommitted` instead of printing the absent-worktree remedy
tests compare the original spelling with normalized diagnostics: `hooks_cli/target_repository.rs:682`, `:771`, `test_gate_cli.rs:1276`, `:1602`, `:1658`

context: Reproduction (2026-10-27, line tip `5f2fe3827`, test binaries built in the planning worktree, run outside the sandbox because one test file's name holds `secret`):

Outcome: **a guard judges a path with a doubled slash, in the candidate or in the root it compares against (`HOME`, a checkout, a worktree, a configured store), exactly as its plain spelling, failing closed when it cannot; absent-worktree handling accepts a repeated separator; the tests compare normalized paths; and the essential gate's run directory holds no `//`, so the essential suite passes on macOS.**
Rules:

items.text: Both sides of every prefix or containment comparison are normalized the same way before comparing; a path that cannot be normalized refuses.
The sibling sweep covers every comparison against `HOME` or another root in `crates/codeflow-core/src/security/` and `src/hooks/`, not only the sites above.
The test-config fix (no `//` in the run directory) does not replace the product fix; a regression test sets a `//` root directly.

context: Order: build after TSK-1002 (PR 346), which reshaped the same guard code in `security/interpreter.rs`. TSK-1002 landed in PR 346 on 2026-10-30 and the `depends_on` edge is recorded. Before unblocking, the planning amendment rechecked TSK-1002's landed code for the `HOME` comparison (`security/interpreter.rs:1447-1451` still strips an unnormalized `HOME` prefix); whatever it finds, this task keeps a regression case for the doubled-slash `HOME` miss (AC-2), even if TSK-1002 already repairs the mechanism.
Non-goals: other spellings the guard tasks already own (symbolic links, case, `~` forms).

TSK-1036.title: A blocked task can be unblocked in its own pull request
context: Issue #365 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, `48104f48b`). A task whose record is `blocked` on the target cannot be moved to `todo`, or on to `complete`, by a pull request that names it. The only range that passes is a planning amendment on a `plan/` branch whose `Task:` line names some open epic, even one the range does not touch. The documented route says otherwise: `cf-method` `references/project-organization.md:320` says a status change "rides in the task's PR", and its table (`:328`) lists "blocked to todo | `codeflow task status TSK-NNN todo`". Blocking is asymmetric: `todo -> blocked` passes in the task's own pull request, because the merge-base still holds `todo`.
Sites, read on the line tip `5f2fe3827` (the issue cites 3.1.1 lines; the `lifecycle.rs` lines were refreshed on `53749287c` on 2026-10-29):

items.text: `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:1874` `check_task_anchor` reads the status at the merge-base and projects only a reopen of a complete task (`:1904-1931`); `start_gate` (`:2310`) then refuses the blocked base record. This holds for epic tasks as well as standalone ones (code reading; the issue ran the standalone case).
`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/lifecycle.rs:1148` refuses `blocked -> complete`, and `judge_range_against` (`:2197`) judges the range whole, so a separate unblock commit does not help.

The refusal is raised at `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1715` and `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/classification.rs:986`; its remedy, `crates/codeflow-core/src/remedy.rs:244-248`, says to commit the record on this branch, which a record already on the target cannot satisfy.
`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/amendment.rs:10` lists a standalone task's change in an amendment ("listed, never refused"), but the planning class needs at least one `Task: EPC-NNN`.

context: Issue #400 (CodeFlow 3.1.1) is the same range judgment seen from a sync merge. `judge_range_against` compares each changed record only between the merge-base copy (`:2209`, one old copy at `:2260`) and the head copy, so a merge of `main` that carries `blocked -> todo -> complete` is read as `blocked -> complete` and refused (`:1148`). The triage of 2026-10-29 reproduced it on the line with `codeflow ci`: the sync merge range is refused, each of the two commits alone gave no `work.records` finding, and the plain two-commit range is refused too. The issue itself reports that pushing the sync in two steps passes; the pre-push hook was not run in the triage. The endpoint rule has a gap in the other direction: `todo -> cancelled -> todo` in one range nets to `todo -> todo` and passes, although its second step alone is refused because a cancelled task is terminal. Judging each step on its own commit closes both. As an argument about status transitions only, it accepts nothing that two separate pushes would not already accept; it proves transition legality, not review or authorship, which TSK-1066 owns. AC-7 carries it, because the fix is one change to the same function as AC-3.

TSK-1022 (this epic) is blocked on TSK-1002. Its unblock does not wait on this task: it rides in the EPC-022 batched amendment that adds `depends_on: [TSK-1002]` once PR 346 lands, a graph change that belongs in an amendment anyway, and the issue shows that route passes.

Widened 2026-10-30 for issue #424 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, by an adopter, the same root as #400). On `main` a record went `blocked -> todo` and then `todo -> complete` in two commits; a line holding it at `blocked` merged `main` in one step, and `work.records` refused the range as `blocked -> complete`. Merging `main` in two stages, one per step, passed each time and ended at the identical tree. The verdict on a status change shall not depend on how the same history was split into merges. AC-7 already requires the one-merge sync to pass; AC-8 adds the reporter's two shapes as fixtures and the same-tree comparison.

Outcome: **a task's own pull request can move it from `blocked` to `todo`, and on to `complete` when its work is done, with the Blocker removal shown to the reviewer; the remedy names a route that works; and the documented status route matches what CI accepts; and a range is judged step by step, so a sync merge that carries legal steps passes and a hidden illegal step is refused.**
Rules:

items.text: The unblock is judged on what the range does: the head record has no Blocker and the status passes through `todo`, so the start gate judges `todo`, as a reopen is projected today. Every other planning input still comes from the merge-base.
A head that unblocks a task whose blocker names an unfinished predecessor is judged by the ordinary `depends_on` rules; the unblock never admits work the graph does not.
A planning amendment that changes only standalone records needs no epic on its `Task:` line, or the docs say why one is required; AC-1 decides.

context: Non-goals: the repeated-closeout sequence (TSK-340), which this task builds on.

TSK-1038.title: Work next never offers a task whose work has landed as ready
context: Issue #370, its `work next` part. `codeflow work next` trusts each task record's status, so a task whose work has landed but whose record was never completed is offered as ready, and a session may start finished work again. The backlog already holds the fact that would stop it: `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs` `backlog` (`:774`) splits each record's claim branches into open and landed (`split_landed`, `:638`, proving a landing with `git cherry` in `landed`, `:446`), then marks the task `Ready` when no open branch remains (`:846-847`), so a task whose only branch has landed shows as ready. The landed names reach `Backlog::landed` but `work next` (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/work.rs:100`) never prints them.

Planning found no live instance on this line: no ready EPC-022 task had a remote `task/` branch merged into the line (checked on 2026-10-28 with `work next --json` and `git branch -r --merged`), so the defect is shown by code reading and AC-1 reproduces it on a fixture.
This is a defect in an existing command, reporting finished work as ready from facts it already computes, so it is placed in 4.0.0. The full audit of every drift class is TSK-1042 in EPC-023 (4.1.0).

Outcome: **`codeflow work next` never offers as ready a task whose branch has landed in its target while its record is still open; it lists such a task as landed with the suggested `codeflow task status` command, and `work claim` refuses it with the same reason.**
Rules:

items.text: A record-only branch (one that only filed or amended the record) does not count as landed work; AC-1 settles how that is told apart.
Nothing changes a status; the command reports and refuses.

context: Non-goals: the other drift classes (blocker cleared, idle claims, abandoned, owed completion, epic out of step), which are TSK-1042 in EPC-023.

TSK-1039.title: A quick gate with no comparison base explains its full run
context: Issue #371 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, `48104f48b`, opened 2026-10-28 01:16Z). With targets that declare `narrow` paths and a complete green full run recorded at the merge base, the 3.1.1 pre-push hook runs every quick target on every push with the reason "no proven comparison base", about 550 to 580 seconds a push in the reporting repository, and the adopter is building its own selection map as a workaround. At 3.1.1 the hook reaches `run_gate_exact(root, "quick")` with default options (the issue cites `git_hook.rs:1278` and `gate.rs:152-153`), and the selector has no base when `--since` is absent.

That path no longer exists on the 4.0.0 line. TSK-449 (complete, PR 325, 2026-10-24) removed test-config targets from the push on purpose: the push set is `codeflow ci` over each pushed range and runs no target (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:5`, `docs/policy-reference.md:75`, the test at `crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli.rs:5537`, EPC-022 AC-125). The adopter runs 3.1.1, before TSK-449, so 4.0.0 removes the reported cost, and nothing in this task returns a test target to the push.

Issue #494 (filed 2026-11-01, also 3.1.1, `48104f48b`, tag v3.1.1, merged 2026-10-12) is the same mechanism on two more pushes: the 3.1.1 push ran the quick gate (`push_set.rs` at that commit, lines 6 and 195), so one intermittent test at the tip refused a records-only push and the push made by `codeflow work claim`, and the task that fixes the flaky test could not be claimed. PR 325 (TSK-449, 2026-10-24) is after that release, so neither push can fail on a test on this line. This task owns the regression test for both shapes (AC-2). The issue's third ask, a recorded pre-existing failure, has no push to attach to here; a failure of the cited quick gate stays the builder's to report at ready.

What remains is the quick gate that a pull request cites when it is made ready. TSK-352 (complete) gave `codeflow test` a default base: `comparison_base` in `crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/delivery.rs:388` takes an explicit `--since`, else the merge base of `HEAD` with the declared target of the task the branch carries. With no task on the branch (`plan/`, `chore/`), a detached head, or a task with no declared target (`:405`, `:413`, `:416`), it runs every target and prints only "no comparison base: ..." (`:465-467`), without saying that `--since <commit>` narrows, the route the issue itself found working.

Outcome: **issue #371's push cost is confirmed gone on the 4.0.0 line and stays gone (a push runs no test-config target), and a quick or essential gate with no comparison base runs every target and states its reason; it names `--since <commit>` as the way to narrow only where `--since` can narrow (row A below), and otherwise says that local narrowing is unavailable (row B).**
Credit rows (TSK-1044 settles which one holds; every criterion below that narrows, skips, reuses or recommends `--since` is checked against both):

head: Row
When
Required behavior
rows: the operator adopted a protected recorder in TSK-1044
the positive journeys: selection narrows, skips and reuse happen only from attested executions

every requested target runs and the reason is reported; no output recommends `--since` where it cannot narrow; positive narrowing, skip and reuse journeys are marked deferred in the epic's planning notes

items.text: TSK-449's push contract holds: a push neither runs nor waits for a test-config target.
The base stays TSK-352's rule: an exact commit from `--since` or the carried task's line, never a mutable branch name and never the push's old tip; an unproven base runs everything and names why.
