TSK-1121.title: A present document on a topic is revised in place with its version history and per-view change marks
TSK-1121.about: After this merges, a session that presents a topic again updates the topic's existing document instead of opening a new one, the reader sees which views and blocks changed since the previous revision, and an author or generator carries prior blocks forward unchanged by their ids.

next.reason: task TSK-1121 depends on TSK-1120, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: The operator's feedback of 2026-10-31: things must be reused where it makes sense, each time a report on a topic is presented, so tokens and effort are not wasted redoing them, with proper revision or versions; and it cannot be random, with too much change and no consistency from one report to the next. The runtime already keeps immutable revisions per session with a block digest per block (`crates/codeflow-present/src/state.rs:137`, `RevisionRecord`; `revision.rs:141`, `diff` marks a block `unchanged` or `changed` by digest) and `codeflow present update <session> <file> --expected-revision N` adds a revision (`cf-present/SKILL.md` section 4). What is missing is the topic: nothing ties a new document to the sessions that presented the same subject before, so a session asked for the same report opens a new session and redraws everything; nothing shows a reader which views changed since the previous revision; and an author who wants to carry a prior revision's blocks forward has no command for it, so the blocks are rewritten and drift.

Outcome: **a document may declare a `topic` (a stable key such as `status:epc-022` or `design:present-shell`; a generator derives it by lower-casing its scope key, so one scope always yields one topic); `present list --topic <key>` finds its sessions and `present open` on a document whose topic has an open session says so and offers `update`; a revision's shell marks each view and each block `changed`, `unchanged`, `new` or `removed` against the previous revision from the stored digests, in the side menu and on the view, with a "since revision N" line in the header; `present show <session> --revision N --blocks <ids>` and `--view <id>` print a prior revision's blocks as document JSON so an author reuses them unchanged; and `present diff` groups its result by view.**
Figure: the second report updates the first report's session; the runtime, not the author, works out what changed, from digests it already stores.
Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

items.text: **A topic is a key in the envelope**, `topic`, optional, lower-case words, digits, `:`, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 80 characters; it names a subject, never a revision. The session store indexes sessions by topic under the present state directory; `present list --topic` lists them newest first with revision count and last update; `present open` of a document with a topic that has an open session prints the session id and the `update` command and opens a new session only with `--new-session`, so reuse is the default and a fresh start is a stated choice. A closed session on the topic is listed and never reopened (SKILL.md section 4).

**Change marks come from digests, never from the author.** On a revision after the first, the renderer compares each block's digest with the previous revision's by block id (`block_digest`, `state.rs`, which serialises one block) and each view's digest by view id, where a view's digest covers its title, kind, context strip, the ordered ids of its blocks and children, and its place in the tree (Codex round 8, F2): a view is `changed` when any of those changed or any block in it changed, was added or removed, `unchanged` otherwise, `new` when its id is only in the new revision and `removed` when only in the old, listed in the header line and shown struck in the menu; a block id present only in the new revision is `new`, only in the old is `removed` and listed in the header line. A changed context strip with identical blocks is therefore `changed`, and a view moved under another parent is `changed` with "moved" as its word. The marks draw with the grammar vocabulary (two non-hue channels, the word in the accessible tree), on the side menu beside each view and as a small chip on the view's header; the header carries "since revision N: so many changed, new, removed"; the first revision carries no marks. A block whose id changed is `new` plus `removed`, which is the cost of breaking the id and is said in the authoring reference, so authors keep ids stable for conceptually unchanged blocks (the rule SKILL.md already states). The marks are a reading aid; they never change comment anchors or the feedback lifecycle.

**Reuse is a read, not a copy inside the runtime.** `present show <session> --revision N --blocks <id,...>` and `--view <id>` print the named blocks of that revision as document JSON an author pastes or a generator reads, so a repeat report carries unchanged sections forward byte for byte and only revises what the facts changed; a generator that writes the whole document (TSK-1098) gets the same effect by writing stable ids and stable content, and the marks then show only real change. No runtime-side merge, template or partial update: the document stays one file an author owns, and the revision history is the version history.
**`present diff` groups by view** when either revision has `views`: per view, the block changes as today; a linear document diffs as today.
Boundaries: `topic` is text through the existing validation; the topic index is a file under the session store, never in the repository; no network, no write to any record.

context: Non-goals: the shell itself (TSK-1120); the status facts and their `--since` delta (TSK-1095); the status document's ids and revision flow (TSK-1098); the skill's topic register and reply (TSK-1099); a stored template or a partial-update API; reopening a closed session.

TSK-1123.title: A completion that reaches a task range unchanged through a merge is not bound at the range head
TSK-1123.about: After this merges, a maintainer whose task branch takes another integration line's tip and then builds on it passes `codeflow ci` without reopening a task that line completed, and a completion the range itself adds, changes or reopens is still bound at the head, with later non-planning commits on it refused as before.

next.reason: task TSK-1123 depends on TSK-1083, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Source: issue #455 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, `48104f48b`, by an adopter), read on the line tip `79eec1783` after a diagnosis found no open task that covers it. TSK-1083 binds a landed task's own completion and TSK-1066 judges a sync; neither changes which commit a foreign completion is bound at in a task range.

A task branch can merge in another integration line that carries a completed task X. `codeflow ci` then binds X's completion at the task range's head and refuses every non-merge, non-planning commit on the head's first-parent chain after the merge that brought X in. Those commits belong to the task under review, not to X, so any line that takes another line and then builds on it gets a `work.acceptance_binding` block against a task nobody changed. No waiver clears it (a waiver is checked for validity only), no planning amendment clears it, and rebuilding the branch moves the block to another commit. The only route the message offers is to reopen X and complete it again at the new head, which attributes the later unit's work to a task that did not do it.
Sites, read on the line tip (the issue cites `48104f48b` lines; the code has moved):

items.text: `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:3857` `completions_in_range`. For a range that cannot be amended (a task range), `origin` is `head_oid` at `:3956-3961` for any completion that is new against the anchor, including one that arrives unchanged through a merge. A planning or line range binds at `introduced` (`introduced_at`, `:3945-3954`).

`acceptance.rs:1594` `task_landing` walks the first-parent chain from that origin back to the merge that brought the reviewed commit and records the first non-merge commit with a non-planning change (`after_merge`, `:1632-1697`). It refuses that commit at `:1753` ("only merges, planning records and landed line adoptions may follow it").

context: The issue's reproduction, in a pnpm/Nx monorepo: line A holds task X (complete, reviewed commit R, landing merge on A); line B's tip is a commit; task Y's branch on B merges A's tip, adds 13 of its own product commits and records. `codeflow ci --base <B tip> --head <Y head> --branch task/Y --into integration/B` blocks X at Y's first product commit. The same tree rebuilt as one merge with A as second parent blocks X on a record file; with A as first parent it blocks X on A's own later commits; with `main` merged into B first (ci run with `--base` at that merge) it blocks X on a `main` commit.

Design (Fable reviews it before the build): a completion that reaches the range through a merge, with its record unchanged since the merge parent that holds it, belongs to the line it came from. In a task range it binds where it was introduced, as a planning or line range already does, and is judged there:

items.text: `introduced_at` (`:4228-4259`) walks back through the first parent and then the second while the parent holds the same complete record and block, so line A may be either parent of the bringing merge. The shape with A as first parent is in scope; it is refused today because `stacked` stops when the reviewed commit is not on the first parent (`:1519-1522`), and a head merge that changes non-planning paths is refused as the completing commit (`:1680-1684`).

The completion is bound at that point by the binding the range already runs (`bind_completion_with_amendment`, `:3969-3987`), as its own line binds it. It is never skipped unjudged: a record whose bytes match the bringing parent but whose block would not bind on that parent is still refused (AC-4).
Commits after the bringing merge on the task's chain belong to the task under review and are judged against its own record, not X's.

context: What still binds at the head and is refused as today:

items.text: a record or acceptance block of X that the merge, or any later commit of the range, changes against the parent that holds X's completion;
a completion the range itself adds, changes or reopens.

context: A squashed shape (one merge whose tree also holds the task branch's own product changes) is not a change to X when X's record is byte for byte the copy on the parent that holds it; the merge's other changes are the task's own work under review, judged by the task's own binding and review, and raise no finding for X. Rejected: skipping a completion whose record equals the second parent's copy, because it accepts bytes without judging them and misses the first-parent shape.
This binds trust: the choice decides which completions a task range accepts without re-binding at its head.

Two completions in one range (the reporter's comment of 2026-10-31, https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/455#issuecomment-6550610794). The route the refusal offers, reopening X on Y's branch and completing it again at Y's head, cannot pass when Y also completes in that range. `reviewed_span_problem` (`acceptance.rs:1366`; the comment cites `:816-821` at `48104f48b`) lets only the task's own record change after its reviewed commit (SPC-013 R-60), so X's completion refuses Y's record and Y's refuses X's, in any order or commit split. The reporter's workaround is a second, records-only landing for X whose reviewed commit is Y's completion commit.

Decision on the reporter's fallback (allow any planning path after the reviewed commit, as after a landing merge): rejected as stated, taken in a narrow form, in this task's scope because the route this task's refusal prints must be passable.

items.text: Threat the broad form opens: a commit after the review could change another task's criteria or body, an epic, a spec or a decision record, and the completion would still bind, so a reviewed verdict would cover planning content no reviewer saw. Other rules judge some of those changes, but the binding would stop naming them.

Narrow form: after T's reviewed commit, another task U's record may change only when the change is U's status and Closeout (U's `reviewed_part`, `acceptance.rs:245`, is unchanged) and U's completion is itself made in this range and binds by its own rules, its own reviewed commit and review included. Any other change after the reviewed commit (U's criteria or body, a status step with no bound completion, an epic or spec) stays refused.

Why the narrow form is safe: nothing reaches a verdict unreviewed. U's status and Closeout are the part R-60 already lets a completion write after its review, and U's own binding judges them; the reviewed content of every record is unchanged.

context: Non-goals: the sync-merge check (TSK-1066), the landed-task binding (TSK-1083), a waiver that suppresses `binding_problem`.

TSK-1124.title: A sync that takes a main task's record unchanged is not a change the line makes
TSK-1124.about: After this merges, a maintainer who syncs `main` into an integration line passes `codeflow ci --branch <line>` when `main` reopened and recompleted a task the line has never held, and a sync that edits that record by even one byte still blocks.
context: Source: issue #456 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, by an adopter), read on the line tip `79eec1783` after a diagnosis found no open task that covers it. TSK-1066 makes a clean sync pass and a hand-edited sync block; neither says what `ci --branch <line>` does with a `main` task the line has never held and that `main` reopened.

A sync merges `main` into an integration line. `main` holds a task (TSK-739 in the issue) that the line has never held. On `main` it was completed, reopened with one added criterion, and completed again. The merge carries `main`'s record unchanged: the blob is the same on the merge and on `main`'s tip. `codeflow ci --branch <line> --base <line tip> --head <sync merge>` blocks it twice with `work.acceptance_binding`:

items.text: "`refs/remotes/origin/main` (commit ...) records a completion of this task, but it is not the target this run is judged against, so its criteria stay as they were; a reopened task keeps its criteria once a completion of it has landed";
"a reopened task keeps its criteria as the anchored target has them; change them in the epic's batched amendment, a planning pull request on the target".

context: The pre-push check on the same push passed: it judges from `main`'s tip, where the record is current. In the issue's table the task is absent at the line tip, complete (after the reopen and an added criterion) at `main`'s tip, and the same blob at the sync merge.
Sites, read on the line tip. Both quoted findings come from the binding of T's completion, `bind_completion_with_amendment`, under `work.acceptance_binding`:

items.text: The first sentence: `recovered_completion` (`acceptance.rs:2124`) finds main's earlier completion, because `reopened_in_range` (`lifecycle.rs:2388-2416`) sees main's reopen commit in the sync's range. `judge_reopened` (`acceptance.rs:2257`, tips at `:2308-2342`) does not count the default-branch tip as a criteria base, so the landing is `Landing::Unjudged` (text at `landing.rs:128-130`), and the refusal at `acceptance.rs:2176-2179` is pushed under `work.acceptance_binding` at `acceptance.rs:657`. That refusal keeps the earlier criteria.

The second sentence: `reopen_problems` (`lifecycle.rs:1190`) compares those kept criteria with the recompleted record and returns `REOPENED_CRITERIA` (`acceptance.rs:3679`), pushed under `work.acceptance_binding` at `acceptance.rs:658-663`.

The same text is also raised as `work.criteria_frozen` by `reopened_criteria` (`acceptance.rs:3656-3666`), but only when the line's base, or its history through `RecordStore::recovered`, holds an older complete record of T (`acceptance.rs:3768-3786`). A line that never held T gets `Ok(None)` there and raises nothing. A line that synced main's first completion earlier does hold it, so that shape can raise `work.criteria_frozen` as well.

context: Pre-push passes the default-branch tip as `--policy-from` (`ci.rs:108-113`, `ci.rs:429-447`), which makes that tip a judged criteria base, so neither finding fires there; AC-1 confirms this.

Design (Fable reviews it before the build): a record that the head holds byte for byte as the default branch tip holds it is `main`'s own content, whose criteria `main` already judged. For that record, `ci --branch <line>` shall take the default-branch tip as its criteria authority, as the pre-push check does. The choice binds to the default-branch commit and to blob equality, never to a name or a flag, and a record that differs from `main`'s tip at the head, by even one byte, is judged as the line's change.

Blob equality changes only the criteria authority for these two acceptance findings. It exempts nothing else: the status steps a sync carries stay judged one by one as TSK-1036 AC-7 requires (no remote-tracking ref or default-branch tip exempts a step), and the record is still bound and checked for its review and landing.

The issue's related report (a completed task's own branch cannot push its completion, `work.stable_planning_anchor`) is the family of #454 and is not part of this task. TSK-350 AC-13 covers the `work.criteria_frozen` shape of #454; the refusal to start from a complete record is still uncovered, and the builder names what it needs in Findings for the primary (AC-1).
Non-goals: the sync-merge hand-edit check (TSK-1066), the status steps a sync carries (TSK-1036), the #454 pre-push family.

TSK-1125.title: A work claim pinned to a predecessor accepts a local copy that is behind the pinned remote tip
TSK-1125.about: After this merges, an agent whose clone holds a stale local copy of a predecessor branch can claim a task pinned at that predecessor's pushed tip, while a copy that is ahead of the pin or diverged from it is still refused with a message that names the real cause.
context: Source: issue #459 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, source `48104f48b`), read on the line tip `b6cf648d3`; the issue's line numbers have moved, and no open task covers it.

`codeflow work claim <task> --on <TSK-A>@<sha>` refuses with "TSK-A predecessor branch has advanced; rebase on its new reviewed head and recheck" when the predecessor's remote-tracking branch is exactly at the pin and a local branch of the same name sits at an earlier commit that the pin contains. The local copy is behind, not ahead, so the message names the wrong cause and its remedy (rebase on a new reviewed head) does not apply. Deleting the local branch clears the refusal.
Sites, read on the line tip, all in `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs`:

items.text: `PinBranches::read` (`:1100`) maps each remote-tracking branch to its tracking name with `tracking_branch` (`:1117-1121`) and inserts the commit into one tip set per task and branch name (`:1124-1129`). The local `task/X` and `origin/task/X` therefore share a set, and the set does not record which tip came from which side.

`PinBranches::pin_name` (`:1188`) finds the one branch name whose set holds the pin, then refuses with "predecessor branch has advanced" when that set holds more than one tip (`:1196-1201`). It does not look at how the other tip relates to the pin.

Callers of `pin_name` or `pin_branch` (`:1260`): `reviewed_pins_in` (`:1403`), the helpers at `:1502` and `:1523`, `work start` at `:1573` and `validate_dependencies` (`:2505-2506`). The claim reaches it through `resolve_pins` (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/work.rs:288-297`) and `reviewed_pins_in`.

A second consumer holds the same refusal under another message. `stacked_pins` (`:1763`) collects, for each code dependency, every visible tip the pushed HEAD contains (`tips_of`, loop at `:1809`) and returns "this branch contains several tips" when more than one qualifies (`:1812-1828`). A claim cut from the pin has the pin and the stale ancestor both contained in HEAD, so it fails here. `codeflow ci` calls it on a push (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:700-708`, the note and empty list at `:1780-1787`), and the pre-push push set runs that command (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:297-335`). On the error the predecessor's commits are judged in the range (`classification.rs:454-459`). Today's push check fails in this shape (`crates/codeflow-cli/tests/work_cli.rs:1854-1859`, `:2018-2046`); `a_claim_on_a_reviewed_head_passes_its_own_push_check` (`:1880`) passes only when the pin is honoured.

context: Design (Fable reviews it before the build): the refusal exists so a pin is never used after its branch moved past it. A copy of the branch that the pin contains has not moved past the pin, so it is not "advanced". `pin_name` shall accept the pin when every other tip of the same branch name is a strict ancestor of the pin, judged by `descendant_of` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/history.rs:288-293`, which returns an error for an overlay, incomplete ancestry or a shallow boundary), so an ancestry that cannot be read refuses (issue 79), never reads as "behind". A tip that is ahead of the pin or diverged from it still refuses; this replaces today's "advanced" message for those two cases with one that names the branch, both tips (the pin and the other tip), the relation and the fix. `stacked_pins` applies the same rule: extra contained tips that are strict ancestors of the one tip the claim would accept collapse to that tip, an ancestry error still returns the error, and an ahead or diverged extra tip still returns an error, so the push nomination honours the pin exactly when the claim does. Both share one helper, so the two surfaces cannot drift. The choice binds to commit ids and ancestry, never to a branch name, a remote name or which side a tip came from. `pin_name` is shared with the pre-push and CI pin checks, so the builder confirms in its findings that no consumer relies on the old refusal for a behind copy, and the review carries the `cf-security-reviewer` checklist.

Non-goals: adopting an agent's own branch as the claim (TSK-1093), the pin-chain and clean re-merge rules (TSK-341), and the choice between a stale pin and a moved branch for a pin that is not the tip of any copy, which keeps its current refusal.

TSK-1152.title: A status change rides in a PR that is already landing
TSK-1152.about: After this merges, an agent or maintainer can cancel or supersede a task in the PR that settles the work, and `codeflow ci` accepts it; no guidance sends them to a PR opened only to change a status.
TSK-1152.theme: Status updates ride with the work amendment (2026-11-01)
context: Operator direction, 2026-11-01 about 14:22 EST: epic and task status updates are marked along with the work that completes them, and no PR is raised only to mark a record done or cancelled, so time, money and CI minutes are not wasted. A task's completion already rides in its own PR. Three places force a status-only PR today: `outside_own_record` in `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs` (`:3249`) refuses any change to another task's record in a task PR; `task_record_additions` in `crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/classification.rs` (`:1020`) lets a task PR add only its own record; and the cancellation route for an unlanded standalone task goes through its own `plan/` PR (`amendment.rs:337`, `classification.rs:703`, `project-organization.md:335-344`, `docs/troubleshooting.md:174`).

The change: a task PR may carry the `todo` or `blocked` to `cancelled` change of another task, and the cancelled record of an abandoned standalone task, when the carrying task's own reviewed record names it. The epic close PR carries the epic's `complete` status with its outcome record; an epic cancellation, a supersession and a follow-up status change ride in an open planning PR or the task PR that settles them. The skills, docs, templates and managed rules say so, and the `plan/` cancellation code path stays accepted for records already filed that way but is no longer recommended; with no carrier landing, the cancellation waits on the abandoned branch for the next PR that touches that work. Research and the full place list (25 rows): `coordination/coordinators/planning/status-rides.md` in the agentic-systems workspace.

Non-goals: no change to the transition table or to completion binding; a task PR still never completes another task or any epic. TSK-1036 AC-4 refuses a head "that changes another record's status"; this task narrows that refusal for the named, status-only cancellation and no other case, and its builder updates the TSK-1036 test fixtures that assert the broader refusal.

TSK-1154.title: A landing candidate accepts a task's own criteria change that its pull request already judged
TSK-1154.about: After this merges, a maintainer can land a reviewed task whose own criteria changed in its PR through a landing candidate that `codeflow ci` accepts, with no separate amendment branch.

next.reason: task TSK-1154 depends on TSK-350, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Source: issue #488 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, by an adopter), read at commit `4880597073` (the step 4 planning branch head) after a search found no open task that covers it. `cf-plan` says a task's own criteria change rides in its own PR. A task that rewrites one of its own criteria on its task branch, gets that reviewed and lands it on its integration line still fails `codeflow ci` on the landing range with `work.criteria_frozen`. The only way through is a separate records-only epic amendment that copies the criterion byte for byte onto the line first. The adopter paid that cost twice in one day (an extra branch, review, push and CI run each time).
Why no open task covers it:

items.text: TSK-350 AC-6 (issue #380) gives the task's own PR range, judged with `--into <line>` and in pre-push, a bounded exception for the task's own criteria change. Its range is the task branch's. A landing candidate is a different range: base is the line tip, head is the tip plus a no-ff merge of the task head, on a branch that is neither the task's nor an `integration/` head. Criteria classification gives such a head no own-task identity: with no class it takes the `integration/` or amendment path, and otherwise `Criteria::Frozen` (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:290-345`, with `task_criteria` at `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:4394`). TSK-350 AC-1 resolves the task from the judged head, but only for a task branch name. This task is the landing half of the same outcome, so it depends on TSK-350 and reuses its rule rather than writing a second one.

TSK-1129 (PR 478) lets a task's completion waive a criterion by naming an amendment in its own range; it does not change which range may change a criterion. TSK-1124 and TSK-1152 change `work.acceptance_binding` for a `main` sync and `work.criteria_frozen` for a carried cancellation. None admits an own-criteria change in a landing candidate.

context: Design. A range whose destination is a confirmed integration line (decided from the destination the run is given and the trusted-line binding `epic_line_binding`, `crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:883`, never from the head's branch name) judges each no-ff merge it holds as that task's own range: base is the merge's first parent, head is its second parent. A task's own criteria change brought in by such a merge is accepted exactly when TSK-350 AC-6 accepts the same change in the task's own PR range at that second parent. Everything the merge does beyond that stays judged as today. Fail closed, and bind to base-branch content and exact SHAs. The trusted line tip is the one the destination advertises for that exact ref, resolved once to a commit at the start of the run (the remote-tracking ref as fetched for a local run), never a local branch, a requester-supplied anchor or a commit the head names, as TSK-1089 fixes it (`project-management/tasks/TSK-1089.md:60-74`). With no `--into`, as in the issue's invocation, the line is the one fetched `integration/EPC-*` ref whose tip is exactly the base commit; none found means the range is not a line landing and keeps today's verdict, and two or more refuse. The checked range starts at that pinned tip: a supplied `--base` that is not the tip does not shorten it, so the whole tip-to-head range is judged, or the run refuses with the cause. The line and the epic come from the trusted records at that tip, the task's declared target is read at the line tip and at the second parent, and a criteria change that no exact parent pair explains is refused. The PR body reason line TSK-350 reads for the task's own PR is not read at landing (a landing candidate has no body to trust); the dated amendment note inside each changed criterion, which `cf-plan` already requires, is the record that travels with the content.

Decision owner: the operator approved TSK-350 AC-6 (the criteria-authority exception with its binding) on 2026-10-28, and that approval is now recorded in TSK-350's record. This task applies that approved check at the task's own merge in the line landing and moves no other criteria boundary. If AC-1's findings show the landing range needs a different authority than AC-6's, the change goes back as a planning amendment first.
Non-goals: no change to the TSK-350 PR-range verdicts; no acceptance of another task's criteria change; no change to the reopen freeze or to the completion binding.

TSK-1155.title: codeflow ci refuses a direct commit on an integration line before the gate runs
TSK-1155.about: After this merges, a maintainer sees a direct commit on a landing candidate in `codeflow ci` before the full gate runs, so the candidate is rebuilt without a wasted gate.
context: Source: issue #489 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, by an adopter), read at commit `4880597073` (the step 4 planning branch head) after a search found no open task that covers it. A landing candidate for an integration line held one commit made directly on it (a task's completion record) after a no-ff task merge. `codeflow ci --base <line tip> --head <candidate>` and the full gate passed; the pre-push hook then refused the push with `work.epic_line`. The gate (about 12 minutes there) had run on a candidate that could never land, and the candidate and the next two queued landings were rebuilt.
Cause, read on the tip above:

items.text: The rule is raised only by the pre-push hook: `epic_line_push` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs:1302`) calls `line_adoption::check_range` over the pushed range and emits `work.epic_line` (`:1396`). Nothing in `codeflow ci` emits that rule id.

`codeflow ci` runs `check_epic_line_with_adoptions` only when the head's branch name starts with `integration/` (`crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/classification.rs:639`), and that judges the line's range into the default target. A candidate named otherwise, with the line tip as base, reaches no epic-line check.

The hook's own doc comment says a range it cannot read is a note because "CI stays the hard line (charter D19)" (`git_hook.rs:1293-1301`). CI does not hold that line for this rule today, so the hook is the only check.

context: Overlap checked, none found: TSK-1151 (records-only landing candidates, PR 486, coord/parallel) changes which checks a candidate's class selects (`classification.rs`), not the epic-line rule; TSK-1089 keys line treatment on a branch's commits for a line-to-main range, not a range onto the line; TSK-433 and TSK-248 are complete; TSK-402 judges a carry merge onto another line and must keep passing here (a merge is not a direct commit). The nearest region is coord/parallel's: this task lands in `codeflow ci`'s candidate classification beside TSK-1151, so the two are one writer at a time, and the candidate-checking route is the parallel lane's to use.

Design. `codeflow ci` judges a range whose destination is a confirmed integration line with the same `line_adoption::check_range` the hook runs, and reports the same `work.epic_line` finding with the same remedy. The destination comes from the run's inputs, never from the head's branch name:

items.text: With `--into <line>` (or the pre-push destination), the line is that ref.

With no `--into`, as in the issue's invocation, the line is the one `integration/EPC-*` remote-tracking ref (as fetched) whose tip is exactly the base commit. Zero such refs means the range is not a landing on a line: ordinary behaviour, with a note that no line destination was found. Two or more refuse, naming them.

The line is bound by `epic_line_binding` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:883`) read at the trusted tip, never at the head, as TSK-1089 does (`project-management/tasks/TSK-1089.md:60-74`). The trusted tip is the one the destination advertises for that exact ref, resolved once to a commit at the start of the run (the remote-tracking ref as fetched for a local run), never a local branch, a requester-supplied anchor or a commit the head names. A line whose authority cannot be established refuses.

The checked range starts at that pinned tip, as the hook's range does (`git_hook.rs:1361-1369`). A supplied `--base` that is not the tip does not shorten it: the whole tip-to-head range is judged, or the run refuses with the cause. `check_range` excludes history through the base it is given (`line_adoption.rs:185`), so without this a base placed after a direct commit would hide it.

context: A destination confirmed to be something else, such as `main`, keeps ordinary behaviour: this rule adds nothing there. Fail closed for an intended line: a binding that cannot be established, an ambiguous destination, history that cannot be read, and malformed adoption entries each refuse in `codeflow ci` with the cause, since CI is the hard line. The adoption entries are the ones `check_range` already reads (landed at the target or in the line's history); the head alone cannot adopt its own direct commit.
Non-goals: the hook keeps its note for an unreadable range (charter D19); no change to which direct commits an adoption entry may excuse.

TSK-1158.title: An epic closes a criterion that moved to another epic, with a waiver naming the moving amendment
TSK-1158.about: After this merges, a maintainer can close an epic whose criterion moved to another epic with the serving tasks, using a waiver that names the moving planning commit, without deleting the criterion line.
context: Source: issue #492 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, by an adopter), read on the step 4 planning branch head `e0494dcb9` after a search found no open task that covers it. A planning-only amendment moves a criterion from epic A (AC-5) to epic B (as its AC-1) together with the tasks that serve it. The moved tasks keep their `(serves A AC-5)` tags, because their criteria are frozen in the line's range (issue #488, TSK-1154). `codeflow epic status A complete` then refuses AC-5 as unverified, although A's acceptance block waives it and names the planning-only commit that made the move. The adopter's workaround is to delete the criterion line from A, which leaves the moved tasks tagged with a criterion that no longer exists and which nothing reports.

Cause: `serving_tasks` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/lifecycle.rs:1472-1482`) matches a task to a criterion by its `(serves ...)` tag alone and ignores the task's `epic_id`. A's AC-5 therefore still has serving tasks, so it is not treated as an unserved criterion (`epic_own_block`, `lifecycle.rs:1548-1560`) and the epic's waiver, which `epic_waiver_problem` (`crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:1126`) already binds to a planning-only amendment of that criterion, is never consulted.
Why no open task covers it:

items.text: TSK-1129 (PR 478 head `d1ba70489`, `TSK-1129.md` Description and AC-2 to AC-4) changes the task waiver's own-range route and the planning-only path test that the epic waiver also uses (AC-3). It does not change which tasks count as serving an epic criterion, so issue #492 fails the same way after it. Nothing is added there; this task relies on that planning-only test as it stands and does not change it.

TSK-1154 (issue #488) lets a task's own criteria change land. The moved tasks' tags are not a task's own change, and the freeze is not the cause here. TSK-350 is the PR-range rule, TSK-1124 and TSK-1152 change `work.acceptance_binding` and `work.criteria_frozen` for a `main` sync and a carried cancellation. None touches the epic completion check.

context: Design. A task serves the epic criterion its tag names only while the task's `epic_id` is that epic. A tag that names epic A on a task whose `epic_id` is another epic B is a moved serving task and is handled by a recorded move, not by the tag alone:

items.text: A's criterion carries a recorded move to B's criterion (the form is the dated note that criteria already use, settled in AC-1 against the existing criteria text rules; the existing `Moved YYYY-MM-DD` sub-bullet is a text-correction note, `record_text.rs:40-43` and `:64`, so the move form must not reuse that word). The move counts only when, read at the reviewed commit, B exists and its status is open (`EPIC_OPEN`, `lifecycle.rs:1034`; a complete, cancelled or archived B never counts), the single planning commit that records the move also introduces B's target criterion with the same obligation text and the same `(journey)` and `(after release)` tags, and the moved task's `epic_id` is B. A forged, dangling, self-referencing or pre-existing-destination move grants nothing, so a note cannot aim finished tasks at a criterion B already had.

For A, the moved criterion is closed only by a `waived` row in A's own block that `epic_waiver_problem` accepts (a planning-only amendment the reviewed commit contains and which amends this criterion) and whose commit is the one that records the move, not an earlier wording change. A `verified` row, a tick or silence never closes it, and an `(after release)` source criterion stays on today's deferral path, which a waiver does not close, so moving a task cannot lower the proof a criterion needed.

For B, the moved tasks' tags resolve through the recorded move to B's criterion only when those tasks are its only serving tasks, so B's close still needs a complete serving task that verified it, and a `(journey)` source still needs `journey: verified` on B. The proof stays with the tasks; only the epic's name changes.

`codeflow validate --docs` warns (does not block) when a task's `(serves X AC-n)` names a criterion that does not exist, or names an epic other than the task's own that records no move to the task's epic.

context: Fail closed: a move that cannot be read, or any doubt about it, leaves the criterion served and unverified, as today. Non-goals: no change to the waiver's planning-only test, to the reopen freeze, to task criteria (frozen as the line holds them) or to the criteria-authority rules of TSK-350 and TSK-1154.

TSK-1173.title: A claim is one step that records the task's start
TSK-1173.about: after this merges, `work claim` creates the task branch and its worktree, commits `claimed:` and `claim_base:` into the task's record as one commit, pushes the branch with that commit and runs the start preflight; `estimate outcomes` takes the `claimed:` time as the start when it is the task's own claim; `work start` stays the read-only re-entry check for a resumed session and CI; and a claim with no later commit reads as an idle claim with its age.
TSK-1173.theme: Estimation cut, TSK-336 split and issue 502 amendment (2026-11-01)
context: Issue #334 item F and section 1.5 ("claim and start are one step"), under operator decisions D1 and D4 (2026-11-01). Today `work claim` pushes an empty branch and prints "check it out and run `codeflow work start`". The task's start is only the first later commit, and a squash landing loses even that (`ADR-0079:42-44`). This task makes the claim the one step that starts the clock.

Outcome: **after this merges, `work claim` creates the task branch and its worktree, commits `claimed:` and `claim_base:` into the task's record as one commit, pushes the branch with that commit and runs the start preflight; `estimate outcomes` takes the `claimed:` time as the start when it is the task's own claim; `work start` stays the read-only re-entry check for a resumed session and CI; and a claim with no later commit reads as an idle claim with its age.**
Design (settle in the PR; recommendations from the start-clock research):

items.text: One commit on the task branch writes `claimed: <RFC3339>` and `claim_base: <40-hex sha>` into the record frontmatter (the one-line edit `task status` already makes, `status_verb.rs`), using `git commit --only` on the record path. In git, so ADR-0079's derivation holds and a squash or rebase landing keeps the start; the record's own PR may change its record (ADR-0076). Rejected: a ledger event (not in git, lost on a clone) and the pushed branch's creation time (not stored in git).

Order for a fresh claim: branch, worktree, the claim commit through `status_verb::replace_if_unchanged`, create-only push, preflight, with an attempt file in the worktree's git directory. The record is restored before any rollback; only a verified-disposable worktree and branch are rolled back, and never after the claim commit exists.

Order for an adopted (TSK-1093) or renamed branch: push as it is, create-only, so a lost race leaves the local branch unchanged; then write the two lines in the worktree where it is checked out, commit with `--only`, and push that commit with a lease. A staged or modified record file refuses the claim. A re-run resumes only on the two cases the attempt file proves; a lost race never resumes.

Start rule: the `claimed:` time; for an adopted or renamed branch the earlier of that and the first commit after `claim_base`, with provenance `known`, `declared` (the line readable, the commit or base not) or `unknown`. A hand-written line is read as declared, not as a claim. `refresh_claim` keeps the first time.

`codeflow ci` classification is not changed. The task's own `claimed:` edit selects `Tracked` and meets no new admission requirement (read from `classification.rs:217-230` and `:926-1067`; this task proves it with fixtures).

Hotspots read first: TSK-1093, TSK-1125, TSK-1047, TSK-341, TSK-416 and TSK-1105 (both this task and TSK-1105 edit `readiness.rs` and `work.rs`; one writer at a time, the Coordinator's call; this task first, since it sets the shape).

TSK-1179.about: after this merges, `codeflow ci` accepts a reopened task whose completion landed when its own PR completes it with `AC-n: waived | <40-hex sha>`, where that commit appends a waiver annotation to criterion n, keeps its original text unchanged, cites the superseding commit by its SHA, and changes only planning records; any other change to a frozen criterion, and any unprovable condition, is refused with the cause named and the planning route.
TSK-1179.theme: Estimation cut, TSK-336 split and issue 502 amendment (2026-11-01)
context: Issue 502. After a task's completion has landed and the task is reopened, `work.criteria_frozen` refuses any edit of its criteria in its own PR, and `work.acceptance_binding` accepts a waiver only when its commit amends that criterion. Together they leave a planning amendment as the only route, even for a one-line ruling. The report gives three attempts, each refused: rewrite the criterion text, a records-only note that does not amend the criterion, and a waiver note appended to the criterion's line.

This task opens one route inside the task's own PR, the second of the issue's two options, tightened: an append-only waiver annotation on the criterion's line, bound to the waiver commit's content and SHA. The original criterion text stays byte for byte, which is what the freeze protects, so the freeze is unchanged for every other edit. Neither a name nor a branch decides it.

Outcome: **after this merges, a reopened task whose completion landed can complete in its own pull request with `AC-n: waived | <40-hex sha>`, where that commit appends a waiver annotation to criterion n, keeps its original text unchanged, cites the superseding commit by its SHA, and changes only planning records; any other change to a frozen criterion, and any unprovable condition, is refused with the cause named and the planning route.**
Rules (fail closed; authority bound to content and SHAs):

items.text: **Content, not claims.** The waiver commit's diff for criterion n must be a pure append: the pre-image of the criterion block is an unchanged prefix of the post-image, and the added text matches the annotation form `Waived <date>: <reason>. Superseded by <40-hex sha>.` No other line of any criterion changes, and no criterion is added or removed.

**SHA-bound.** The waiver value is a full 40-hex commit id. A branch, tag, abbreviated id, PR number, person or role name is refused. The commit must be in the head's own range, after the reopen commit and strictly before `reviewed` (the existing ordering rules), and must be the commit that adds the annotation (not a later or earlier record commit).

**The superseding commit is named by SHA and resolved.** The annotation's SHA must resolve to a commit reachable from the head's history; it is recorded, and review judges whether it supports the reason. The check proves existence and reachability, never meaning.

**Authority from the trusted side.** The rule runs under the policy authority the run pins (`--policy-from`, the pre-push hook's default branch tip), never the head's copy: a head that edits the policy cannot admit its own waiver.

**Paths.** The waiver commit changes only the task's own record, judged by the planning-only test TSK-1129 gives both waiver routes (no product code, policy, harness instruction, hidden file, adopter-facing path, symbolic link or submodule).
**Verb and CI agree.** `codeflow task status <id> complete` and `codeflow ci` reach the same verdict and print the same refusal.
**Scope.** Only a task with a landed completion that was reopened is affected. Other tasks' criteria, a task that was never completed, and a criterion text rewrite keep today's refusals.

TSK-424.title: One exemption register and relaxation report serves every managed check

next.reason: task TSK-424 depends on TSK-1077, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Issues #274 (item 2 to 5), #275 (items 4 and 5) and #279 (item 5) each ask for the same mechanism: a project that relaxes a default check, or exempts one occurrence from it, records why, who owns it and when it is revisited, in one format every check reads, and `codeflow ci` reports the register's health in the pull request evidence. CodeFlow 3.1.1 has no waiver or exemption concept, so each adopting project invents its own register, field set and refusal rules.

Outcome: **one exemption register format under `.codeflow/` serves every managed check this epic adds: each entry carries id, kind, rule, paths, value where it applies, reason, task id, owner role, date, expiry and revisit trigger; the register also holds permanent admissions (`admitted`, frozen-tree, provenance and `removed` rows); for every blocking class an entry applies only when the default-branch authority holds it; a check refuses a missing field, a malformed task id, an exception past its expiry, a head-introduced entry that matches nothing, a class-wide entry and an inline suppression that cites no register id, and reports a stale base entry for retirement in that pull request; admitted debt, admitted once in the pull request that introduces the check and compared against the previously admitted baseline by stable occurrence identity, can only shrink; and `codeflow ci` reports entries, expiring entries, baseline size and its change in the PR evidence.**
Rules:

items.text: The register (provisional `.codeflow/exemptions.json`) and the baseline (provisional `.codeflow/baseline/<check>.json`) are project files. The default-branch authority (TSK-1077) governs the check's own configuration and level, so a head can never turn a check off or lower it (as the secret-scan exemptions are judged, TSK-292, TSK-336). For a blocking class, an entry applies only when the authority holds it; a pull request that adds only register entries is the exemption-PR class (`docs/policy-reference.md:301-308`) generalised to the register file, and lands through the operator's merge. For warn-tier and report-only consumers, an entry introduced or amended at the head applies only with every required field and is listed in the PR evidence as a new or changed exemption, never silent. An entry retired at the head is accepted when its occurrence is gone at the head (the ordinary same-PR repair-and-retirement); a base entry that matches nothing at the head is reported as stale and retired in that pull request, never refused; a head entry that matches nothing is refused. A setting `max_exemption_days` bounds the expiry of exceptions.

Admitted debt is separate from exemptions and has its own lifecycle. The baseline records stable occurrence identities (path, rule and a content hash of the occurrence, never a line number), each naming its fix task. The ratchet compares the head's occurrences against the previously admitted baseline, the one at the default-branch authority, never against a baseline the head edited: a pull request passes only when every head occurrence is in the admitted baseline by identity, so growth and replacement debt (one admitted occurrence removed, a different one added) are refused whatever the head's baseline file says; a head may change the baseline only to remove occurrences that are gone (shrinking), and any other head edit of the baseline is refused. Initial admission needs no extra pull request: `codeflow baseline admit <check>` (provisional) writes the first baseline from the current occurrences, each with a fix task, inside the pull request that first introduces the strict check for that project, and `codeflow ci` accepts an admission only when the authority holds no admitted baseline for that check and prints the admitted occurrences in the PR evidence; every later head may only shrink it, and widening admitted debt is forbidden by the ratchet (any relaxation is a separate operator-authorized policy change, never a baseline edit). An occurrence with no fix task is refused at admission and at validation.
A project-wide relaxation of a default (issue #275 item 5, #279 item
is an entry of kind `relaxation` naming the setting and its value, with the same required fields; `codeflow ci` lists each one.

Permanent admissions: `admitted` rows without expiry (allowed `lowers`; never for secret-name, ignored-path, oversize, frozen-tree or provenance classes, except the per-path size admission of TSK-323's route 3); frozen-tree rows (the tree id equals the authority's; the candidate's final tree is compared, modes included); provenance rows (source repository, commit and digest, checked each run); and `removed` rows for TSK-428's citation rule. Expiry applies to exceptions only. Task state an entry cites is read from the authority's records.
The checks that consume the register are TSK-425, TSK-426 and TSK-428; this task ships the reader, the writer, the schema and the report, with one consumer stub test.

context: Non-goals: any one check (the consumers); the secret-scan and dependency-audit exemption routes that exist today (unchanged).

Rules (decided 2026-10-29, design revision 5 for issue #279, decisions 7, 9, 10 and 11):

items.text: Placement. The checks are content classes of `path_policy`, judged by `codeflow ci` in the `pull_request_target` job from the authority's binary and policy, and by pre-commit and pre-push from the landed policy. They are never a `testing/` target or a job in `codeflow-ci.yml`, because those run head code on `pull_request` and a block tier there would let a pull request change the check that judges it (design N-5).

Tiers. **Block** refuses; **warn** lists the finding in the `codeflow ci` PR evidence and passes; a warning acknowledged in the body informs the reviewer and is never a pass. Default tiers (decision 7, hybrid): block per-task evidence folders under the configured root (default `docs/verification/`, so `docs/verification/TSK-001/...`), `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/` and `.DS_Store`; warn `dist/`, `*.log` and other run output, single-tool caches, byte-identical duplicates, superseded iterations (an explicit superseded marker outside record frontmatter, or a removed path added again), large files, draft siblings (`-r2`, `-v3`, `-final`), tool-output-like JSON or text, uncited research, and a live record citing a path under the local evidence home. A class moves only by a reviewed policy change on the authority.

No review-record class (decision 10: this repository holds 11 legitimate review paths). The superseded marker warns (decision 11: three accepted ADRs would fail a block). No named catalogue and no public fixture format (decision 9).

Scope. Junk classes use net scope: a path in the head tree that matches a class and is absent from the base tree. A file added and removed on a line never blocks its pull request, and an existing file is never judged by an unrelated pull request. Audit mode (`codeflow ci --audit`) lists the final tree and never gates. Secret names and the gitleaks content scan keep history scope, untouched here.

Citation safety. When evidence is removed, a live citation of the removed path is refused unless it carries a commit pin that resolves to a commit reachable from the authority the run judges with and holding the file. Managed baseline files and their exact mirrors are exempt from this check only.

Exceptions. Every exception is a TSK-424 register entry; for a blocking class it applies only when the authority holds it, so a pull request cannot admit the file it adds (design N-6). No entry exempts a directory as a whole.

Exempt inputs. Content classes exempt only `.codeflow/policy.json`, `.codeflow/project.toml` and the two policy workflows; TSK-424's register file is not exempt unless a later operator amendment says so.

Matchers are declarative only (folder segment, exact name, suffix, name token, root glob, size, duplicate blob, superseded marker), compiled into the binary, with no executable adapters. Name patterns compare whole parts of the file name without its last extension, split at `-`, `_` and `.`, in lower case, so `confirmed` does not match `confirm`.

The security contract below governs every run. AC-6 holds the contract. If the builder finds the rerun too large for one pull request, it is split out as one tracked EPC-024 task that takes AC-6, through the batched epic amendment, and is never dropped.

context: Security contract for the rerun (Codex review 06 of PR 449, F7). The command comes from a record a contributor writes, so it is untrusted code, and the rerun is a command-execution feature. Each rule names the threat it closes and why its design is the standard one.

items.text: Activation from the trusted authority. `work.evidence_rerun` (off by default) and its limits (`timeout_secs`, `network`, default `false`) are read only from the policy at the default branch resolved to one SHA, the authority TSK-1077 defines (ADR-0091), before any candidate input is read. The candidate branch's policy, the working copy's and the exported tree's are never read for these keys. A missing or unreadable authority means off, with a note; it never means on. `ci` and `task status complete` use the same resolver. Threat closed: a contributor turning on execution of their own command, or loosening its limits, from the change under review. Standard design: authorization comes from the protected base, never from the change (the trust rule GitHub applies to fork pull requests, and CodeFlow's own ADR-0091).

Containment by a named provider, fail closed. The runner launches the command itself inside an operating-system sandbox: Seatbelt (`sandbox-exec`) on macOS and bubblewrap (`bwrap`) on Linux, the same mechanisms the harness sandboxes use, with a deny-by-default profile. The existing `crates/codeflow-core/src/security/actions.json` supplies the action and read-rule catalogue the profile draws on; translating it into Seatbelt and bubblewrap profiles is new work in this task, since no profile generator exists today. The profile allows reads of the exported tree and the system toolchain paths, writes only to the exported tree and one fresh temporary directory, and no network unless the trusted policy's `network` is `true`. The command starts with an empty environment plus a fixed allowlist (`PATH` set to fixed system directories, `HOME` and `TMPDIR` set to the temporary directory, `LANG`); nothing is inherited, so tokens, `GIT_*`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and cloud credentials are absent, and the profile denies the home credential paths. If the provider is missing (Windows, no `bwrap`), cannot start, or any check below fails, the runner refuses before running any command and says why. A timeout and a temporary directory are not described as containment. `codeflow test`'s runner is not the boundary: it inherits the environment and applies no sandbox. The required properties follow; the mechanism is the builder's, settled with the task's security review.

Provider floor. The provider executable is resolved independently of the candidate (a fixed trusted path or the trusted policy, never the exported tree, the candidate's `PATH` or its configuration), and its version is checked against a stated minimum secure version before use; an older or unverifiable provider is refused. For bubblewrap the floor is 0.12.0 or later: earlier versions have a setup-time symlink escape when creating files on attacker-controlled content ([GHSA-pxhw-h44j-8pfx](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/security/advisories/GHSA-pxhw-h44j-8pfx)). The Seatbelt floor is the macOS version the builder qualifies and records.

Tree fidelity. The exported tree's tracked paths, file bytes, modes and link targets equal the pinned commit's tree exactly, with no attribute processing: `export-ignore`, `export-subst`, filters and any candidate, working-copy or local (`info/attributes`) attributes change nothing. A tree entry the export cannot reproduce faithfully (a submodule, for example) is refused, never skipped. The export keeps no `.git` link to the repository's object store. A plain `git archive` does not meet this (it applies export attributes; this repository's `.gitattributes:18` drops a tracked file from it), so it is not the named mechanism.

Setup never follows candidate links. Exporting the tree and creating every sandbox path (mounts, bind targets, the temporary directory and any file written during setup) never follows a symlink from the candidate tree to a location outside it; a link that would require that is refused before execution. In-tree links are reproduced as links and resolved only inside the sandbox.

Trusted probe. The containment probe is trusted launcher code, not the candidate's, run under the same provider and profile as the command. It uses synthetic controls the launcher creates outside the sandbox (a file holding a fresh secret token, a writable file and, when the trusted policy's `network` is off, a reachable local endpoint), and attempts a read, a write and a connection from inside the sandbox. The probe establishes the outcome of each attempted operation independently and reports it through a channel the candidate cannot write. A read counts as denied only when trustworthy evidence shows the attempt did not obtain the file's content (for example, the launcher checks that the probe's reported read result does not contain the token it wrote); an unchanged file, no output or a generic command failure does not count. A write counts as denied only when the control file is unchanged, and a connection only when the endpoint received nothing. The read and write denials are always required; the connection denial is required only when `network` is off. A missing control, an unreachable endpoint, a probe error or any required outcome not established refuses the run. The mechanism is the builder's. Threat closed: a command that reads credentials, changes files outside its tree or sends data out, then returns the expected code. Standard design: an OS sandbox with deny by default, an emptied environment and a pre-run probe, as Bazel's sandboxed execution and the harness sandboxes do; refusing when the boundary cannot be shown is the fail-closed rule of 2026-10-24.

Parsing as untrusted input. One `run:` token per evidence field; the token takes the rest of the field. It splits at the last occurrence of ` => exit ` (one space either side) that is followed by a decimal code from 0 to 255 and then the end of the field; the text before it is the command. CodeFlow applies no unquoting, escape processing or expansion of its own: quotes and backslashes in the command pass byte for byte to `/bin/sh -c` inside the sandbox, so a `=> exit` inside quotes is command text unless it is the final delimiter. Refused before any execution: no delimiter, a code outside 0 to 255 or with a sign or leading zeros, an empty command, a newline, NUL or other control character, and a command over 4096 bytes. The reviewed sha, export path, sandbox profile and policy are computed before the command is read, and the command reaches only the sandboxed shell's argument, never a path, a git argument or the policy lookup. Threat closed: delimiter or quoting tricks that change the expected code, or that leak command text into runner setup, export or policy selection. Standard design: a fixed grammar with a single defined split point, and untrusted text passed as one argument, never re-parsed by the host.

Distinct failure classes. A provider, probe, export or launch failure is reported out of band by the launcher, never through the command's exit code, and refuses the binding as "rerun could not run"; only a command that ran to completion is compared with `<code>`. A timeout kills the process group and refuses. Threat closed: a runner or sandbox failure that happens to return the expected nonzero code being read as a reproduced failure.
The acceptance block format is shared with TSK-436 (deferred results, 4.0.0), which lands first; this task extends that format, not a copy.

context: Non-goals: proving evidence honest beyond the structural and existence checks above and the opted-in `run:` rerun; rerunning `test:` or `cmd:` evidence; re-judging completed records.

context: Issue #302, filed against CodeFlow 3.1.1 (`48104f48b`). TSK-1043.title: Each release records the tests and checks behind every managed script

next.reason: task TSK-1043 depends on TSK-427, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Issue #372 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, opened 2026-10-28 01:16Z). CodeFlow installs executable scripts into adopting repositories as managed files. An adopter with strict checks (a type checker, a linter, coverage) must decide whether those scripts are in scope, cannot fix a managed file (the next `codeflow update` overwrites it), and cannot tell from the repository what CodeFlow checked upstream. The adopter's repository holds 36 tracked Python files from 9 distinct scripts (each in `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` and twice under `.codeflow/.baseline/`); `cf-evaluate-model/scripts` ships 5 scripts with 3 test files, and `cf-herdr/scripts/deliver.py`, which types prompts into other agents' terminals, ships no test. `.codeflow/manifest.json` records `src`, `ownership`, `sha256` and `exec` per file and nothing about tests or checks. The adopter excludes byte-identical managed copies from its strict checks by a path and SHA-256 manifest, as a recorded workaround.

Outcome: **every executable file CodeFlow installs is covered by an upstream test suite and passes the strict checks CodeFlow applies to its own code, and each release ships a machine-readable assurance record per managed executable (hash, covering tests and their result, coverage, type checker and linter with versions, settings and results, the release commit and CI run), which `codeflow doctor` checks against the installed files, so an adopter can exclude a file from its own checks exactly while it is byte-identical to what CodeFlow vouched for.**
Rules:

items.text: Shipped tests: either every managed script ships its test with a documented way to run it, or none ships and the record carries the assurance; a partial set is not kept. AC-1 decides which.
The record is generated by the release pipeline from the run that produced it, never hand-written.
Provenance (a signed record or a build attestation) is in scope only if AC-1 finds the release pipeline can produce it without a new secret; otherwise it is a tracked follow-up.
The shell hooks under `.codeflow/git-hooks/` and every other file marked `exec` are in scope, not only Python.

TSK-1115.title: Python runs under the gate resolve only from the lock
TSK-1115.about: After this merges, an adopter's Python checks under the gate resolve packages only from the lock, on every machine and in CI, and an inline script cannot pull a package the lock does not hold.
context: Issue #275's comment of 2026-10-29 reports what two adopting repositories built because CodeFlow has no equivalent (lessons 8 and 9, custom parts 2 and 5): a locked-environment launcher and inline-script admission. Strict results differ between machines and CI unless every Python run under the gate resolves from one lock; and PEP 723 `# /// script` blocks let `uv run --script` resolve packages outside the lock, through `[tool]` tables (index, source, override, constraint and dependency-metadata keys) or unpinned packages. TSK-1116.title: New files meet the strict profile at once against a recorded boundary
TSK-1116.about: After this merges, an adopter migrating a large codebase to the strict profile has every new file held strict from its first commit, while the old code pays down its recorded debt.
context: Issue #275's comment of 2026-10-29, lesson 7: new files can be strict at once, before the old code is fixed. Repository A checks every new file against a recorded boundary revision per line; a copy, a rename, a new folder or a missing pragma never makes a file count as existing; lines with no recorded boundary are reported as "unproved" rather than silently passed. TSK-424's ratchet admits existing debt by stable occurrence identity and only shrinks it; TSK-426 configures the strict profile; neither makes a new file strict while the baseline is being paid down, so a long migration can grow its debt in new code.

This task adds the mode: a recorded boundary revision per target branch and line, held in the register's configuration at the default-branch authority; every file absent from the tree at the boundary is checked at the full strict profile with no debt admitted; a line with no recorded boundary is reported unproved and fails at `block`; moving a boundary is a register event with the ratchet's semantics (authority-only, and a later boundary only widens the strict set). Non-goal: the per-diagnostic ratchet itself (TSK-424) and the merge rules (TSK-1117).

TSK-1117.title: The register holds across a line's merge of main and on the merged tree
TSK-1117.about: After this merges, two parallel pull requests that are each clean cannot leave the register broken when both land, and an integration line can merge main without importing unchecked debt.
context: Issue #275's comment of 2026-10-29, lessons 3 and 6: two clean removals in parallel pull requests can combine into a broken register, so the check must run on the merged tree; and an integration line needs an adoption rule when it merges `main`, or lines either cannot merge `main` or import unchecked code. TSK-424 admits debt by stable occurrence identity at the default-branch authority and shrinks it against the previously admitted baseline; it judges one range at a time and has no rule for a line's merge of `main`. This task adds both: `codeflow ci` and the hosted job judge the register on the pull request's merge tree, and when a line merges `main` new debt is allowed only for files that differ from that `main` commit, recomputed from the line's previous tip, each entry naming the open task that owns its fix, while anything the merge itself adds fails. TSK-1118.title: Generated models match their schemas in the gate
