TSK-422.title: The coordination ledger has its contracts, store and follow command
context: Issue #272, items 2 and 4 and the comment of 2026-10-21, under ADR-0086 as the operator decided on 2026-10-22 and as the independent Codex review of the design (sound with changes, 22 findings, 14 high) settled it. An orchestrating session owns a "task ledger" that CodeFlow gives no shape, no closure rule and no home; in an adopting project a hand-written ledger stopped after nine days, handed-over items went quiet, a merge of lane stocktakes produced about 940 rows mostly duplicating tracked work, and a deleted lane lost what only its conversation held. This task ships the shared contracts first (actors, references, transitions, transactions), then the store and the `follow` command on them, with its own docs, help and tests.

Outcome: **the coordination ledger lives in the clone's common git directory (`.git/codeflow/coord/`) as one append-only JSON Lines event log with one sequence, liveness in overwritten status files, and `codeflow follow` keeps follow-ups `FU-NNN` as full records with typed links, derived due times, closure only on target-aware proof by an allowed actor, exact-duplicate refusal, bounded and scanned text, and a read-only status that never writes; and `codeflow work status` lists per task the worktrees with uncommitted changes, unpushed commits and commits on no branch.**
The contracts, decided by ADR-0086 and applied here:

items.text: **Store** (location A): `events.jsonl` (the one coordination log: stream, follow-up, lane and coordinator events, one sequence), `status/` (overwritten liveness files, one per holder, never a log), `counters.json` (reserved FU and LN numbers, reserved before use, gaps allowed, never lowered), `coord.lock` (a stable sidecar lock, never removed or replaced) and `instance.json` (this ledger's UUID; FU and LN numbers are local display ids within it). Paths come from Git's own common-dir discovery (`hooks/repo.rs` `RepoInfo::discover`, `ids/state.rs`), never a literal `.git/`. The supported live scope is one clone on one machine; an exported reference is qualified by the instance UUID; import is recovery into an empty instance or an explicit reconciliation, never a live lease. No compaction in the first cut; the 10,000-event read path is measured.

**Transactions.** One append is one commit, under the lock, with `sequence` assigned there; sync before success is reported; a retriable operation carries an idempotency key; a torn tail is repaired or quarantined under the lock before the next append; interior damage, a duplicate or decreasing sequence, a broken transition or an unknown state-changing schema version makes the ledger read-only with a diagnostic; events are validated on replay as on input; hooks wait a bounded time for the lock and report busy as distinct from empty; readers use the committed prefix; network and model work run outside the lock and revalidate the expected revision on commit. Tested on macOS, Linux and native Windows with `fs2` advisory locking; shared network filesystems are not supported.

**Envelope**, field names in full: `schema_version`, `event`, `subject_id`, `sequence`, `recorded_at` (UTC, for people, never for order), `recorded_by` (role `coordinator`, a lane id or `operator`; an actor instance id always; harness, model and session id when known, unknowns explicit), optional `comment`; a mutation that depends on ownership carries the expected generation and entity revision and is refused when stale.

**A follow-up is a full record** for a cold reader. Required: `title`, `description`, `done_when`, `source` (operator, coordinator, a lane id, a review, an issue, outside), `source_reference` where one exists, `stream` (the `WS-NNN` it belongs to, or the project intake list until a coordinator takes it), `holder` (`coordinator` or a lane id), `links` typed `context`, `prerequisite` or `fulfils` (each with repository identity and the record UID where one exists) or a `no_link_reason`, and an effective schedule (`next_check` supplied or filled by the documented default). Optional: `waits_on`, `awaiting_operator` (a condition, never a holder). Dropped from the first cut: `priority`.

**Events**: `item_added`, `item_updated` (never `source`), `item_checked` (what was observed and the next check), `item_handed_over`, `item_closed` (evidence marked `asserted` or `machine_verified`, a reference a fresh session can open, the applicable revision and target), `item_dropped` (reason; the disposition of what it leaves), `item_reopened` (a reverted or invalidated proof keeps the old proof in history).

**Links and due times.** A `prerequisite` changing state (claimed, complete, blocked, cancelled; a pull request merged, closed or its checks finished; a lane reporting, idle or stale; another follow-up closed; a time passed) makes the follow-up due, never closed. Only a declared `fulfils` condition whose evidence satisfies `done_when` on the target, judged through the existing target-aware readiness and acceptance machinery (`workgraph/readiness.rs`), closes it automatically, naming the observation source, repository, target, revision and time; completion on a feature branch never counts. A cancelled task makes its follow-ups due for relinking or an explicit drop. A dependency wait has a maximum recheck time and records the observed dependency version. Cycles and reference integrity are checked on every dependency change, under the lock.
**A lane is optional.** A follow-up held by the stream's coordinator itself, with no lane, is tracked, checked and closed on the same proof as a lane-held one; direct work by the coordinator is work.

**Permission matrix**, one for every action: any bound actor adds; the holder updates, checks and hands over; the holder closes and drops, and the stream's coordinator may drop with a reason; a cross-stream wait names another stream's item or lane by id and is read-only; the operator's answer is recorded with its source, never as the operator; the operator may run the commands by hand, recorded as the operator. Every actor is bound to its instance and generation.

**Dedupe.** Only an exact duplicate (same source identity or idempotency key) is refused, atomically; similar follow-ups and matching open tasks, epic criteria and feedback items are suggested with a link or reject reason, never blocked.

**Privacy.** Every free-text field is scanned after decoding and size-bounded without echoing a rejected secret; files and directories are private with symlink and path checks; rendering to terminal and Markdown is safe; an explicit purge and repair path exists; the opt-in snapshot is never committed automatically and is exported redacted; a reader never assumes a line was validated on write.

**Read-only status.** `follow list` (table or `--md`, bounded: counts, the urgent subset and a pointer to the full list) never writes, claims a role, refreshes a heartbeat or creates a lock; a denied read is `unavailable`, no ledger is `empty`, a denied write is `unwritten`. Heartbeats are refreshed only by bound mutating operations (TSK-439 names them); an unbound observer reads and gets no heartbeat.

**Role binding.** This task ships the actor and binding contracts and binds actors in tests through a fixture; the commands that claim, release and adopt roles are TSK-439's, and the stream and status surfaces are TSK-439's and TSK-440's.

**An aid, not a control.** Nothing here blocks git, records, CI or landing; a missing or damaged ledger only warns; the ledger reads task, epic and ADR state and never writes a record; records, pull request bodies and `codeflow ci` never cite FU, LN or WS ids and never read the ledger.

context: Non-goals: lanes, attempts, streams and the coordinator lease, with their commands (TSK-439); the hook surfaces and `coord status` (TSK-440); the rules and the fresh-context test (TSK-423); compaction; cross-machine coordination; semantic duplicate refusal.

TSK-423.title: The rules and skills adopt the coordination ledger, proven fresh-context

next.reason: task TSK-423 depends on TSK-387, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: Issue #272, item 1 and its acceptance, under ADR-0086. Each of TSK-422, TSK-439 and TSK-440 ships the docs, CLI help and tests its own behaviour needs; this task is the integrated adoption: the managed rule and map row, the skill sections, the concepts, the per-harness notes, the architecture section and the fresh-context qualification from #272, with every requirement of the issue and its comment mapped to a task or an explicit deferral.

Outcome: **every guidance home says how the coordination ledger and lanes are used, in one vocabulary (session, stream, coordinator, lane, seat, attempt, follow-up), with the ledger named as an aid and never a control; and a fresh-context qualification shows a coordinator reporting three handed-over items, one stalled, with holder, task and next check, without being asked, beside the lone session, the lost transcript with in-flight workers, the stale-but-live holder and the delegated Stop lifecycle.**
Rules the guidance states:

items.text: The coordinator logs every operator-handed and every unsettled or untasked item at once as a full follow-up, follows it up, closes it only on proof of a listed kind, never on "handed to a lane", reads the ledger at session start (the digest), after compaction and before every status reply, and builds status from `follow list` with items awaiting the operator under "needs you".

One canonical role name, `coordinator`; the skills' existing `host` wording maps to it. Several coordinators can run at once, one per stream, within one harness and across harnesses; a session names its stream when it claims; a lane belongs to one stream and moves only by a two-sided handover; a task active in another stream's lane is a warning to heed; the coordinator's digest shows its own stream and a line per other stream, and `codeflow coord status` the whole project. A holder is the coordinator or a lane id; the operator is a condition, never a holder an agent impersonates.

The coordinator claims the lease explicitly, sweeps all items, opens and closes lanes (only the coordinator opens lanes), runs the inventory before adopting, and keeps the peer and worker prohibition on nested duos; a lane sees and closes its own items and adds items for what it hands back or finds; a lone session is its own coordinator and needs no lane, and a follow-up the coordinator holds itself is tracked and closed like a lane-held one; a coordinator in a new harness continues lanes it cannot reach by their own heartbeat and reports (fresh: leave running, read reports, start no duplicate writer; silent past the timeout: investigate with the inventory, replace on the same branch and worktree only with stopped-work evidence or a resolved overlap, else keep it as unresolved and possibly live and say so; a returning old seat stops), stated in `cf-model-orchestrator`, `cf-herdr` and `cf-delegate`; a seat attaches with `--lane` or a recorded `--no-lane` reason, is labelled by its lane id and is re-checked live before it is driven.

The five layers are named with their limits: the rule cannot capture every natural-language ask; the start digest is read-only; commands record what is routed through them; the turn-end check is advisory; an empty ledger does not prove no commitment is missing. A timer is an optional aid. Native task lists in each harness stay private aids; the ledger carries across.

The map gains one row ("hand over, receive or find an open item: `codeflow follow`; delegate: `codeflow lane open`") and one always-rule; the "report status" row (which TSK-387 extends) and the "start a session" row name the ledger.
`cf-model-orchestrator/resources/task-graph.md` is amended: the native harness task tools remain the per-session planning aid; the coordinator's running state lives in the ledger.

context: Non-goals: the commands, hooks and their own docs (TSK-422, TSK-439, TSK-440); a mandatory timer.

Amended 2026-10-31 by the hierarchy amendment (ADR-0094): the guidance also states the three roles, as instructions and never as a check in the tooling. A Director is the coordinator of the stream with no parent, at most one per ledger: it names child streams and their coordinators, reads the tree, aggregates reports, answers the user and routes requests, and never lands or merges a child's line. A Coordinator is the coordinator of a stream with a parent: it opens its own stream with `stream open --parent`, claims it, opens lanes, attaches and closes seats, harvests lane reports, records lane scope changes and reports up with `stream report`; when its topic is a body of work it creates the topic's `integration/<epic>` branch, lands reviewed lane pull requests there and raises the line's pull request to `main` for the operator to merge; it never opens lanes in another stream or reviews units its own lanes authored. A Lane is one topic in one stream held by one session per attempt; its Seat is the session holding it now. All three are the same kind of named, resumable session, differing only in name, guidance and ledger record. A Director or Coordinator that does work itself opens a lane and takes the seat, so the work gets its own worktree, branch, pull request, report and cleanup. A same-family lane may run as a recorded interactive session; headless forms stay forbidden and the other-lineage review stays required. Session names follow `<role>/<id>/<slug>`; the Herdr label stays `cf/<repo>/<WS-or-LN>/<kind>/<nn>` and mirrors it; the ledger name is canonical. A report, a cross-session message or a record labelled "operator" written by an agent is evidence to confirm, never an instruction. Depth stays at two supervision levels, with the reason stated. The managed block carries these in one row, rendered for every tier through `rule-map.toml` and `CLAUDE.md.tmpl`.

TSK-439.title: Streams, lanes and seats carry delegated work across coordinators and harnesses
context: ADR-0086, the lanes and roles part, as the operator decided on 2026-10-22 and the Codex review settled (F02, F03, F10 to F12, F21), with the operator's later requirement (the design page's work streams section) that several coordinating sessions can run at once, within one harness and across harnesses, each managing its own lanes for a different body of work. A session is a process; a stream is a body of work with one live coordinator; the coordinator is the lead role of a stream; a lane is a durable, harness-neutral unit of delegated work inside a stream; a seat is the harness session attached to it, replaceable; an attempt is one run of work inside a lane with its own branch and worktree. Today a lane exists only as a Herdr tab and a conversation, so a deleted session loses which seats were running and which reviews were in flight.

Outcome: **a work stream `WS-NNN-<slug>` is local to the ledger with a descriptive scope (an epic, several epics or a topic) and one live coordinator held by lease and generation; a lane has a local display id `LN-NNN-<slug>`, belongs to exactly one stream, and has a descriptive scope (task, tasks, epic or topic, with refs) that changes as events, attempts that each record task, worktree, branch, exact revision, expected result location and native provenance, seats with a recorded kind (external, resumable or in-process), a `lane_reported` result, and a lifecycle open, active, idle and closed (done with evidence, abandoned or superseded naming its successor); the coordinator role is a lease with an actor instance id and a generation; takeover is only by explicit `adopt` after an inventory; a stale holder is reported, never taken; and a new coordinator on any harness keeps the same lane numbers for the same work and continues from disk.**
Rules:

items.text: **Streams.** `WS-NNN-<slug>` is reserved ahead of use like FU and LN and local to the ledger; `stream_opened` records a descriptive scope (links to an epic, several epics or a topic phrase; never an amendment of any record), `stream_scope_changed` a change with its reason, `stream_closed` a reason and a disposition for its open lanes and follow-ups. One live coordinator per stream, held by lease and generation; a session names the stream it coordinates when it claims, and the start digest never guesses one. Every lane belongs to exactly one stream and only that stream's coordinator opens or closes it; a lane moves between streams only by a recorded handover both coordinators make (`lane_handed_over`, two events, one per coordinator). A task is active in one stream's lane at a time; a second stream starting it gets a warning naming the owner, and claims stay advisory. A lone session gets a default stream automatically. Adoption and harness switching are per stream. Every coordinator event carries its stream.

**Identity.** `LN-NNN` is reserved ahead of use in `counters.json`, rising, never reused, local to the ledger instance; the slug is presentation, derived from the scope, lowercase and short, unique among open lanes, renamable; labels and seat names carry a bounded stable `LN-NNN` (within Herdr's 32-character name limit), never the scope prose.

**Scope is descriptive only.** `lane_opened` records kind (build, review, research, consult), scope (kind `task`, `tasks`, `epic` or `topic` with refs) and purpose; `lane_scope_changed` records a new scope and reason as an event, so the history shows which work the lane carried. A scope change never amends criteria, dependencies or approved assignments, which keep their tracked process. Only the coordinator opens lanes (decided). Readiness applies to starting implementation, through the same core as `work start`, including reviewed stacks and standalone tasks: a `task` or `tasks` lane starts a task when `work next` reports it ready, an `epic` lane takes the epic's tasks in order as each becomes ready, a `topic` lane builds nothing until it creates or links tasks. Review and consult lanes bind an exact revision and never re-claim the task.

**Attempts.** `seat_attached` records an attempt: task, worktree, branch, exact revision, expected result location, requested and observed model and effort, and native provenance where the transport offers it (`codeflow delegate` run and turn records, native thread or resume ids; unknowns explicit). Every implementation attempt keeps its own task branch and worktree; a lane may hold several attempts. `lane_reported` records a result as reported, harvested or accepted, with its reference. In-session workers are recorded under their parent attempt, not as lanes; a crashed parent cannot resume them by replaying ids.

**Seat kinds.** `external` (a CLI in a Herdr pane) survives its coordinator and is re-checked live (pane, cwd, native session, ownership) before anything is sent or closed; `resumable` (a native resume id) is resumed in its own harness when available; `in-process` (an Agent-tool subagent, an in-app worker) dies with its parent, so the attempt is marked lost and the recovery inventory runs.

**Seats the new coordinator cannot reach** (the operator's case: lanes ran as Claude desktop sessions and the coordinator restarts in Codex, which can neither resume nor drive them). Such a seat is never assumed dead: it is judged by its own recorded heartbeat and reports, because the shared file is the channel and a live seat keeps writing `lane_reported` and refreshing its status through `codeflow` commands. Fresh: leave it running, keep reading its reports, start no duplicate writer on its worktree. Silent past the heartbeat timeout: the timeout triggers investigation, never replacement by itself, because a silent seat is not proof its work stopped (a long command outlives the timeout and may still write its worktree). The recovery inventory runs (branch, worktree, revision, expected result, dirty state, in-flight operations). Replacement on the same branch and worktree needs stopped-work evidence (the seat's harness session ended, its process gone, its worktree removed, or its last report says it finished) or an explicit resolution of the overlap under AC-5 (a new branch and worktree for the new attempt, or the operator stopping the old seat); only then is `seat_detached` recorded with reason `lost` and a new seat attached in the current harness that continues from the task record, the branch and the worktree, in its own attempt. With neither, the seat is kept as unresolved and possibly live, no duplicate writer starts on its resources, and the coordinator says so in its status. An old seat that comes back finds the lane adopted and stops. A resume id is a recovery lead, never permission to drive a matching pane.

**Coordinator lease.** `coordinator_claimed` binds an actor instance id and a generation; `coordinator_released` records a hand-over; `coordinator_adopted` and `lane_adopted` compare the expected holder, generation and the observed last heartbeat under the lock, then increment the generation; a stale writer is refused at the operation that can check it. A lease is coordination ownership, not an execution lock: before replacement work starts, the old seat's live panes, in-flight operations, branches and dirty worktrees are inventoried, anything not shown stopped is kept and overlapping work needs explicit resolution; nothing is cleaned up from a timeout. A returning session that finds its role or lane adopted stops and says so. Two coordinators by accident: the first claim wins; the second is told who leads and works as a lane or observer.

**Timing.** `check interval` (default 10 minutes) and `heartbeat timeout` (default 30 minutes) are advisory project settings placed by TSK-280's rule, the timeout longer than the interval, per stream for the coordinator lease; the caller's status file is refreshed by every bound mutating operation (`follow add|update|check|hand-over| close|drop|reopen`, `lane open|attach|scope|report|adopt|close`, `coordinator claim|release|adopt`, `work claim`, `work start`, and the turn-end check of a bound session), never by a read-only surface (`follow list`, `coord status`, `lane list`, `lane inventory`, `session-orient`, any status read, which write nothing); an unbound observer (a session that has claimed no role) reads only and gets no heartbeat; liveness uses monotonic elapsed time within a valid clock context and treats a clock discontinuity as uncertain; expiry proves contact overdue ("operation may still be running"), never death.

**Switching.** A new coordinator on any harness or model keeps the same lane for the same work and attaches a new seat that continues from the attempt's branch and worktree, never from the old conversation; a lane closes as superseded, naming its successor and handing over its open follow-ups, only when the scope changes, the state cannot be recovered or the operator restarts it. Review independence is judged against the work's author, not the coordinator; a changed model on an attempt rechecks the lineage rule. Lane `done` needs result evidence and a disposition for each open follow-up; abandonment hands them over, never completes them.

**Hooks into existing commands.** `work claim` keeps its verdicts, prints a hint when no lane holds the task and links a lane given with `--lane`; `cf-herdr` seat open takes `--lane LN-NNN` or a recorded `--no-lane "<reason>"` (consults, canaries, evaluations and the operator's own seats), and its live identity checks still decide.

**Recovery inventory** (the issue comment's third point): a read-only `codeflow lane inventory` (provisional) lists, per lane and attempt, the worktree state, unpushed and unreferenced commits, the last seat and its kind, and what is not recoverable.

context: Non-goals: the hooks (TSK-440); the rules (TSK-423); nested duos (the peer and worker prohibition stays); cross-machine lanes (an external reference only).

Amended 2026-10-31 by the hierarchy amendment (ADR-0094, accepted by the operator that day): this task also carries the ledger side of the Director, Coordinator and Lane hierarchy, with no role check in the tooling. A stream gains an optional `parent`, so a Director's stream has Coordinator streams under it, and `stream open --parent WS-NNN` reserves the id through the store. A coordinator claim and adoption carry the holder's `harness`, `session_name` and `resume_id`, and a seat carries `session_name` and `resume_id`, so every level is a named, resumable session: `coord rename|resume` and `lane rename|resume` record and look them up, and `resume` never launches. The schema moves to version 2 in one cutover with the report task (TSK-1126), which extends the same files after this task lands; binaries built between the two, the hook binary on `PATH` included, stay off the shared live ledger. The `stream_reported` event, the report body and the report identity rule are TSK-1126's; `lane report` with `summary` stays here. Depth stays at two supervision levels as guidance: a stream with a parent takes no children, and the tree view (TSK-440) shows depth rather than refusing.

TSK-440.title: The ledger surfaces run on every harness through one implementation

next.reason: task TSK-440 depends on TSK-439, whose anchored status is 'todo', not complete

context: ADR-0086, the enforcement part, as the Codex review corrected it (F13, F14, F20). Surfacing the ledger never depends on a session timer, which is session-scoped and vendor-specific: one implementation in the binary serves every harness through adapters. Today Claude wires SessionStart, Stop and UserPromptSubmit in `.claude/settings.json`, Codex wires SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit in `.codex/hooks.json`, and Grok has PreToolUse only in `.grok/hooks/codeflow.json`; wiring is not runtime evidence, so each route is proven by a native canary.

Outcome: **at every session start, `codeflow hook session-orient` reports, read-only, the session's own stream in detail (who leads and whether it is stale, the follow-ups owed, overdue or awaiting the operator, the lanes with stale seats) plus one summary line per other stream and the intake list, bounded to counts, the urgent subset and a pointer, never guessing a stream; `codeflow coord status` shows every stream, its coordinator's liveness, lanes, owed follow-ups and operator items, and flags, as an advisory, more than one distinct epic with active build attempts in a stream unless the earlier epic records an outside wait (issue 280's rule with its allowance); at every turn end, a check reports follow-ups past their next check, follow-ups with no effective schedule and a turn that answered an operator ask without an item, advisory, never blocking inside a tracked delegate session, and blocking elsewhere only as a verified project opt-in; any `codeflow` command can print the overdue count; status and `orient` are built from `follow list`; and a truthful capability matrix says what each harness runs.**
Rules:

items.text: The surfaces are one module the hooks and the CLI's shared output call; a harness adapter only wires an event. Claiming a role is a separate explicit step (TSK-439); the start digest never writes.

Capability matrix, published in the docs and checked by a scaffold test: Claude (start, stop, prompt), Codex (start, prompt; the turn-end check runs at the next prompt or an explicit command until a stop route exists), Grok (PreToolUse only: a session hook is added where Grok supports one, else the orchestrator's launch prompt runs `codeflow orient` explicitly and the matrix says so). A no-hook harness uses explicit orientation with reduced coverage.

Observations of pull requests and tasks (for due derivation and fulfilment) run with a bounded network budget and cached freshness, report offline as unknown, and promise discovery at the next check, never unattended execution (no daemon scheduling, `docs/product.md`).

The turn-end check never blocks inside a tracked delegate session; a blocking mode elsewhere validates its effective policy and compatibility at launch, avoids recursive Stop loops, never reads "still waiting" as a demand for another answer, and ships its own targeted tests against the delegate Stop lifecycle. Semantic "ask without item" detection stays advisory.

Orient stays within its line budget: counts, the urgent subset and a pointer to `follow list`; each stream folds once per invocation; backlog checking is resumable without marking unchecked items fresh. Whether coordination events enter `recall` is decided explicitly, with the privacy exclusions named.

context: Non-goals: the store (TSK-422), lanes (TSK-439), the rules (TSK-423).

Amended 2026-10-31 by the hierarchy amendment (ADR-0094): the surfaces show the Director, Coordinator and Lane tree that TSK-439 and TSK-1126 record. `codeflow coord status --tree` groups child streams under their parent, lists unharvested reports with their age, labels the role that recorded each line and marks a lane whose recorded worktree or branch is gone while its record is open as "worktree missing", from the inventory, never removing anything. The start digest shows the session's own stream, its children one line each and one line per other stream, and stays read-only. The traversal is bounded: a cyclic, missing-parent, closed-parent or deeper-than-two shape terminates and is shown as marked rows, never refused, because depth is guidance (ADR-0094). A Claude hook that appends a lane report at Stop or Notification is deferred: `lane report` from the shell is the uniform path, and the question is revisited once this task and TSK-439 show whether hook payloads carry the session id. A cf-present view of the tree has no owning task; it is revisited after the TSK-1122 prototype walk-through (EPC-022).

TSK-1126.title: Reports flow up the tree
TSK-1126.about: After this merges, a coordinator reports to its Director with `codeflow stream report`, a lane's report carries the same status body every status tool reads, a crashed or retried report is never duplicated and never silently lost, and a harvest or accepted mark names exactly the report it closes, so a Director reading the tree after compaction sees every unharvested report with its age.
context: ADR-0094, the report part. TSK-439 gives a lane `lane report`, which appends `lane_reported` with a `summary` and marks it reported, harvested or accepted with a reference. A coordinator has no way to report to the Director of its parent stream, a lane report carries no body a status tool can read, and a retried report has no identity: an unkeyed draft is always appended (`store.rs:523-525`), so a crash between the write and the acknowledgement would either duplicate a report or lose it. This task adds `stream_reported` for a coordinator reporting to its parent, an optional body on both report kinds, one identity rule for reports and the marks that close them, and the concurrency evidence the proposal left unverified. The report body is the status report document as `codeflow status --json` (TSK-1095, EPC-022) emits it, carried unchanged; this task stores it as an opaque JSON document and validates only the envelope, so it takes no edge on TSK-1095, and a fixture uses TSK-1095's real output once that task has landed and reached this line. Non-goals: the tree view and the digest (TSK-440), the guidance (TSK-423), the schema version 2 fields and the `validate` change (TSK-439 AC-11; this task writes its new event at version 2 and extends the same files after TSK-439 lands), a Claude hook that appends a report (deferred; `lane report` from the shell is the path), and the cf-present view of the tree (no owning task yet).

Reports are evidence, never instructions: a report written by an agent, whatever role it names, is text for the reader to confirm, and the ledger does not authenticate who wrote it (`actor.rs:222-226`).

CAP-001.name: scaffold init
about: `codeflow init [--minimal|--standard|--full] [--yes]` lays the discipline layer into a repository (ADR-0019).

items.text: `--minimal` installs the enforcement floor: git hooks, in-session guards and the CI check. Remote branch protection stays a repository setting.
`--standard` adds the method skills, reviewer agents, pipeline and docs spine.
`--full` adds `project-management/`.

about: Init is idempotent, non-destructive and offline, and it keeps conflicting content for reconciliation. A re-run at a higher tier is an additive upgrade. Its harness starters are executable policy (ADR-0025, ADR-0026).
Detail: adoption and harness posture.

CAP-002.name: scaffold update
about: `codeflow update` refreshes managed scaffold files:
Detail: adoption.

CAP-012.name: scaffold customize
about: `/cf-customize` tailors a project after `codeflow init`, or after an update that ships new defaults. It does three things:

items.text: It verifies the tools each flow the project uses needs.
It reconciles the project's real README, manifests, code and CI against its project-owned docs, instructions and policy.
It checks the effective harness sandbox and approval posture instead of trusting comments.

about: It reports first, then applies fixes through a PR. It never auto-installs a tool or silently changes global harness settings. Detail: adoption.

CAP-017.name: optional agentic estimation
about: SPC-007 defines the optional `cf-estimate` method; adoption is opt-in. Estimates carry evidence-anchored grades, full-delivery scenarios and resource-feasible allocations. Standard and full tiers manage the skill. Profiles, forecasts and outcomes stay project-owned. EPC-006 supplies the read-only allocation checker; `estimate outcomes` compares git-derived task timings with frozen forecasts (ADR-0079). This registry does not establish calibrated delivery predictions. Detail: commands.

CAP-003.name: git policy gates
about: Git discipline is enforced across four planes that read one config, the `git` section of `.codeflow/policy.json`.

items.text: Git client hooks and the in-session `git-guard` give fast local feedback.
CI re-runs the same checks through `codeflow ci`. Together with remote branch protection, it forms the authoritative perimeter (ADR-0017).
The anti-bypass layer has no off switch. It is the strict policy validator, the gate-context token for protected-branch advances, and the guard's refusal of override variables set in-session.
Secret scanning fails closed.

Agent sessions are judged by the landed policy on the remote, so a local edit, commit or branch cannot relax the session checks. The authority is the default branch at one commit, never a line or a guess (ADR-0091).

about: Other checks on these planes:
Detail: enforcement planes and policy reference.

CAP-008.name: remote protect doctor

items.text: `codeflow remote protect` writes GitHub rulesets it owns: one role moves the default branch, and pull requests with strict, pinned checks guard it, the integration lines and each other protected branch. It never weakens a rule and reports what the plan cannot apply.
`codeflow doctor` runs twenty-six health checks on the repository and the tools around it, including the default branch's host rules.

about: Doctor leaves live interactive account and tool canaries to the harness (ADR-0023). Detail: troubleshooting and commands.

CAP-011.name: security redteam review
about: The duo develop flow includes a mandatory security and red-team stage (ADR-0016).

items.text: The CI `security-review` job runs `osv-scanner` for software composition analysis (SCA) over every lockfile ecosystem. It blocks only when `security_review` or `dep_audit` is `block`; the shipped default is warn.
Secrets found by gitleaks always block, with exemptions read from the trusted commit.
The `cf-security-reviewer` agent runs a two-vendor adversarial review. Its findings warn locally and force bounded rework, with the human merger as the backstop (ADR-0007).

about: Detail: enforcement planes.

CAP-004.name: test gate
about: `codeflow test [--mode full|quick|essential] [--strict] [--since <rev>] [--all] [--only <targets>]` runs the generic test engine against the targets in `.codeflow/test-config.json` or a detected stack.

items.text: With no stack detected it is a loud no-op that exits 0. `--strict` turns that into a non-zero exit for unattended callers.
With a stack it is a real gate, re-run in CI. Coverage thresholds count toward the verdict (ADR-0021).
Every run executes every eligible target: no local run record earns selection credit (ADR-0089). The test-gate reference defines the fields a record holds.
`codeflow test setup` fills absent configs and never auto-replaces populated ones.

about: Detail: commands.

CAP-005.name: integrate
about: `codeflow integrate <branch> [--into <target>]` is the sanctioned local landing path for protected branches. Under a file lock it rebases and fast-forwards by default. With `--merge`, it gates a no-fast-forward merge commit that preserves the reviewed source head and its acceptance binding. Both modes advance only the local target ref after every stage succeeds; neither pushes. Merge mode runs from a linked worktree. A gate-context token lets the protected ref advance only through integrate or a human-merged PR. Detail: commands and enforcement planes.

CAP-007.name: orient session summary
about: `codeflow orient` builds the session-start digest live: product, branch, worktree, work counts, ADRs and gates. Its 30-line base guideline excludes the complete integration-line and open-epic inventories. `git.line_sync_interval` optionally enables overdue reminders. The `session-summary` SessionEnd hook records sessions for recall. Claude wires both through `.claude/settings.json`; interactive Codex gets the digest through `.codex/hooks.json` (ADR-0013).

Rules return after context loss and where a prompt needs them (TSK-128). One advisory command, `session-orient`, is wired on `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` and reads the event from the payload. Sizes are guidelines.
`codeflow status` also prints a read-only cleanup inventory of linked worktrees and unattached local branches (ADR-0044). Detail: commands.

CAP-006.name: recall registry
about: `codeflow recall [--all] "<query>"` searches project memory: ledger events, session summaries, ADRs, epics, tasks, frozen specs and capabilities. It uses bundled SQLite full-text search (FTS5) and discloses coverage gaps. The cross-repository view comes from `~/.codeflow/registry.json`, a locked registry updated on every command run and read lazily at query time, with no daemon. Detail: commands.

CAP-009.name: cross vendor delegation
about: Consult or delegate a unit of work to another vendor's coding CLI at the process boundary, each under its own subscription auth. CodeFlow's gates judge the output whoever wrote it (ADR-0005). Transport is interactive only and stated once, in `cf-model-orchestrator/resources/routing/transport.md` (ADR-0077): another family runs its own interactive CLI in a Herdr tab that `cf-herdr` hosts, Codex on its app-server; the Codex plugin is an optional fallback and tmux the last. Headless task execution is prohibited. Delegates edit only inside a worktree on a feature branch, under the same gates. Detail: delegation.

CAP-010.name: duo model orchestration
about: `/cf-model-orchestrator` is the host-neutral entry for routed repository work. Touched paths decide what is routed:

items.text: adopter-facing paths
research that will drive such a change
plan, design, security or irreversible work

about: It selects the smallest complete outcome mode, so research or planning work stops before implementation. Planning, review and batch landing follow how work moves to main (ADR-0076).

Both seats independently discover from the same immutable brief before either sees the other's findings. Claude then drafts the one plan, Codex challenges it, and both approve one version before implementation.
Material product or visual work also records a `DESIGN_INTENT` in that plan (ADR-0043, ADR-0051).
The work records a plan produces are judged by one core (SPC-013):
Detail: duo model orchestration.

CAP-013.name: model binding evaluation
about: `/cf-evaluate-model` qualifies a new model or version, native harness release, permission profile, or material CodeFlow instruction change as the complete system users will run. The standard and full skill carries:

items.text: stable requirement IDs
balanced regression and capability cases
a native-interactive run protocol
a standard-library tool for validation, scoring, baseline comparison and fail-closed cleanup

about: Focused diagnostic packs do not qualify a model binding.
Detail: model and harness upgrades.

CAP-014.name: transport neutral delegate lifecycle
about: `codeflow delegate init|arm|wait` and the `hook delegate-turn --state-dir` mode drive a delegated harness turn through durable, owner-only protocol records instead of tmux signalling.

items.text: The binary never launches a harness or delivers a prompt. The host does both, and the current event adapter is Claude hooks.
`arm` records one turn as the SHA-256 of the exact prompt bytes. Acceptance requires a matching `UserPromptSubmit`.
`wait` has a stable exit contract.
Poison is durable. Recovery is a new run in a fresh directory.

about: The status stays building while broader native-platform and stress evidence is open. Detail: delegation.

CAP-015.name: opt in documentation portal

items.text: `codeflow portal setup --path <repository-relative-directory>` explicitly adopts the pinned Starlight and Pagefind repository guide. Ordinary initialization never installs it.
Setup preserves user-owned configuration. Runtime drift or a collision stops all portal writes.
`codeflow portal transfer --confirm` hands runtime maintenance to the project.
The adapter generates pages, Markdown twins, `llms.txt` and search output from one clean committed snapshot. It fails closed rather than publish mixed content.
`codeflow validate --portal` runs no project code, writes nothing and checks the generated evidence.

about: Detail: opt-in documentation portal.

CAP-016.name: interactive presentation review
about: `codeflow present` turns a closed, versioned JSON and Markdown document into one bounded local review surface with anchored feedback.

items.text: The standard and full tiers supply the `cf-present` authoring skill and its schemas.

The runtime serves an authenticated loopback-only page to an isolated browser profile. It keeps immutable revisions and append-only feedback in owner-private state, and it retains ambiguous state rather than deleting it.
The `diagram` block was removed with Mermaid. New input carrying one is refused with its conversion named. A revision stored with one loads read only, with a notice and its escaped source.

about: The status stays building until task TSK-007 records the full native platform and browser matrix. Detail: present architecture and present guide.
